The Macrons’ complaint additionally identifies public inauguration footage showing the two siblings together. [1][2]The separate French libel convictions of two other women were overturned in July 2025 on good-faith grounds, as Full Fact records. That was not a finding that Brigitte and Jean-Michel are the same person. Nor does the filing of the Macrons’ American lawsuit itself prove their case. The criticism rests on the underlying evidence, rather than the mere existence of litigation. [2]2  Accusing the Zelenskys of stealing to finance shoppingOn December 21, 2022, Owens told Volodymyr Zelensky to “Stop stealing from our people” while alleging that his wife was spending tens of thousands of dollars shopping in Paris. Mediaite reproduces the post and links to it. [3]The shopping allegation came from a poorly sourced viral story about an alleged €40,000 purchase. The reporting traced its circulation through NewsPunch and a social-media account rather than verified evidence of the transaction. Owens nevertheless converted it into a direct accusation that Zelensky was stealing from Americans while his wife spent the money. [3]The precise criticism here is an unsupported accusation presented as fact. An absence of evidence does not independently prove that no purchase of any kind occurred. It does mean that this story supplied no sound basis for her accusation of theft. Disagreeing with aid to Ukraine would not require making that accusation.3  Implicating Brian Harpole in a murder conspiracyOwens promoted Mitch Snow’s account placing Charlie Kirk’s security chief, Brian Harpole, at a purported military meeting at Fort Huachuca on September 9, 2025, the day before Kirk was killed. Her December broadcasts and posts connected the alleged meeting to government involvement in the assassination. Harpole’s federal complaint reproduces these statements and supplies links to the broadcasts. [4]Harpole says his travel records place him in Dallas and that Owens continued publishing the allegation after acknowledging she had reviewed those records. Those assertions are part of his lawsuit, and I am not presenting them as findings already made by a judge. [4]This is a documented, disputed accusation of involvement in a murder conspiracy, with an asserted documentary alibi that must be confronted. Establishing that Snow visited a military base would not establish that Harpole attended the alleged meeting, much less that anybody there planned a killing. The accusation requires evidence of those additional propositions.4  Lance Twiggs and the police investigationOn Shawn Ryan’s show, around 1:02:00, Owens suggested that Lance Twiggs was a federal asset and offered as a reason that police “didn’t even question him.” In a separate post reported on July 10, 2026, she claimed investigators had merely photographed his phone instead of collecting it. These are specific factual assertions about an alleged investigative failure. [5][6][7]The hearing record contradicts them. July 8 testimony states that Twiggs was interviewed in September 2025 and again in April 2026, that both interviews were recorded, and that he voluntarily provided his phone to FBI agents during the first interview. On July 9, Agent Davis confirmed that a Cellebrite forensic extraction had been performed and that he had reviewed it. [8][9]The claim that police did not question Twiggs is false according to that testimony. So is the description of an investigation limited to taking pictures of his phone. Questions about the authenticity or interpretation of particular messages remain legitimate, but they must address the evidence actually collected. The separate assertion that Twiggs was a federal asset was speculation, not something established by the supposed lack of questioning.5  Harvey Weinstein and accusations against his accusersMy reference to Weinstein is also easy to document. In an August 1, 2025 interview with Tucker Carlson, Owens portrayed his accusers as women who had consensual sex in anticipation of film roles and turned against him when the expected benefits failed to appear. She said: “They assumed he was going to give them these roles, and he didn’t.” TheWrap reports the comments and embeds the interview. [10][11]That is a substantive accusation about the women’s honesty and motives. The court record does not support dismissing the cases as a collective fabrication: a New York jury convicted Weinstein in June 2025 of sexually assaulting Miriam Haley, and he received a 15-year state-prison sentence on September 23, 2026. [12]The record must also be described fairly. That jury acquitted him on another sexual-assault count and did not reach a verdict on the rape count. One conviction does not establish every accusation ever made against him. Equally, an acquittal or an unresolved count does not establish that his accusers collectively invented assaults for money or because they regretted consensual sex. Owens’s sweeping explanation goes well beyond defending his right to a fair trial. [13]6  Her public defense of Andrew TateOwens published an episode titled Candace Investigates Andrew Tate’s “Victims” on August 5, 2023. In her March 2025 interview with Tate, she defended her assessment of the Romanian case and depicted the Florida investigation as a response to political opponents’ anger. The original episode listings, video and transcript document that advocacy. [14][15][16]Defending an accused person is legitimate. My criticism is the readiness to treat hostile motives as an explanation for investigations and accusations while presenting her own assessment with such confidence. Her programs support describing her as a public defender of Tate; they do not, by themselves, prove that every criticism she made of his accusers was false.Tate’s guilt must not be assumed. The Crown Prosecution Service announced additional charges in July 2026 and expressly stated that a charging decision is not a finding of guilt. I apply that distinction here. I also reject the opposite shortcut: a suspect’s denial, a procedural setback for prosecutors, or a sympathetic interview does not establish that his accusers are liars. [17]7  Trying to clear Tyler Robinson while implicating othersOwens’s Shawn Ryan interview makes the Robinson point explicit. Around 1:00:00–1:02:00, she says she does not think he was the person shown at the scene and confidently states that he did not kill Charlie Kirk, while allowing that he might have played an accessory role. That is an affirmative effort to clear him of the shooting. [5][6]Robinson has pleaded not guilty, and the decision to send him to trial was not a conviction. Nevertheless, the prosecution has presented surveillance, DNA evidence and alleged admissions. Those are matters to test against the defense’s challenges, not evidence that can be displaced by an unsupported alternative story. [18]I would not bolster the prosecution with a nonexistent fingerprint match. The July 9 stipulation says a Utah examiner excluded Robinson as the source of three window prints, while the FBI’s subsequent examination was inconclusive. That limitation deserves an accurate account, just as the phone evidence does. [9]The reasonable criticism of Owens is her unequal standard of proof: she is prepared to express confidence that Robinson did not shoot Kirk while casting suspicion on other people through claims that are unsupported or contradicted by the hearing record. Asking her to substantiate those claims is entirely appropriate.Lionel’s imagined critic cannot explain why he objects to Owens. I can: the claims above identify real people, and the sources make it possible to check what she said and what supports it. Calling the criticism “hate” does nothing to answer those examples. If she wants the benefit of skepticism for the people she defends, she should apply comparable care before accusing somebody else.

Sources and relevant passagesNumbered citations in the response and the source titles below are clickable. Sources checked October 1, 2026. Original interview. Relevant discussion is approximately 1:00:00–1:03:00: Robinson’s alleged role, the assertion that he did not shoot Kirk, and claims about Twiggs.[6] Clipto, transcript of Shawn Ryan Show episode 318. text:
Contribution to society by Palestinians?  Terror, murder, rape, mutilation, suicide bombing, babies in microwaves ,etc. 

Contribution to society by Israelis in less than 80 years?

Mathematics
Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma, a mathematical result concerning low-distortion embeddings of points from high-dimensional into low-dimensional Euclidean space contributed by Joram Lindenstrauss.
Development of the measurement of rigidity by Elon Lindenstrauss in ergodic theory, and their applications to number theory.[1]
A proof of Szemerédi's theorem using ergodic theory, by mathematician Hillel Furstenberg.
Expansion of axiomatic set theory and the ZF set theory by Abraham Fraenkel.
Development of the area of automorphic forms and L-functions by Ilya Piatetski-Shapiro.[2][3]
Development of Sauer–Shelah lemma and Shelah cardinal.
Development of the first proof of the alternating sign matrix conjecture.
Development of Zig-zag product of graphs, a method of combining smaller graphs to produce larger ones used in the construction of expander graphs by Avi Wigderson.
Development of Bernstein–Sato polynomial and proof of the Kazhdan–Lusztig conjectures by Joseph Bernstein
Generalization of the marriage theorem by obtaining the right transfinite conditions for infinite bipartite graphs. He subsequently proved the appropriate versions of the Kőnig theorem and the Menger theorem for infinite graphs by Ron Aharoni.
Development of the Amitsur–Levitzki theorem by Shimshon Amitsur.
The Benjamini-Hochberg procedure for controlling the False discovery rate, a statistical method for regulating Type I errors.[4]

Science

Chemistry
Discovery of quasicrystals by Dan Shechtman of the Technion.[5] The discovery led him to receive the 2011 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.[6]
Discovery of the role of protein Ubiquitin by Avram Hershko and Aaron Ciechanover of the Technion Institute (together with the American biologist Irwin Rose). The discovery led them to receive the 2004 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.[7][8]
Increased understanding of how proteins are made - Ada Yonath of Israel alongside Venkatraman Ramakrishnan of India and Thomas A. Steitz of the US shared the 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for increased understanding of the structure and function of ribosomes.[9]
Development of multiscale models for complex chemical systems by Arieh Warshel and Michael Levitt of the Weizmann Institute of Science (presently at University of Southern California and Stanford University, respectively), together with the Austrian-born American chemist Martin Karplus. The discovery led them to receive the 2013 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.[10]
Discovery and Isolation of the Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), a cannabinoid found in cannabis, by Raphael Mechoulam while working in the Weizmann Institute of Science, 1964.[11][12][13]

Physics
See also: Category:Israeli physicistsDiscovery of the Aharonov–Bohm effect by Yakir Aharonov and David Bohm.[14]
Jacob Bekenstein was the first to propose Black holes also have Entropy while working in the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.[15][16]
Discovery and classification of hadrons through the SU(3) flavour symmetry, led to the development of Eightfold way, by Yuval Ne'eman, 1961.[17][18]

Optics
📷Endoscopic capsule
Pillcam by Given Imaging, the first Capsule Endoscopy solution to record images of the digestive tract.[19][20] The capsule is the size and shape of a pill and contains a tiny camera.[21] Created by Israeli engineer Gavriel Iddan[22] who sold the company to Irish medical device maker Covidien for $860 million.[23][24][25] Iddan has expressed regret for the sale due to the companies fulfillment of an ancient Jewish prophecy “The Pillcam was based on military technology... It was a good example of how we shall beat our swords into plowshares", as the Hebrew prophets predicted.[26] Covidien was acquired by Medtronic in 2016, and is now the provider of Pillcam.[27]
Line free single power bicentric prismatic spectacle lens for correction of anisometropia. Sydney J. Bush UK patent no. 1539381.

Medicine
The flexible stent, also known as NIR Stent or EluNIR. Developed by Israeli company Medinol, which is headquartered in Tel Aviv.[28][29]

The pressure bandage - known widely as the Israeli Bandage is a specially designed, first-aid device that is used to stop bleeding from hemorrhagic wounds caused by traumatic injuries in pre-hospital emergency situations.[30] First used for saving lives during a NATO peacekeeping operation in Bosnia and Herzegovina,[31] by inventor, Israeli military medic, Bernard Bar-Natan.[32] The bandage was successfully used during operations Enduring Freedom and Iraqi Freedom and is widely used today, across the world.[33][34][35] The bandage was nicknamed "Israeli bandage" by American soldiers, and has been "the bandage of choice for the US Army and special forces". Before the Israeli emergency bandage was invented in 1998, wounded soldiers were told to find a rock and wrap it on top of hemorrhaging wounds in order to hold direct pressure.[36] Bar-Natan sold his company to PerSys Medical Inc in Houston, Texas, the company that first introduced the bandage to the US military.📷An Israeli Bandage being used by Sudanese and US Naval service members during a training exercise.
Eshkol-Wachman Movement Notation – a notation system for recording movement on paper that has been used in many fields, including dance, physical therapy, animal behavior and early diagnosis of autism.[37]
Development of the Copaxone immunomodulator drug for treating multiple sclerosis. It was developed in the Weizmann Institute of Science in Israel by Michael Sela, Ruth Arnon and Deborah Teitelbaum.[38][39]
Development of bioengineered recombinant interferon proteins by Michel Revel from the Weizmann Institute of Science in Israel.[40]
Development of taliglucerase alfa (Elelyso), a recombinant glucocerebrosidase enzyme produced from transgenic carrot cell cultures.[41] Taliglucerase alfa won approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in May 2012 as an orphan drug for the treatment of Type 1 Gaucher's disease.[42]
Development of ENvue, a feeding tube placement system with advanced methods of navigation, integrated sensors and body mapping, for accurate enteral tube placement, by the Israeli company ENvizion Medical, used in Hospitals and Medical centers in the US.[43]
Development of engineered recombinant Chimeric Antigen Receptors by Professor Zelig Eshhar of the Weizmann Institute of Science and his trainee Gideon Gross, today a component of novel cell-based immunotherapy for various cancers.[44][45]
Development of Azilect, a drug for Parkinson's disease, by Moussa Youdim and John Finberg from the Technion - Israel Institute of Technology, and commercialized by Teva Pharmaceutical Industries.

Economics
Work of Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky of the Hebrew University of Jerusalem explaining irrational human economic choices.[46] The work led Daniel to receive the 2002 Nobel Prize in Economics.[47]
Developments in Game theory. Israel Aumann of the Hebrew University of Jerusalem received the 2005 Nobel Prize in Economics for his work in this field.[48]
The Rubinstein bargaining model, one of the most influential findings in game theory, refers to a class of bargaining games that feature alternating offers through an infinite time horizon. The proof is from Ariel Rubinstein 1982.[49]

Biotechnology
See also: Category:Israeli biologists📷Eshkol-Wachman Movement Notation
Nanowire – a conductive wire made of a string of tiny particles of silver, a thousand times thinner than a human hair. Developed by Uri Sivan, Erez Braun and Yoav Eichen from Technion.[50]
World's smallest DNA computing machine system – "the smallest biological computing device" ever constructed, according to Guinness Book of Records, which is composed of enzymes and DNA molecules capable of performing simple mathematical calculations and which uses its input DNA molecule as its sole source of energy. Developed in 2003 in the Weizmann Institute of Science by professor Ehud Shapiro and his team.[51][52]
OrCam MyEye, is a portable, artificial vision device that allows the visually impaired to understand text and identify objects through audio feedback describing what such people are unable to see.[53]
TraitUP – a new technology that enables the introduction of genetic materials into seeds without modifying their DNA, immediately and efficiently improving plants before they're even sowed. It was developed by Hebrew University agricultural scientists Ilan Sela and Haim D. Rabinowitch.[54]

Theoretical computer science
RSA public key encryption, introduced by Adi Shamir with Ron Rivest, and Leonard Adleman[55]
The concept of nondeterministic finite automatons, introduced by Michael O. Rabin[56]
Amir Pnueli introduced temporal logic into computing science
Lempel–Ziv–Welch algorithm, a universal lossless data compression algorithm created by Abraham Lempel and Jacob Ziv of the Technion institute, together with the American Information theorist, Terry Welch.[57]
Feige–Fiat–Shamir identification scheme - a type of parallel zero-knowledge proof developed by Uriel Feige, Amos Fiat, and Adi Shamir in 1988.

Computing
The Intel 8088 – This microprocessor, designed at Intel's Haifa laboratory, powered the first PC that IBM built,[58] which is credited with kickstarting the PC revolution.[59][60][61][62][63] The 8088 was designed in Israel at Intel's Haifa laboratory. The widespread use of the IBM's PC,[64] using the 8088 processor, established the use of x86 architecture as a de facto standard for decades. The IEEE wrote that "almost all the world’s PCs are built around CPUs that can claim the 8088 as an ancestor."[65][66] Intel has credited the 8088 with launching the company into the Fortune 500.[65]
Quicktionary Electronic dictionary – a pen-sized scanner able to scan words or phrases and immediately translate them into other languages, or keep them in memory in order to transfer them to the PC. Developed by the company Wizcom Technologies Ltd.[67]
Kernel-based Virtual Machine, was developed by Avi Kivity at Qumranet in 2006.[68]
Laser Keyboard – a virtual keyboard is projected onto a wall or table top and allows to type handheld computers and cell phones. Developed simultaneously by the Israeli company Lumio and Silicon Valley startup company Canesta.[69][70][71][72] The company subsequently licensed the technology to Celluon of Korea.[73]
Stateful Inspection as part of firewalls - Although academic work on this had been performed by others, Gil Schwed and Nir Zuk, at Israeli company Checkpoint, released the first commercial, stateful firewall.[74][75][76]
TDMoIP (TDM over IP) − in telecommunications, the emulation of time-division multiplexing (TDM) over a packet-switched network (PSN), developed by engineers at RAD Data Communications[77]
Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) - technology for voice based communications using the internet instead of traditional telephone systems. VoIP was originally conceived by Danny Cohen, an Israeli-American scientist, but was first created, implemented, and commercialized by Netanya-based, Israeli company VocalTec and its founder Alon Cohen[78][79][80][81][82]
Thunderbolt, a widely used interface technology, was developed as a joint venture between Apple Inc and Intel, in Israel[83][84][85]
The first instant messaging (IM) service, ICQ. Originally developed by the Israeli company Mirabilis in 1996. Mirabilis invented a system for creating unique identifiers (UINs) that could be applied over IRC leading it to be the first widely adopted IM service.[86][87][88][89][90][91]
Umoove, a high-tech startup company that invented a software only solution for face and eye tracking is located in Israel.[92]
EPROM - a type of programmable read-only memory (PROM) chip that retains its data when its power supply is switched off. invented by Dov Frohman in 1971.[93] led to the development of Intel MCS-48 and other microcontrollers.
Network Vault - A system for secure data storage, exchange and/or sharing through a protected central storage facility, containing at least one "network vault" to which access is controlled through a single data access channel. developed by Alon Nisim Cohen and is used for Israeli software company CyberArk.[94][95]
FaceID, the Apple Inc facial recognition software used in iPhone devices.[96] FaceID is based on technology created by Israeli companies PrimeSense,[97][98][99] which was bought by Apple Inc. for $360 million on November 24, 2013,[100] and RealFace[101][102][103][104]
USB flash drive – a flash memory data storage device integrated with a USB interface. The Israeli company M-Systems (in partnership with IBM) claims to have developed and manufactured the first USB flash drives available in North America.[105] This claim is challenged by multiple companies in the following three countries which also independently developed USB technology: Singapore (Trek Technology), the People's Republic of China (PRC) (Netac Technology) and the Republic of China (Taiwan). See USB Flash drive § Patent controversy.
WAF - a specific form of application firewall that filters, monitors, and blocks HTTP traffic to and from a web service. Developed by Gili Raanan

Robotics
ReWalk a bionic walking assistance system that enables paraplegics to stand upright, walk and climb stairs.
Development of robotic guidance system for spine surgery by Mazor Robotics.

Defense, Aviation and Military
Iron Dome – a mobile air defense system in development by Rafael Advanced Defense Systems and Israel Aircraft Industries designed to intercept short-range rockets and artillery shells. On April 7, 2011, the system successfully intercepted a Grad rocket launched from Gaza, marking the first time in history a short-range rocket was ever intercepted.[106] The Iron Dome was later utilized more fully in the Israeli-Gaza conflict of 2012, where it displayed a very high rate of efficiency (95%–99%) in intercepting enemy projectiles. The United States had provided financial assistance in millions of dollars in developing the Iron Dome.[107]
The Uzi submachine gun was developed by Maj. Uziel Gal in the 1950s.
IMI Tavor TAR-21 is an Israeli bullpup assault rifle.
Desert Eagle a large-caliber pistol.
Barrel bomb - an improvised unguided bomb. first used by the Israeli Air Force during the 1948 Arab–Israeli War.
Sponge bomb - a specialized device designed to seal the end of a tunnel. Developed by the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) to address the use of tunnels by Hamas in Gaza.[108][109]
CornerShot - a weapon accessory created by Lt. Col. Amos Golan of the Israel Defense Forces in cooperation with American investors.
Ukraine Siren Alerts - a siren alert electronic system created by Israeli student Bernard 'Boaz' Moerdler in 2022.
Tactical Robotics Cormorant - a flying car unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) built by Tactical Robotics Ltd. Invented by Rafi Yoeli in Yavne, Israel.[110][111]
Wall radar – a unique radar utilizing Ultra Wide Band (UWB) to allow users to see through walls. Developed by the Israeli company Camro.[112]
Protector USV is an unmanned surface vehicle, developed by the Rafael Advanced Defense Systems. It is the first of its kind to be used in combat.[113]
Trophy APS - an Active Protection System designed to protect vehicles from incoming threats, such as Rocket-propelled grenade rounds and ATGMs by firing charges to intercept them after detecting and tracking them.[114][115]

Agriculture
Plastic emitter for practical surface drip irrigation - developed in Israel by Simcha Blass and his son Yeshayahu in 1959. Rather than allowing water to flow through small holes that could easily be clogged by fine particles, this method directed it through wider and longer channels, using friction within a plastic emitter to slow the flow. The technology is widely used in arid and semi-arid areas all over the world.[116][117][118][119]

text:
Warren.

"Bernie Sanders is correct."

Honestly, that was my first clue that you're an idiot. You didn't even make it to the second sentence before I had my red pen out. Some people are a few decimals short of a data set. You're missing the whole spreadsheet.

And then you kept going. "This community note is misleading." Warren, a community note only shows up when people who usually disagree with each other look at the same post and agree it needs a correction. That's not a conspiracy. That's the internet's version of a jury, and it came back against Bernie. You're Bernie's longtime staff director, paid by taxpayers, and your job today was to stand in front of that verdict and yell "objection!" after the gavel already came down. You're a sock puppet with a spreadsheet, Warren, and somebody's hand is very clearly up the back.

So let me do what I do every day with sixteen-year-olds who turn in a lab report with suspiciously perfect results. Let me check your data. Fair warning, this is going to go about as well as a mime explaining calculus.

Bernie posted that the "total wealth" of the bottom 50 percent of U.S. households was $317.8 billion in 1989 and $313 billion in 2026. Then a community note pointed out that the Federal Reserve's numbers don't say that. And your defense is, and I'm quoting you, that the figures come "from the Fed data minus durable goods & promises of future Social Security benefits."

Minus.

MINUS, Warren.

You know what we call that in a science classroom? We call it throwing out the data points you don't like until the graph says what you wanted it to say. I had a student try that once. He got a zero and a long talk after class. You got a blue checkmark and a repost from Ro Khanna. That's like getting a gold star from the kid who copied off you.

Let's start with where the numbers actually come from. https://t.co/5tUfkVY18K is not the Federal Reserve. It's an academic project run by economists Emmanuel Saez, Gabriel Zucman, and Thomas Blanchet. Fine people, I'm sure. But when Bernie's followers see "Fed data," they think the government's official numbers. They're not. That's a little like telling your mom you got the recipe "straight from Grandma," when really you found it on a blog and swapped out half the ingredients.

So what does the Fed's own Distributional Financial Accounts say? Roughly $700 billion for the bottom half in 1989, and more than $4 trillion in 2026. That's about six times higher in plain dollars, and still more than double after you account for inflation. Bernie's 2026 number is somewhere around one-thirteenth of the official one.

One-thirteenth, Warren. If my students were off by a factor of thirteen, I'd ask if they were measuring in the right units. You weren't off by accident. You cut out the parts on purpose. That's a ruler with the first six inches sawed off, Warren. Of course everything comes up short.

Now let's talk about what got cut.

First, "durable goods." That's cars. Refrigerators. Washers and dryers. Furniture. The pickup truck a guy uses to get to work. Those are real things people own. They can sell them. The Fed counts them because they EXIST. And here's the part you didn't mention: for a working family in the bottom half, the truck and the appliances are a much bigger share of everything they own than they are for a billionaire. Cut those out, and you're not measuring the bottom 50 percent more "accurately." You're measuring them with their own stuff hidden behind the couch. It's like a guy setting the bathroom scale back twenty pounds and then bragging to the whole gym about his diet.

Second, Social Security. And Warren, this one is my favorite, because it's so perfectly backwards.

Bernie Sanders has spent his whole career telling America that Social Security is the backbone of working families' retirement. He's right about that much. Research by economists Sylvain Catherine, Max Miller, and Natasha Sarin found that Social Security is roughly HALF of the wealth of the bottom 90 percent of Americans. When you count it, a big chunk of the supposed explosion in inequality since 1989 flattens out.

So the man who calls Social Security sacred, who says it's the most important thing working families have, just deleted it from working families' wealth so his chart would look scarier.

Bernie loves Social Security right up until it gets in the way of a graph. Then it's "promises of future benefits," and out it goes. That's the intellectual depth of a kiddie pool, and somebody already pulled the plug.

You want to play that game, Warren? Fine. Let's run Bernie's own numbers your way. Take away his Senate pension, since that's just a "promise of future benefits." Take away his cars and the furniture in all three houses, since those are just "durable goods." Bernie's still doing fine, because he has the houses. But a lot of the families you claim to be fighting for? You just erased half of what they own and then held a press conference about how little they have.

That's not a correction. That's a magic trick. Make the rabbit disappear, then complain that there's no rabbit. You're the kid who sticks the thermometer in ice water and then tells Mom he's too cold to go to school.

And the math in the post is slippery even on its own terms. $317.8 billion to $313 billion is a 1.5 percent drop. Your own chart labels it negative 1.5 percent. But in 1989 there were about 247 million Americans, and today there are about 340 million. The number of households went up by roughly 40 percent. Bernie wrote "total wealth" like everybody would know exactly what he meant. They didn't. That's the whole reason the community note exists.

And look at the chart you posted. It compares the top 20 households to the bottom 50 percent, using a definition of "wealth" that strips the bottom half's stuff out and leaves the top half's stock in. You put a stack of stock certificates next to a family with their car and their retirement subtracted, and then you act surprised that one line goes up and the other goes flat. Warren, you didn't discover inequality. You manufactured a slope. You couldn't find the mean with a map and a flashlight, but you sure know how to find a mean headline.

Here's the honest version, and it's still not great. The Fed's own numbers show the bottom half's SHARE of total wealth is lower than it was in the late 1980s, about 2.3 percent today compared to the high 3s back then, with a big crash during the 2008 housing bust and a partial recovery since. That's a real conversation worth having. But the bottom half's actual wealth went up a lot. Share down, level way up. Bernie told everybody the level didn't move. That's just not true.

Let me name what you did, Warren, because I teach this too.

Cherry-picking: you picked the one private data series that gave you the scariest line.

Moving the goalposts: when the community note caught Bernie saying "total wealth," you changed the definition to "total wealth minus the stuff we decided not to count."

Appeal to authority: you waved "Fed data" around even though the actual Fed data says something completely different.

And the ad hoc rescue: when the claim got caught, you didn't fix it. You invented a reason it was secretly right all along.

That's four fallacies in one tweet. I'd give you credit for efficiency, but this isn't that kind of class. In my room, your standard deviation is just how far you deviate from the standard. Every single time.

Quinn's Law Number Six: facts are the enemy of liberalism. Put the real denominator back under the scary number, and the scary number goes away. So you just took the denominator out. Dumber than a box of paper clips, and at least paper clips hold things together.

And here's where all this was headed. A chart like this exists to sell one thing: a wealth tax. Bernie's been pushing one in California this week, and Ro Khanna, who just reposted you, has been on stage with him doing it. But even if your chart were perfect, it wouldn't prove a wealth tax works. France tried one and scrapped most of it in 2018 after money and people left. Sweden dumped theirs. Germany stopped collecting theirs. The chart is the sales pitch. The product has already been recalled in half of Europe. Selling it anyway is like pushing a parachute that opens on the second bounce.

What's next, a Senate staffer defending his boss by deleting half of poor families' wealth and calling it "more accurate"... wait. I'm being told that's this post.

Warren, you're a GPS that only gives directions to the conclusion. You're a calculator with the minus key taped down. You're the guy who comes to a math test with the answer already written on his hand and then argues with the teacher about the question.

You're holding the magnifying glass upside down and wondering why everything looks so small. You've got a bell curve that's a flat line and a brain that's buffering. You're the brightest bulb in a burned-out chandelier.

And I mean this sincerely: whoever taught you statistics owes the taxpayers a refund.

I'll make you the same offer I make your boss. If you really think the bottom half is that broke, go tell them their car isn't theirs, their fridge doesn't count, and their Social Security is just a "promise." Say it to their faces. Say it at a Bernie rally. I'll wait.

But what do I know? I'm only a physics teacher who makes teenagers keep every data point, show every unit, and explain every exclusion, which is apparently three more rules than a Senate staff director follows.

@BernieSanders @RoKhanna @TPUSA @atrupar @JoJoFromJerz

Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma, a mathematical result concerning low-distortion embeddings of points from high-dimensional into low-dimensional Euclidean space contributed by Joram Lindenstrauss.

Expansion of axiomatic set theory and the ZF set theory by Abraham Fraenkel.

Development of multiscale models for complex chemical systems by Arieh Warshel and Michael Levitt of the Weizmann Institute of Science (presently at University of Southern California and Stanford University, respectively), together with the Austrian-born American chemist Martin Karplus. Before the Israeli emergency bandage was invented in 1998, wounded soldiers were told to find a rock and wrap it on top of hemorrhaging wounds in order to hold direct pressure.[36] Bar-Natan sold his company to PerSys Medical Inc in Houston, Texas, the company that first introduced the bandage to the US military.📷An Israeli Bandage being used by Sudanese and US Naval service members during a training exercise.

Developments in Game theory. Israel Aumann of the Hebrew University of Jerusalem received the 2005 Nobel Prize in Economics for his work in this field.[48]

text:
🗺️ $SPX heatmap: the narrow green 🟢

Today's S&P 500 map is a study in concentration. The index is green, but look at what's green: GOOGL +2.05% doing the megacap heavy lifting, MSFT +1.04%, AMZN and META modestly higher — and then the real story, semicap equipment: AMAT +1.55%, LRCX +1.43%, KLAC +1.28%, the hottest corner of the entire map. 🔧
Everything else is sitting out. AAPL -0.91%. Healthcare a sea of red: LLY -0.70%, JNJ -0.66%, MRK -0.62%, ABBV -0.86%. Energy soft (XOM -0.63%). Banks red across the board (JPM, BAC, WFC, MS all lower). This is the same rotation family as yesterday's cool-PCE session — growth bid, defensives offered — except today's leadership is narrower and more specific.

Two divergences deserve your attention. First: NVDA +0.20% while its own equipment suppliers rip 1.3–1.6%. The market isn't selling AI — it's rotating within AI, from the crowded GPU trade into the picks-and-shovels capex names. That's a mature-bull move, not a euphoric one. Second: INTC -1.52%, the reddest large semi on the board while the group rallies. When the group is up and one name is down 1.5%, that's idiosyncratic — worth a headline check, not a sector call.
Session context matters: this map is the market's answer to this morning's ISM Manufacturing PMI plus a five-speaker Fed parade (Barkin, Collins, Schmid, Williams, Logan). The verdict so far: growth bid intact, no rate scare, tech carrying the tape into the data.

The risk is breadth. An index carried by GOOGL and three equipment stocks while Apple, healthcare, energy, and banks all sag is not a healthy rally — it's a concentrated one. Fine for the bulls as long as leadership holds; fragile the moment it doesn't. Friday's NFP is the next judge. 👀

Its 2026, @HBLPak   Incase if you guys are confused.
Sometimes I think about Pakistani banking systems and I honestly just laugh. 

They try to secure one thing and break three others in the process. ( HBL Give your developer Fable access please, sonnet is ruining instead of fixing it) 

Just now I am trying to reset my HBL mobile banking password. Simple, right? 

Heres the loop I got stuck in: 
→Tap Forgot Password App tells me to stay on the screen to verify OTP comes as a phone call,
→Not an SMS Not a normal call either.
→Select your language. 
→Enter a 4-digit PIN. 
→To do that, I have to leave the app Come back, and the app has thrown me to the home screen Log in again, request again, get a new call Leave the app again to answer it (At this point I was pretty sure the app and the IVR were in a toxic relationship and I was the kid stuck in the middle xD)

Each piece makes sense on its own. 

Kill the session when the app goes to the background? 
Fine, thats anti-hijacking. Verify over a call? Fine, thats a second channel. 

Put them together on one phone and the user cant finish the job at all. 
So I did what any normal person does. 
I called customer support. 

25 minutes on hold. Twenty-five. (Writing this post while still on waiting ) 
Users either give up, go to a branch, or tie up a support line that already cant handle the load. 
The fix isnt rocket science: 

→ Keep the reset session alive for 60–90 seconds in the background 
→ Offer SMS OTP, with the call as a fallback 
→ Actually test the full journey on a real phone, not each feature in isolation These are some of the biggest banks in the country with massive tech budgets. How does something like this make it to production?

text:
Google offered 3 college kids $30 MILLION to buy their project. They said NO. Today that project makes $3 BILLION per year.

This is Dropbox.

In 2007, Drew Houston was on a bus from Boston to New York. He opened his laptop to work. He forgot his USB drive.

All his files gone. He was furious.

He thought: "Why can't my files just follow me? Like my email?"

He went home and started coding in his MIT dorm.

He built a folder that syncs everywhere. Drag file in, appears on all computers.

Simple.

He showed it to his co-founder Arash. They made a video — just a screen recording with funny jokes. Posted on Hacker News.

Overnight: 75,000 people signed up for the waiting list. Their servers crashed.

Steve Jobs saw it. Called Drew to his office.

Jobs said: "You are building a feature, not a company. I will give you a great deal, join Apple or we will crush you."

Drew said no.

Then Google came. $30M offer. For 2 kids in college. That's life-changing money.

Drew said NO again.

Everyone thought he was crazy. His parents thought he was crazy.

He kept building.

2012: 100 million users
2018: IPO'd at $9.2 BILLION
Today: $3B revenue per year, 700M users.

That $30M he rejected became $1.4B for him personally.

Lessons:
 1.  If Steve Jobs threatens you, you are building something big.
 2.  A simple frustration + simple solution = billions.
 3.  $30M is small money if you believe your idea is $3B/year money.

Would YOU have rejected $30M at 24?

Follow for 1 startup story daily.

text:
"...why a highly educated policy analyst like @DougAMacgregor would look at the historical layout, know the data, and still drop a prediction that completely contradicts how Congress operates... look past simple cognitive dissonance...

When people steeped in Beltway history make claims that  flies in the face of political reality, it usually boils down to three very tactical, calculated reasons:

 The "Electoral Magic Wand" Fallacy
Macgregor’s modern commentary heavily focuses on the collapse of American hegemony, institutional corruption, and the stranglehold of the defense lobby. When he shifts to forecasting a midterm reversal of Section 219/1217, he isn't analyzing Congress's track record—he is leaning into an operational narrative to mobilize voters

By treating the  midterms as a massive, world-altering inflection point, he frames the election as a tool capable of shattering deeply entrenched military policy. It’s a classic rhetorical device: you have to tell the audience that the system can be overridden by their vote, even if your own understanding of history tells you the defense establishment almost always wins

 Tailoring Content for @jimmy_dore ’s Audience
Jimmy Dore's entire platform is built on exposing institutional betrayals, the uniparty and the failure of the political establishment. If Macgregor went on the show and said, "Hey Jimmy, look, this defense-industrial merger is permanent, the midterms won't change it, and the Democrats will just reauthorize it anyway," the conversation hits a dead end.

Predicting a sweeping reversal creates narrative momentum. It sets up a high-stakes scenario:
• It gives Dore’s audience a specific metric to track.
• It creates an immediate enemy out of the current legislative session.
• It allows them to spin a story about how the public can force a course correction, feeding the exact flavor of populist optimism his listeners tune in for.

The "Anti-War Realignment" Illusion

Macgregor has long been a vocal proponent of a nationalist, non-interventionist foreign policy. There is a prevailing theory among certain populist factions that a massive public backlash against foreign wars and rising inflation will trigger an unprecedented, systemic purge of defense establishment hawks.

When he predicts a reversal, he is likely treating the incoming freshman class not as standard political operatives, but as an idealized wave of populist disruptors who will break party lines to smash the NDAA. He is substituting a wish for a structural reality—hoping that public anger over global escalation will override decades of institutional inertia.

The  Failure Point
The factual disconnect in his theory isn't just about party identity; it's about interoperability. Because Sections 219/1217 embed tech development and supply lines deep within the military infrastructure, reversing them isn't as simple as changing a policy stance. It means actively pulling apart joint programs, canceling defense contracts, and severing hardware/software pipelines that are already operational.
Macgregor knows how hard it is to untangle military supply lines. Choosing to broadcast a clean, simple "midterm reversal" anyway is a calculated media play to keep the anti-interventionist base engaged, rather than delivering a cold, institutional analysis that offers no easy way out." — @GeminiApp

text:
In 1996 an envelope arrived at the home of an old man in New York. Inside was a Pepsi-Cola advertisement, forty-odd years out of date, showing a woman holding a six-pack while a small boy reached up toward one of the bottles.

The woman in the picture was a Harlem model named Sylvia Fitt, hired for the shoot. The boy was Ronald H. Brown, who grew up to become Secretary of Commerce of the United States and who had been killed that April in a plane crash on a trade mission to Croatia.

Brown had kept that advertisement on display in his office. After he died, his mother mailed it back to the man who had made it.

His name was Edward Francis Boyd, he was eighty-two years old, and almost nobody in America knew what he had done. The story starts half a century earlier, with a company that was losing.

In 1947 Pepsi-Cola was the cheap cola. Coca-Cola owned the country, and Pepsi was the twelve-ounce bottle for a nickel, the drink you bought when you were counting.

Walter Mack ran the company and had done arithmetic his competitors would not do. There were roughly fourteen million Black Americans and they bought soda like everybody else.

Almost no major corporation in the country was addressing them as customers. The ones that pictured Black people at all pictured them as Aunt Jemima.

He had tried this once already. In 1940 he hired an advertising man named Herman T. Smith, ran an essay contest to recruit Black college graduates, and brought Allen L. McKellar and Jeanette Maund to New York as interns before the war shut the whole effort down.

In 1947 he tried again. He called in a thirty-two-year-old housing specialist from the National Urban League and offered him a job he had not come asking for.

Boyd had been a singer and an actor in Hollywood in the late thirties, and he knew what rooms in this country were closed. On the night Hattie McDaniel became the first Black performer to win an Academy Award, Boyd was her escort.

He took the title of assistant sales manager and built a team of twelve. On paper they were absurdly overqualified to be selling soda.

Charles E. Wilson came out of Hampton Institute wanting to be a doctor. Jean F. Emmons held one of the very few business master's degrees in Black America, William Simms had been told by W. E. B. Du Bois himself to go get educated, and Alexander L. Jackson had a Harvard degree.

Boyd's idea for the advertising was so plain it should not have been revolutionary. Show Black Americans as ordinary middle-class people, in their own homes, buying things, living well.

One series was called Leaders in Their Fields and put men like Ralph Bunche in front of the country before Bunche had his Nobel Prize. A run of six magazine ads in 1949 profiled outstanding students at Black colleges, and those pages ended up pinned to classroom walls in Black high schools and colleges around the country.

Another series was drawn by Jay Jackson, a Black cartoonist known for putting satire about race into the Chicago Defender. The Ron Brown ad came out of the same work, a mother and a son and a six-pack, nothing remarkable in it, which was the entire point.

Then there was the selling, and the selling is the part that gets left out.

These twelve men worked the country on the ground, and much of that ground was the segregated South. They called on bottlers, churches, civic clubs, business associations and professional meetings, and they often did it seven days a week.

They rode in the back of buses. They ate behind curtains on trains, and when the curtain was more than a man could take, they carried their meals into the Pullman car.

They drank from the fountains marked for them. Hotels turned them away, so they slept in the spare rooms of Black families in whatever town they were working that week.

Alexander Jackson was ordered to the back of a bus during a campaign in the South. He had a degree from Harvard University and a Pepsi-Cola sales case in his hand, and he got up and moved.

The Ku Klux Klan sent threats. The insults that landed hardest came from inside the company, from white Pepsi employees who did not care for the sight of them.

In 1949 Mack stood up at the Waldorf-Astoria in front of five hundred Pepsi bottlers who were nervous that the campaign was turning Pepsi into a Black drink and would cost them their white customers. To settle the room, the president of the company used the ugliest word in the American language to describe what he did not want Pepsi to become.

Boyd was in that room.

He got up and walked out of the auditorium. Mack apologized to him afterward, and Boyd went back to work building the thing his own president had just disowned in front of five hundred men.

He talked about it decades later, in his eighties, to a reporter from The Wall Street Journal. He said he had not forgotten it and had not held it against the man either, which is a sentence worth sitting with for a while.

What those twelve men built out of all that worked. Pepsi sales climbed through Black communities across the country, and in Chicago the company passed Coca-Cola for the first time, in a market where that had been considered impossible.

Coca-Cola's chairman, in those same years, publicly backed Herman Talmadge in Georgia, a governor who ran on segregation. Word of that traveled through Black America the way word travels, and Pepsi picked up a reputation as the cola that treated you like a person.

The salesmen themselves became known. Jet and Ebony wrote them up, and families cut the pictures out, because a photograph of a Black man with a briefcase and a corporate title was not a thing you saw.

There is a detail in all of this that will stay with you. Harvey Russell, who joined the team in 1950, said that in a striving Black household you served Pepsi in the kitchen and brought out Coke when guests came into the living room.

They were selling a drink some of their own people were quietly ashamed to be seen holding. They kept selling it, and they turned the shame around into something like loyalty.

Around 1950 Walter Mack lost a corporate fight and left the company. The special markets team did not survive him by long.

The new leadership dismantled the division. Some of the men were folded into regional sales, and Edward Boyd, who had built the entire thing from nothing, was let go.

He was thirty-seven years old and he had just proved something no other corporation in America had proved.

One of the twelve, a man who had spent years succeeding at Pepsi and who held a master's degree in business from the University of Chicago, later took a job mopping floors to feed his family. That is what sat on the other side of the door for a Black executive in 1951.

There was no next corporation and no second offer. A man who had helped build a national market for one of the largest brands in the country picked up a mop, and the record of his working life after Pepsi is a job cleaning somebody else's building.

Harvey Russell was the one who stayed.

He had tried the other road first. Before Pepsi he worked briefly for the Brown Belle Bottling Company, a Black-owned soft drink outfit run by A. G. Gaston that put out Joe Louis Punch with Joe Louis himself invested in it, and the company failed.

He joined Pepsi as a field representative in 1950 and stayed thirty-three years. In July 1962 the company made him a vice president, and he became the first Black officer of a major American multinational corporation.

More than a hundred newspapers carried it and cabinet members wrote letters of commendation. Ebony called him "the top Negro in American big business."

The Klan called for a boycott of Pepsi over the promotion of one man. It failed.

Forty-three years after Boyd took the job, in July 1990, Pepsi-Cola sold controlling interest in its Washington bottling operation to Earl G. Graves Sr. and Earvin Johnson for sixty million dollars. Graves took better than sixty-five percent of it and the title of chief executive.

The trucks running out of that six-acre yard in Forestville, Maryland delivered to the White House, the United States Capitol and Air Force One. It was announced at the National Press Club and covered as the largest minority-controlled Pepsi franchise in the country, which it was.

Edward Boyd was seventy-six that summer and living in New York. Go through the coverage of that announcement, the wire copy and the trade press and the business pages, and the twelve men who made Black America a Pepsi market are not in any of it.

The market Graves bought into was not lying there waiting for somebody with sixty million dollars. The building of it started on foot, in the Jim Crow South, seven days a week, with men sleeping in strangers' spare rooms because the hotels were shut to them.

Boyd lived to ninety-two and died in 2007. He went a few months after a Wall Street Journal reporter named Stephanie Capparell finally put the whole story between covers, which is the closest thing to a reckoning he got.

Go back to 1949 and leave him there.

That year Boyd went to see a play in New York, Arthur Miller's Death of a Salesman, about a man who gave a company everything he had and was thrown out at the end of it. He was thirty-five, at the height of the thing he was building, two years from being let go himself.

He sat in the dark and he wept.

I put a lot of effort into researching and sharing stories that matter.
If you'd like to support the work, here's the link:
https://t.co/ssPLXOgFfE
Every coffee helps me keep creating.

text:
🚨🇺🇸 U.S. IN DESPAIR: NASA RISKS COSTLY RESURRECTION OF SPY PLANE GROUNDED SINCE 1999

The U.S. Air Force and NASA destroyed a reported $600M stockpile of SR-71 spare parts in 2007. Now NASA appears to be trying to return one of the retired Blackbirds to flight.

Aviation Week reports that SR-71A Tail No. 844, which last flew on October 9, 1999, has been removed from outdoor display and moved into a hangar at NASA’s Armstrong Flight Research Center. The agency has also offered jobs to former Blackbird engineers.

NASA has not officially confirmed the return-to-flight project or disclosed its purpose, budget or schedule.

🔸 Washington destroyed the parts it now needs. The Air Force and NASA reportedly eliminated a $600M stockpile of Blackbird spares after concluding that the aircraft would never fly again. Replacements may now have to be manufactured from scratch or taken from museum aircraft that are almost as old as Tail No. 844.

🔸 The engines may have sat without proper care for decades. Former SR-71 engineer Mike Relja said stored J58 engines were normally rotated every 90 days and run every 180 days. He believes the engines associated with Tail No. 844 may not have received such maintenance since the aircraft’s final flight.

🔸 Much of the support network no longer exists. The Blackbird requires JP-7 fuel, triethylborane for engine ignition, specialized oils and hydraulic fluids. Purpose-built equipment used to lift the wings and remove the engines, inlet spikes and ejection seats has also disappeared.

🔸 NASA would have to rebuild the workforce. Pilots, engineers and maintenance crews would need to relearn how to operate a 59-year-old aircraft. Former personnel can recover some of that knowledge, but several specialists NASA reportedly approached are already in their seventies.

🔸 The Blackbird demanded extraordinary maintenance. Historical records describe a post-flight checklist containing around 650 items. Every 100 flight hours triggered an inspection lasting approximately 11 working days.

🔸 NASA has not explained what taxpayers would receive. The agency previously used SR-71s for research into propulsion, high-temperature materials, aerodynamics and sonic booms. No experiment has yet been announced that would justify recreating the aircraft’s entire support system.

Washington has paid to revive retired military hardware before. Reactivating the four Iowa-class battleships cost roughly $1.7B in mixed 1982–1988 dollars — around $5B today. Wisconsin returned to service in October 1988 and was retired again in September 1991.

The Blackbird could still provide a unique Mach 3 research platform. Until NASA presents a clear mission and budget, however, the project looks like the U.S. paying to recreate a capability its own government deliberately dismantled.

Is bringing back the Blackbird genius or a waste of taxpayer money?

Tel Megiddo (from Hebrew: תל מגידו; Arabic: تل المتسلم, Tell el-Muteselim) is the site of the ancient city of Megiddo (/məˈɡɪdoʊ/; Hebrew: מגידו; Greek: Μεγιδδώ), the remains of which form a tell or archaeological mound, situated in northern Israel at the western edge of the Jezreel Valley. During the Bronze Age, Megiddo was an important Canaanite city-state, and in the Iron Age, it became a royal city in the Kingdom of Israel. The site is renowned for its historical, geographical, and theological significance, especially under its Greek name Armageddon (Ἁρμαγεδών), which appears once in the Koine Greek New Testament in Revelation 16:16.

Excavations have unearthed 20 strata of ruins since the Neolithic phase, indicating a long settlement period.[1] Occupied continuously from the early Bronze Age (c. 3000 BCE) to the Persian period (c. 332 BCE), Megiddo was strategically located at the crossroads of major ancient trade routes, making it a key center for trade, politics, and military affairs. Excavations have uncovered impressive fortifications, including massive city walls and gates, as well as palaces, temples, residential buildings, and a sophisticated water system. The site is protected as Megiddo National Park and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.[2]

Assyrian period
Tiglath-Pileser III of Assyria conquered Megiddo in 732 BCE, turning it to the capital of the Neo-Assyrian Empire's province of Magiddu.[16] Hoshea (c. 732–721 BCE), the last king of the Israelite Northern Kingdom, was vassal to Tiglath-Pileser III. The site was rebuilt as an administrative center for Tiglath-Pileser III's occupation of Samaria.

Egyptian period
In 609 BCE, Megiddo was conquered by Egyptians under Necho II, during the Battle of Megiddo.

Babylonian period
Its importance soon dwindled, and it was thought as finally abandoned around 586 BCE.[64] Since that time it would have remained uninhabited, preserving ruins pre-dating 586 BCE without settlements ever disturbing them. Archaeologist Eric Cline considers that Tel Megiddo came to an end later, around 350 BCE, during Achaemenid times.[1] Then, the town of al-Lajjun, not to be confused with the al-Lajjun archaeological site in Jordan, was built up near to the site, but without inhabiting or disturbing its remains.

Roman and Byzantine periods
During the Roman and Byzantine periods, while the site was part of the provinces of Syria Palaestina (136-390) and Palaestina Secunda (390-638), there were three settlements in the vicinity of the tell: the Jewish village of Kefar 'Othnay (Caparcotna in Latin or Kaperkotnei in Greek); Legio, the Roman military camp of the Legio VI Ferrata ('6th "Ironclad" Legion'); and later, in the 4th and 5th centuries during Byzantine rule, a polis named Maximianopolis.[65] J. C. Howry, processing the results of a surface reconnaissance survey in 2019 which had used LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) technology to obtain enhanced images of the ground, places Maximianopolis northwest of the tell, Legio south-southeast of it, and a village which grew next to the legion camp for which it provided services (the future Arab village of Lejjun), southwest of the tell.[66] Adams, David and Tepper (2014) write that the VIth Legion was deployed to the country sometime between 100 and 132, and was stationed there through most of the 3rd century;[65] Howry (2020) places it at Legio between 192 and 316.[66]

Megiddo church
The Megiddo church is next to Megiddo Junction, inside the precinct of the Megiddo Prison. It was built within the ancient city of Legio. It is believed to date to the 3rd century, making it one of the oldest Christian churches in the world. It was a few hundred yards from the Roman base camp of Legio VI Ferrata. A centurion donated one of the mosaics found in the church.[67]

Modern period
Megiddo is south of Kibbutz Megiddo by 1 kilometre (0.62 mi). Today,it lies at the northern entrance to Wadi Ara, an important mountain pass connecting the Jezreel Valley within Israel's coastal plain.[68]

In 1964, during Pope Paul VI's visit to the Holy Land, Megiddo was the site where he met with dignitaries, including President Zalman Shazar and the Prime Minister Levi Eshkol.[69]

Battles
Famous battles include:
Battle of Megiddo (15th century BCE): fought between the armies of the Egyptian pharaoh Thutmose III and a large Canaanite coalition led by the rulers of Megiddo and Kadesh.
Battle of Megiddo (609 BCE): fought between Necho II, pharaoh of the Twenty-sixth Dynasty of Egypt, and the Kingdom of Judah, during which King Josiah fell.
Battle of Megiddo (1918): fought during World War I between Allied troops, led by General Edmund Allenby and the defending Ottoman army.

What is the Battle of Armageddon?
@gotquestions 
Answer
The word Armageddon is used generically today to refer to any type of catastrophic conflict, especially if it’s seen as likely to result in widespread destruction or the annihilation of human life. In the Bible, Armageddon refers to a climactic future battle between God and the forces of evil, as recorded in the book of Revelation. The word ultimately comes from the Hebrew word Har-Magedone, which means “Mount Megiddo,” the predicted location of the battle.

Revelation 16:12–16 is the record of what will happen toward the end of the tribulation, when an angel pours out the sixth bowl judgment on the earth. The word Armageddon makes its only appearance in the Bible in this passage:

“The sixth angel poured out his bowl on the great river Euphrates, and its water was dried up to prepare the way for the kings from the East. Then I saw three impure spirits that looked like frogs; they came out of the mouth of the dragon, out of the mouth of the beast and out of the mouth of the false prophet. They are demonic spirits that perform signs, and they go out to the kings of the whole world, to gather them for the battle on the great day of God Almighty. . . . Then they gathered the kings together to the place that in Hebrew is called Armageddon.”

In Revelation 19:11–20, a final battle occurs at Christ’s second coming as the conquering Christ defeats the forces of the Antichrist. We take this to be a description of the Battle of Armageddon mentioned in Revelation 19:

“I saw heaven standing open and there before me was a white horse, whose rider is called Faithful and True. With justice he judges and wages war. His eyes are like blazing fire, and on his head are many crowns. He has a name written on him that no one knows but he himself. He is dressed in a robe dipped in blood, and his name is the Word of God. The armies of heaven were following him, riding on white horses and dressed in fine linen, white and clean. Coming out of his mouth is a sharp sword with which to strike down the nations. ‘He will rule them with an iron scepter.’ He treads the winepress of the fury of the wrath of God Almighty. On his robe and on his thigh he has this name written: KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS.

“And I saw an angel standing in the sun, who cried in a loud voice to all the birds flying in midair, ‘Come, gather together for the great supper of God, so that you may eat the flesh of kings, generals, and the mighty, of horses and their riders, and the flesh of all people, free and slave, great and small.’

“Then I saw the beast and the kings of the earth and their armies gathered together to wage war against the rider on the horse and his army. But the beast was captured, and with it the false prophet who had performed the signs on its behalf. With these signs he had deluded those who had received the mark of the beast and worshiped its image. The two of them were thrown alive into the fiery lake of burning sulfur. The rest were killed with the sword coming out of the mouth of the rider on the horse, and all the birds gorged themselves on their flesh.”

The exact location of Armageddon is unclear because there is no mountain called Meggido. However, since Har can also mean “hill,” the most likely location is the hill country surrounding the plain of Meggido, some sixty miles north of Jerusalem. Throughout history, armies have fought countless battles in that region: Egyptians, Assyrians, Greeks, Romans, and Crusaders fought in Megiddo, as well as the armies of Napoleon. Megiddo was the site of battles during World War I and the Arab-Israeli War of 1948 (Weintraub, P., “Rewriting Tel Megiddo’s Violent History,” Discover, Sep 30, 2015). In the future, the plain of Megiddo and the nearby plain of Esdraelon will also be the focal point for the battle of Armageddon.

The plain of Megiddo, or Armageddon, was famous for two great victories in Israel’s history: 1) Barak’s victory over the Canaanites (Judges 4:15) and 2) Gideon’s victory over the Midianites (Judges 7). Armageddon was also the site of two great tragedies: 1) the death of Saul and his sons (1 Samuel 31:8) and 2) the death of King Josiah (2 Kings 23:29–30; 2 Chronicles 35:22).

According to the futurist interpretation of Revelation, which is our view, the Battle of Armageddon will be a real battle in the future, near the end of the tribulation. Demonic influences will cause the kings of the earth to gather their armies for an all-out assault on Jerusalem. The Antichrist will be leading the charge (Revelation 16:13–16). Jesus Christ will return to earth with the armies of heaven (Matthew 25:31; Revelation 19:14); His feet will stand on the Mount of Olives (Zechariah 14:4); He will defeat the forces of evil (Revelation 19:15–16); He will cast the Antichrist and the false prophet into the lake of fire (Revelation 19:20); He will bind Satan; and He will set up His kingdom on earth for 1,000 years (Revelation 20:1–6). At Armageddon the Lord Jesus Christ “treads the winepress of the fury of the wrath of God Almighty” (Revelation 19:15), and all things will be made right.

AURELIA TIDECREST AND THE MAP SHE REFUSED TO FINISH

Aurelia's maps showed roads that only existed in certain weather.

A staircase during a thunderstorm. A bridge in the first frost. A narrow coastal trail that appeared when fog hid the moon.

Travelers paid well for directions like those. They paid even better for someone willing to walk beside them.

The commission arrived in a waterproof envelope. A collector wanted a complete map of the wandering valley, a place that shifted beyond the mountain passes every autumn. Finish the map, the letter promised, and Aurelia would never need another job.

She found the valley after three nights of rain.

There were orchards, bright windows, and people who greeted strangers without asking where they had come from. An old woman offered her soup. A child showed her a bridge made from the roots of two enormous trees.

Aurelia began drawing.

With every road she marked, the valley grew easier to find. With every landmark she named, the fog around its borders thinned.

On the fourth morning, she saw riders on the distant ridge.

The collector had followed her unfinished work.

At the village hall, she learned why the valley wandered. It sheltered people whose former rulers believed leaving was a crime. A complete map would pin the place to the world and turn every hidden path into an entrance.

Aurelia sat beside the root bridge with her pens spread across the grass.

One bedtime book a day hands a child about 78,000 extra words a year.

Ohio State researchers counted the words in 60 common kids books and ran the math to age five. A child read to daily hears about 297,000 book words by kindergarten. A child never read to hears about 4,700.

Five books a day stretches the gap past 1.4 million words. About a quarter of caregivers report never reading with their child.

That is words offered in books. How many become the child's own vocabulary is a separate question this study did not test.

text:
This is a topic that is gaining steam, so let me offer my opinion on this:

It’s really a tier thing at all of these levels.

The top tier of G6 is going to be a hard out for even the top tier of FCS programs week in and week out.

And honestly, most of the FCS outside of maybe 5-10 programs are much closer to the top tier of D2 than they are to the top of the FCS. 

Top-tier D2 programs like Ferris State and Harding are going to be competitive with top-tier FCS programs (see West Florida) while also consistently handling teams toward the bottom of the FCS.

The same thing happens at every level.

Top-tier D3 programs like North Central and top-tier NAIA programs like Grand View can compete with the best D2 teams, while also consistently handling teams toward the bottom of D2.

But I think there is an important distinction: playing up a level and beating a team on a singular day is not the same as being able to compete at that level week in and week out. 

A team can absolutely catch a higher-level opponent on the right day and win. That's college football. But doing that against comparable competition over the course of an entire season is a completely different challenge.

I love the FCS, but sometimes I think we get a little ahead of ourselves when talking about FCS vs. FBS.

The FCS has 6 wins over the FBS so far this season, but it’s not like FCS teams are going out there and blowing out FBS programs. 

Four of those six wins have been one-score games, and only one of the other two has been by more than one score.

Those wins are still impressive and deserve credit. An FCS team beating an FBS team is an FCS team beating an FBS team.

But there’s a difference between winning one game against a higher-level opponent and proving you can consistently compete at that level.

That's really the point with all of these levels of college football.

The labels matter, but the tiers within those labels matter just as much.

text:
Experimental Drug Reverses Paralysis and Vision Loss in MS-Like Disease | University of Virginia Health System, SciTechDaily

An experimental drug reversed paralysis and vision loss in mice with a multiple sclerosis-like disease while also preserving nerve tissue.

For the nearly one million Americans living with multiple sclerosis, current treatments offer ways to slow the disease and reduce flare-ups, but they cannot restore neurological function once it is lost. The condition typically strikes between ages 20 and 40 when immune cells mistakenly attack myelin, the protective sheaths that insulate nerves.

This harmful inflammation disrupts communication between the brain and the body, leading to vision loss, extreme fatigue, and progressive weakness. The autoimmune disorder varies greatly from patient to patient, but it ultimately reduces average life expectancy by seven years. Now, an experimental drug called Kamuvudine K-9 has reversed paralysis and vision loss in mice with a model of the disease.

Some people with multiple sclerosis (MS) experience long periods of remission, while severe cases can bring life-threatening complications. Doctors categorize the disease according to patients’ symptoms and relapses, reflecting the different courses it can take. Despite the benefits of available treatments, MS has no cure and remains the most common disabling neurological disease among young adults.

HIV drugs linked to lower MS risk

K-9 grew out of a discovery involving approved HIV medicines called nucleoside/nucleotide reverse transcriptase inhibitors, or NRTIs. UVA Health scientist Jayakrishna Ambati, MD, found that these drugs can block inflammasome activation, a process that drives inflammation. That finding prompted him to develop K-9, a derivative that appears safer and more effective than the drugs it came from.

Health records provided evidence that NRTIs might also affect MS. In a new paper, Ambati’s team reports an analysis of health insurance data from more than 3 million people. NRTI use was associated with a 41% lower risk of developing MS and, among people who already had the disease, a 36% lower annual relapse rate. Those associations concern the HIV medicines from which K-9 was derived, rather than K-9 itself.

Movement and vision return in mice

The mouse experiments allowed the researchers to examine K-9’s effects on both neurological function and the nerve tissue damaged by MS. Alongside the recovery of movement and vision, the drug preserved nerve fibers and their myelin insulation. It also halted the rise in neurofilament light chain (NfL), a blood marker of nerve damage. Animals given an approved MS drug in the same experiments recovered much less function than those receiving K-9.

“Most MS therapies are aimed at preventing the next attack. What’s remarkable is that K-9 not only prevented further neurological deterioration, but animals recovered function they had already lost,” said Ambati, founding director of UVA’s Center for Advanced Vision Science and the DuPont Guerry III Professor in the UVA School of Medicine’s Department of Ophthalmology. “When that recovery is considered together with the preservation of nerve tissue, the NfL response and the human epidemiologic findings, we believe there is a compelling rationale to test this approach in patients.”

Can K-9 restore function in people?

K-9 remains experimental for MS, and controlled clinical trials will be required to determine whether it can produce similar recovery in people. The drug has already entered trials for eye diseases, including diabetic macular edema and thyroid eye disease, and that clinical experience could help accelerate its evaluation for MS.

Because inflammasome activation and damage to axons, the nerve fibers that carry signals, are implicated in other neurodegenerative diseases, the researchers hope their findings will also inform work beyond MS. K-9 is slated to be tested for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).

“Inflammasome inhibition is now recognized as the cutting edge of therapies for multiple inflammatory diseases,” Ambati said. “K-9 and the related K-8, which has already shown remarkable efficacy in macular degeneration, could also be beneficial in other diseases such as Alzheimer’s disease and Parkinson’s disease.”

text:
Elon Musk’s first wife explains what it takes to become a billionaire:

Justine Musk, first wife of billionaire Elon Musk, knows a thing or two about wealth and hard work — her ex-husband is a founder of PayPal, CEO of Tesla and SpaceX, and has an estimated net worth of $248.7 billion. 

She posted a response to a Quora thread asking the question “Will I become a billionaire if I am determined to be one and put in all the necessary work required?”

Her answer is “no,” though she says that the Quora reader is asking the wrong question altogether. 

“You’re determined. So what? You haven’t been racing naked through shark-infested waters yet,” she writes. “Will you be just as determined when you wash up on some deserted island, disoriented and bloody and ragged and beaten and staring into the horizon with no sign of rescue?”

She then offers some advice: 

“Shift your focus away from what you want (a billion dollars) and get deeply, intensely curious about what the world wants and needs. Ask yourself what you have the potential to offer that is so unique and compelling and helpful that no computer could replace you, no one could outsource you, no one could steal your product and make it better and then club you into oblivion (not literally). Then develop that potential. Choose one thing and become a master of it.  Choose a second thing and become a master of that.  When you become a master of two worlds (say, engineering and business), you can bring them together in a way that will a) introduce hot ideas to each other, so they can have idea sex and make idea babies that no one has seen before and b) create a competitive advantage because you can move between worlds, speak both languages, connect the tribes, mash the elements to spark fresh creative insight until you wake up with the epiphany that changes your life.

The world doesn’t throw a billion dollars at a person because the person wants it or works so hard they feel they deserve it. (The world does not care what you want or deserve.)  The world gives you money in exchange for something it perceives to be of equal or greater value: something that transforms an aspect of the culture, reworks a familiar story or introduces a new one, alters the way people think about the category and make use of it in daily life. There is no roadmap, no blueprint for this; a lot of people will give you a lot of advice, and most of it will be bad, and a lot of it will be good and sound but you’ll have to figure out how it doesn’t apply to you because you’re coming from an unexpected angle. And you’ll be doing it alone, until you develop the charisma and credibility to attract the talent you need to come with you.

Have courage. 

And good luck.
