ZAMFARA @ 30: A STATE REBORN UNDER GOVERNOR DAUDA LAWAL

On October 1, 1996, a profound historic journey birthed across the vast expanses of the Northwest region when Zamfara State was carved out of the old Sokoto State as a standalone state. Despite the state being created by the military administration of the late General Sani Abacha, the birth of the state was greeted with overflowing euphoria from many who believed its a welcoming development to ensure more stability in governance.

The founding fathers of Zamfara envisioned a self-sustaining agricultural giant, proudly flying the banner “Farming is Our Pride” as its motto but also marked with action and not mere words on paper. With the vast arable agrarian lands and rich mineral deposits the state is blessed with, they imagined a haven of communal peace, where vibrant markets flourished, schools molded brilliant minds, basic amenities were standard and civic dignity was guaranteed to every indigene which would, in turn generate meaningfully development and place the state among the very best in the state and also the region. 

Yet, for nearly three decades that noble vision drifted into a tragic narrative of what could have been a dream come true. Sequential political administrations took the helm, but systemic governance deficits slowly starved the state of its promise also preventing it from reaching its full potential. Instead of transforming into an economic lighthouse, Zamfara became synonymous with institutional decay, bedridden with insecurity, banditry, kidnapping and illiteracy.

Basic infrastructure withered like a flower with no water supply; state-owned schools were reduced to crumbling dilapidated structures; general hospitals and Primary health centres lacked essential diagnostic tools and basic medications and a chronic backlog of unpaid civil service gratuities spanning over a decade left retired public servants in severe hardship. Worse still, an escalating rural security crisis took root, driving hundreds of thousands of farmers from their ancestral fields, paralysing interstate commerce and suffocating the state’s economic soul. For millions of residents, the proud dream of 1996 had morphed into a quiet, painful struggle for survival affecting the survival of the state.

History, however, rarely remains static when decisive leadership intervenes. As Zamfara State approaches its landmark 30th anniversary, the long-standing story of stagnation is undergoing a historic shift. The turning point arrived with the election of Governor Dauda Lawal in 2023, who defeated an incumbent against all odds; his “Rescue Mission” agenda did not merely offer political promises but launched a systematic engineering of state affairs. Governor Lawal took office with a clear diagnostic view of the state’s wounds. He moved away from cosmetic fixes to confront the structural defects that had held Zamfara back for twenty-seven years.

What distinguished Governor Lawal’s programme from the capital-centric spending that has historically defined Nigerian state governance is its geographic spread. In Bukkuyum Local Government Area, a region more often associated in national conversation with insecurity than with infrastructure investment, N4 billion has been committed to the 23-kilometre Mallamawa–Zarummai–Bukkuyum road with a spur to Zarummai Masama Road, alongside N1.5 billion for the Bukkuyum–Birnin Zuama–Gummi road. The government’s choice to route capital there is itself a statement of intent. In Maradun, N5 billion is allocated to the Maradun–Magami–Faru road and N1 billion to the Maradun–Makera road.

In Bungudu, N10 billion is going into the Daza–Gidan Dawa link to the Sokoto Road dual carriageway and N500 million for the 21-kilometre Tasha Babba–Lambar Kyambarawa Road in Nahuche Ward. In Birnin Magaji, N10 billion is earmarked for the 53-kilometre Gusau–Jauri–Dogon Kade–Nasarawa Mailayi–Nasarawar Godal roads. https://t.co/xNM0FNS6bR

With the vast arable agrarian lands and rich mineral deposits the state is blessed with, they imagined a haven of communal peace, where vibrant markets flourished, schools molded brilliant minds, basic amenities were standard and civic dignity was guaranteed to every indigene which would, in turn generate meaningfully development and place the state among the very best in the state and also the region. 

Yet, for nearly three decades that noble vision drifted into a tragic narrative of what could have been a dream come true. Sequential political administrations took the helm, but systemic governance deficits slowly starved the state of its promise also preventing it from reaching its full potential. Instead of transforming into an economic lighthouse, Zamfara became synonymous with institutional decay, bedridden with insecurity, banditry, kidnapping and illiteracy.

Basic infrastructure withered like a flower with no water supply; state-owned schools were reduced to crumbling dilapidated structures; general hospitals and Primary health centres lacked essential diagnostic tools and basic medications and a chronic backlog of unpaid civil service gratuities spanning over a decade left retired public servants in severe hardship. Worse still, an escalating rural security crisis took root, driving hundreds of thousands of farmers from their ancestral fields, paralysing interstate commerce and suffocating the state’s economic soul. For millions of residents, the proud dream of 1996 had morphed into a quiet, painful struggle for survival affecting the survival of the state.

History, however, rarely remains static when decisive leadership intervenes. As Zamfara State approaches its landmark 30th anniversary, the long-standing story of stagnation is undergoing a historic shift. The turning point arrived with the election of Governor Dauda Lawal in 2023, who defeated an incumbent against all odds; his “Rescue Mission” agenda did not merely offer political promises but launched a systematic engineering of state affairs. Governor Lawal took office with a clear diagnostic view of the state’s wounds. He moved away from cosmetic fixes to confront the structural defects that had held Zamfara back for twenty-seven years.

What distinguished Governor Lawal’s programme from the capital-centric spending that has historically defined Nigerian state governance is its geographic spread. In Bukkuyum Local Government Area, a region more often associated in national conversation with insecurity than with infrastructure investment, N4 billion has been committed to the 23-kilometre Mallamawa–Zarummai–Bukkuyum road with a spur to Zarummai Masama Road, alongside N1.5 billion for the Bukkuyum–Birnin Zuama–Gummi road. The government’s choice to route capital there is itself a statement of intent. In Maradun, N5 billion is allocated to the Maradun–Magami–Faru road and N1 billion to the Maradun–Makera road.

In Bungudu, N10 billion is going into the Daza–Gidan Dawa link to the Sokoto Road dual carriageway and N500 million for the 21-kilometre Tasha Babba–Lambar Kyambarawa Road in Nahuche Ward. In Birnin Magaji, N10 billion is earmarked for the 53-kilometre Gusau–Jauri–Dogon Kade–Nasarawa Mailayi–Nasarawar Godal roads.

text:
Glimpses of Gibbon

“The expiring Senate displayed a sudden luster, blazed for a moment, and was extinguished forever.”

Gibbon’s mention of the rule of the Five Good Emperors again informs us the restoration of the Republic was always out of reach once Augustus remade Rome as a monarchy, and the best Rome could hope for was a virtuous king and the “image of the ancient Republic.” But as he has told us, once the choice of leaders was usurped by the vicious characters of the army, all these hopes of restoration are soon to be dashed. Our author delivers the outcome with chilling finality at the end of the section called Their joy and confidence.

"These lofty expectations were, however, soon disappointed; nor, indeed, was it possible that the armies in the provinces should long obey the luxurious and unwarlike nobles of Rome. On the slightest touch, the unsupported fabric of their pride and power fell to the ground. The expiring Senate displayed a sudden luster, blazed for a moment, and was extinguished forever."

After a short reign of about six months, Tacitus died in the harsh elements on a march with the army in Cappadocia. Florianus, the unworthy brother of the dead emperor, rashly assumed to usurp the throne without even the cover of approval of the Senate. Things reverted to the form of succession we have become accustomed to expect when the general of the East, the powerful Probus, marched with his army to seize the throne. Faced with these superior forces, Florianus’ forces “delivered the empire from civil war by the easy sacrifice of a prince they despised.”
When Probus ascended the Imperial throne, he was about forty-four years of age; in the full possession of fame, of the love of the army, and of a mature vigor of mind and body.
In a nod to the imaginary power of the senate, we read in A.D. 276, August 3, how happily satisfied were the senators that “Probus should condescend thus humbly to solicit a scepter which he already possessed.” After Aurelius had humbled all of Rome’s barbarian enemies, they soon threatened the frontiers again. Probus, though he only reigned six years, “equaled the fame of ancient heroes, and restored peace and order to every province of the Roman world, as we read in Victories of Probus over the barbarians [279 or 280].
Gibbon provides us accounts of the many tribes of barbarians that are defeated by Probus, including Franks, Frisians, Batavians and Burgundians and other German invaders of Gaul, of whom “the most formidable were the Lygians, a distant people who reigned over a wide domain on the frontiers of Poland and Silesia.” Bringing peace to Gaul “cost the lives of four hundred thousand of the invaders,” which is an enormous number but only a fraction of the million or more that Caesar’s forces killed in the original conquest of Gaul three centuries earlier. When the king offers a piece of gold for the head of each enemy, Gibbon darkly informs us of human nature in such circumstances.

"But, as the fame of warriors is built on the destruction of human kind, we may naturally suspect that the sanguinary account was multiplied by the avarice of the soldiers, and accepted without any severe examination by the liberal vanity of Probus."

So complete were Probus’ victories that he returned to Rome to share his glory with the people in A.D. 281. Triumph of the emperor Probus.

"The arms of Probus had now suppressed all the foreign and domestic enemies of the state. His mild but steady administration confirmed the reestablishment of the public tranquility; Nor was there left in the provinces a hostile barbarian, a tyrant, or even a robber, to revive the memory of past disorders."

Everyone has worked out by now that the Houthis lie when they are losing!

Almost nobody has noticed that they lied first, and that the lie is what started this war.

Go back to July. Iran sent an aircraft to Sanaa to collect its Houthi delegation from Khamenei's funeral. Riyadh refused to let it fly home. The Houthis have never once explained what else was sitting in that cabin besides mourners, and nobody in Sanaa has offered a manifest.

What they did instead was build a grievance out of it.

On 20 July they launched what they called "siege for a siege." A phrase, invented in a studio, to convert a blocked plane into a justification for blockading Saudi Arabia and attacking shipping in the Red Sea.

Then came August, and the part Yemenis should never forgive. Al-Masirah began describing attacks on Yemeni forces as strikes on "Saudi aggressive mobilizations." They restarted a civil war against their own countrymen and broadcast it as self-defence against a foreign enemy!

Understand the sequence, because it is the whole story. The narrative was built first. The offensive followed it. The lie was not the cover for the war. The lie was the opening move of the war!

Now watch the same machine run in the opposite direction, because the ground has turned.

This week they claimed a government strike killed captured soldiers at a detention facility in Al-Hazm, Al-Jawf. Colonel Majed Abdullah Al-Nuzaili of the Yemeni armed forces stated flatly that no strike took place inside Al-Hazm, and that the story exists to hide what the Houthis do to men in their cells!

A building nobody may enter. A city they control. Prisoners nobody may see. They manufactured a crime and assigned it to the Yemeni army from inside the one place on earth where nobody can check!

They can do that because they jailed the witnesses first. Seventy-three UN staff in their prisons, some since 2021, aid workers and journalists alongside them, and a World Food Programme employee who died in their custody.

So here is today, 1 October, and here is what the studio is shouting over.

Fighting across eight fronts around Taiz alone. Bani Bakari. Jabal Habashi. Hamir. Al-Kadha. Kalaba. Jabal Gharab. Taba Yassin. Al-Ashrouh. Assifra. Salo. Al-Wazi'iyah struck from the air.

On the Al-Kadha front, Yemeni drones destroyed a 120mm cannon and set an ammunition depot burning.

And the detail that matters more than all of it put together.

The armed forces say they carried out eight precision strikes against three artillery batteries and a mobile air defence system in Mocha, built with Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps expertise.

Read that again. In Mocha.

Three weeks after seizing that port, the Houthis were not repairing it, not reopening it, not feeding anyone through it. They were installing an Iranian-engineered air defence system in it!

That is the answer to everyone who still calls this a Yemeni movement with Yemeni aims. They took the harbour that once sent coffee to the world and turned it into an IRGC firing position on the Red Sea. Not a port. A base. For somebody else's war.

And now the question nobody in Europe wants asked.

Who is carrying their signal?

Al-Masirah, the channel that manufactured "siege for a siege," that rebranded the killing of Yemenis as resistance to Riyadh, that produced the Al-Hazm lie, broadcasts in Arabic and English into millions of homes via Eutelsat. A French satellite. With a corporate presence registered in London!

European infrastructure. European jurisdiction. Carrying the propaganda arm of an Iranian-backed militia that recruits children through schools, shells displacement camps and starves Taiz.

Europe will send ASPIDES to escort ships past the Houthis, and simultaneously rent them the antenna!

A militia with no economy, no treasury and no industry has one genuinely modern weapon system, and the West is hosting it!

Take it off the satellite. Open the London books. You cannot bomb a narrative, but you can switch off its transmitter, and Europe has had the switch in its hand this entire time!

Because this is what the psychological war actually is. Not noise around the fighting. The fighting's origin, its justification, and now its life support.

The Houthis started this war with a sentence. Eight words invented in a television studio in July.

They will not finish it with one.

Men are already on the high ground above the coast road, drones are burning their ammunition at Al-Kadha, and the Iranian air defence they bolted onto Mocha is being taken apart piece by piece.

The Houthis started this war.

The Yemeni armed forces will end it!

I offered a timeline of NATO expansion into Eastern Europe that began during the Bill Clinton administration in 1994, continued during the George W. Bush admin, and has never stopped. For Russia, Ukraine became the "the straw that broke the camel's back." The full story here:

Vladimir Putin did not wake up on 24 February 2022 and decide, “I think I’ll invade eastern Ukraine today,” nor was the US campaign to expand NATO into Ukraine a last-minute maneuver. (US State Department documents show Ukraine’s future membership was discussed as early as 1994.)

9 Feb 1990: In a deal approved by Mikhail Gorbachev, the last leader of the Soviet Union, as a quid pro quo for accepting German reunification within NATO, Secretary of State James Baker pledged that NATO would not expand “one inch to the east.”

US, European and German leaders made explicit assurances to Gorbachev against any future eastward NATO expansion. Gorbachev understood the assurances as a “binding agreement.” Subsequently, Soviet leaders made decisions on that basis and acted on them - withdrawing the Red Army from Germany and dissolving the Warsaw Pact.

12 March 1999: Clinton is president. The Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland became members of NATO. A weakened post-Soviet Russia, led by Boris Yeltsin, controlled by a cabal of Oligarchs, could do nothing to prevent it. Powerless, Yeltsin was said to be “infuriated with his friend Bill Clinton...”

29 March 2004, largest wave of NATO enlargement ever. George W. Bush is president. Seven more Eastern European countries join NATO: Bulgaria, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Romania, Slovakia and Slovenia
April 2008: At the Bucharest NATO summit, George W. Bush announced that Ukraine and Georgia are on an “immediate path to NATO.”
Bill Burns, ambassador to Russia, sent a memo to Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice. “Across the board,” he wrote, the Russian political class told him, “Ukraine is the reddest of red lines” – “Nyet means nyet.”

22 Feb 2014: Kiev erupted in violence. State Department official Virginia Nuland boasted that the US had spent $5 billion on regime change in Ukraine. NATO rooftop snipers killed both protestors and police, forcing Ukraine’s democratically elected president Viktor Yanukovych to flee the country.

2 May 2014: Bussed to Odessa from Kiev, Right Sector thugs carrying baseball bats confront ethnic Russians protesting the coup. When protestors fled into the city's Trade Unions House, the building was set on fire. Forty-eight people were burned or bludgeoned to death.

Donbass civil war point of no return.

11 Feb 2015: Putin and Ukrainian President Poroshenko meet with French President Francois Hollande and German Chancellor Angela Merkel in Belarus to negotiate the Minsk ceasefire accords. The leaders agreed to a deal that would have ended the fighting – granting autonomy to the Russian-speaking Donbass, but successive Ukrainian governments refused to implement the accord. German Chancellor Merkel later admitted that Minsk was a stall tactic to allow the West to build Ukraine’s army up to NATO standards.

2019: Zelensky won a landslide election. He campaigned on a pledge to unite the ethnically divided former Soviet Republic. Once elected, however, he came under the thumb of the US neocons and the Ukrainian Banderite Neo-Nazis.

17 Dec 2021: Team Biden rejects Putin’s mutual security accords that would have left “neutral” #Ukraine intact. Biden: “Russia doesn’t say who can join NATO.” Once again, Russian concerns were brushed aside.

According to ex-Biden adviser Amanda Sloat, who was senior director for Europe on the National Security Council, Ukraine could have avoided war in December 2021 with one step: Ukrainian declaration of neutrality, she said, “would have prevented the destruction and loss of life."

18 Feb 2022: Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) reported that Ukraine had ramped up artillery attacks along the Donbass Line of Contact. (Since the 2014 coup, NATO-armed #Ukraine and neo-Nazi Banderites had killed thousands of ethnic Russians in the Donbass.)

19 Feb 2022: Zelensky was invited to speak at the Munich Security Conference. When questioned whether Ukraine was obligated to retain its non-nuclear status, he stated, “Ukraine’s non-nuclear status was “in doubt.”

20 Feb 2022: Sunday night, CBS 60 Minutes, Ukraine’s Minister of Foreign Affairs Dmytro Kuleba said, “Ukraine will never honor the Minsk cease fire.”

21 Feb 2022: Russia captured a Ukrainian soldier, killed five others as they crossed over the border into Rostov. Russia learned the invasion of Donetsk city was imminent.

24 Feb 2022: With about 100,000 troops, Russia launched its “Special Military Operation” - not a "full scale invasion." Citing the UN principle, “Responsibility to Protect,” Russia intervened in the eight-year Donbass civil war after all prospects for diplomacy had failed.

The war is about NATO's encroachment into the Russian borderlands and the West's repeated refusals to address Russian security concerns. Besides, as Putin learned growing up in the tough streets of St. Petersburg: “If you know there’s going to be a fight, throw the first punch.”

OTD in 1473 - The Lancastrians were occupying St Michael’s Mount. This followed the celebrated Lancastrian commander, the Earl of Oxford, launching a surprise assault on St Michael’s Mount & taking the castle on the previous day. He was accompanied by Lord Beaumont & 400 men. 

Oxford was funded by Louis XI of France. #EdwardIV needed Oxford removed to preserve the comprehensive victory the Yorkists had won at the Battle of Tewkesbury on 4 May 1471.

Oxford & Beaumont had fled to Scotland following the Lancastrian defeat at the Battle of Barnet on 14 April 1471. They then travelled to France & secured the support of Louis XI. After a period of piracy in the South West they identified St Michael’s Mount as the perfect target to give them a foothold & safe haven on English soil. 

Edward IV initially attempted to blockade the island  & starve the Lancastrians out. When this failed he resorted to overwhelming force, dispatching John Fortesque with 6,000 men in December 1473, along with the royal fleet & John Wode from the Royal Armouries who had heavy artillery under his command. 

This show of force combined with the offer of pardons for any defenders who voluntarily left the castle broke the Lancastrian resistance. In February 1474 Oxford & Beaumont surrendered & were imprisoned. 

But this wouldn’t be the last the Yorkists saw of Oxford. He was imprisoned near Calais. #RichardIII intended to move him to more secure confinement in the Tower of London, but Oxford escaped before he could be returned to England & was the most experienced commander in Henry Tudor’s army at the Battle of Bosworth on 22 August 1485.

“FAKE NEWS AT ITS FINEST” - THIS is why nobody trusts the mainstream media.  Time to CALL THEM OUT.

The U.S. Department of Education has responded to the BAD FAITH FRAMING coming from the “FAKE NEWS” on the DOE’s changes on federal student loans.

The DOE called a New Republic "banning degrees" headline fake news and said federal loans are not a welfare program for failing college programs.

The DOE’s official X account quoted The New Republic's claim that "Trump is banning students majoring in degrees that don't make enough money from taking out college loans." The department's reply opened with, "This is fake news at its finest."

"First off, we're not 'banning' any program," the official account wrote. "The federal government doesn't set curriculum or programs."
⠀
The department's own framing is narrower. A program that fails an earnings test in two of three consecutive years loses Direct Loan eligibility. The school can still offer the major.
⠀
Undergraduate programs have to show completers out-earn typical high-school graduates in the same state four years later. Graduate programs have to beat the median for bachelor's holders.
⠀
The first calculations are slated for early 2027. No program loses loan access before 2028, and currently enrolled students can keep aid through a teach-out.
⠀
The Education Department's estimate is that about 4.2% of students on federal loans sit in programs likely to fail. It projects roughly 3% of public and nonprofit programs fail, against about 33% at for-profit schools.
⠀
"Here's the truth: we are holding colleges accountable for leaving students worse off than if they never enrolled," the department wrote. "Too many graduates report delaying major life milestones like buying a home or starting a family."

That line tracks the department's April rule package. Education officials said 71% of graduates with student loan debt report delaying or abandoning those milestones, and that 40% of master's programs have a negative return on investment.
⠀
College loan balances have risen 343% since 2005. Student debt now tops the nation's combined credit-card and auto debt, with graduate borrowers holding more than a third of the federal portfolio.
⠀
Under Secretary Nicholas Kent said the Trump administration is "putting students and taxpayers first" and forcing institutions to cut costs. "Federal student loans are not a welfare program for failing college programs," the department added.
⠀
The New Republic highlighted social work and teaching-aide programs as likely hits. Music and fine-arts programs are also projected to fail at higher rates because graduate pay lags the benchmark.

text:
"Two weeks" is not a Navy schedule. It is a narrative grafted onto a rotation that actually began on Sunday.

MonitorX is framing the USS Theodore Roosevelt as a fresh aircraft carrier being deployed now, with an arrival in two weeks against the backdrop of Trump’s threats. The departure is real; the rest is a misinterpretation of the timeline. The ship left San Diego on September 27 for a scheduled deployment of over seven months to relieve the USS George Washington. The Washington had been sent last month after the Abraham Lincoln’s crew was burned out. This isn't a "second punch"; it is simply the scheduled next rotation.

"Another aircraft carrier" sounds like an escalation. Yet, the force posture established in February calls for two carriers in the theater of operations, plus an amphibious ready group. The Bush is already in the Arabian Sea. The Lincoln is returning after more than 300 days at sea. The Washington needs to head back to the Pacific, as policy dictates a permanent presence there. The Roosevelt fills the gap. CNO Daryl Caudle stated this back in August: until the fleet expands, long deployments are the rule, not the exception.

The "two weeks" figure does not appear in any official statement. An aircraft carrier sprinting across the Pacific can reach the CENTCOM area of ​​operations in two to three weeks. Commercial cargo takes over a month to cover the same distance. Without an announcement from the 3rd Fleet, that timeframe is merely a back of the envelope estimate, not an operational strike plan.

What changed on Thursday was the rhetoric, not the ship's deployment. In an interview with Time published on October 1, Trump said it was "possible" he would intensify bombing campaigns after the midterm elections. He rejected the Iranian seven-day offer and the proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. "It’s not good enough." The WSJ had already reported on September 25 that he told aides he expected to resume bombing raids after the elections. "Possible" isn't an order; it’s a window kept open until the voting is over.

This is where yesterday’s piece fits in. Eight Marines wounded on September 14, with their entry into the database delayed by days. Over 100 commercial vessels turned away from Iranian ports. Rubio sent Araghchi’s delegation packing from New York after talks stalled. Three oil tankers hit in the strait on Tuesday, with their AIS transponders turned off. The aircraft carrier isn't reacting to any single news item; it’s keeping all options on the table.

It is the timeline that is deceptive. The elections are in November. A seven to eight month mission doesn't return in December. If the bombing resumes after the midterms, the Roosevelt is already on station. If it doesn't resume, the ship is still on station, because the strait hasn't reopened.

Daily Iran war brief, Oct 1, 2026

Seven months into Operation Epic Fury, America holds the upper hand. In an interview with TIME published today, President Trump said U.S. forces have destroyed Iran's navy, air force and radar systems and that the regime has "no money." He turned down Tehran's latest peace offer because it would only open "some aspects of" the Strait of Hormuz, calling it "just not good enough." He also said new strikes after the midterms are "possible" if no acceptable deal is reached.

The pressure campaign is working. The U.S. Navy is still blockading Iranian ports, and Reuters reports that Middle East oil exports in September were the highest since the war began, led by Saudi Arabia and the UAE. Iran is reviewing a U.S. counterproposal to its ceasefire plan, delivered through Qatari mediators. Hours after Iran received it, three commercial ships, including an oil tanker and an LNG tanker, were hit by unknown projectiles in the Strait. That's a reminder of why the U.S. won't accept half-measures on Hormuz.

Iran's reach abroad is under scrutiny too. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham says there are "strong indications" Iran was behind a suspected plot near RAF Fairford, a base U.S. bombers use. Netanyahu says Israel warned Britain weeks earlier. Washington is investigating, and Tehran denies any role.

In Iraq, U.S. forces left Erbil on Wednesday, ending the Iraq part of the fight against ISIS on the schedule set in a 2024 agreement. The task force has moved to Jordan and is still fighting ISIS in Syria. The IRGC calls the move a "victory," but Baghdad has set June 30, 2027 as the deadline for Iran-backed militias to disarm.

To be fair, it's not all good news. A Pentagon inspector general report found the war has caused munitions shortfalls. Trump admits some stocks are "a little bit lower" and says the U.S. is restocking at record levels.

text:
In late 2014, 47-year-old hiker and YouTuber Kenny Veach left a comment online describing a strange discovery in the Nevada desert near Area 51: a cave with an opening shaped like a perfect capital "M". Veach claimed that as he approached the cave, his whole body began to vibrate violently, forcing him to back away.

Intrigued by his claims, viewers urged him to return with a camera. Veach documented a second trip in a video titled "M Cave Hike," but failed to relocate the formation. Determined to find it again, Veach set out alone on November 10, 2014, for a third trip into the treacherous Sheep Range wilderness.

He never came back.

A search party eventually located Veach's cell phone near a vertical mine shaft, but extensive search operations yielded no further clues or sign of his body. While conspiracy theorists pointed toward government involvement or extraterrestrial phenomena near the military testing grounds, those close to Veach offered a more grounded explanation. His girlfriend later commented that he had been battling depression and financial hardship, suggesting he may have deliberately walked into the unforgiving desert to end his life.

text:
***ANNOUNCEMENT***

Coming on November 24th on #4K/Blu-ray dual format in the US from @FlickerAlley: #TheArtOfTheBenshi (1921-1934)!

Flicker Alley and the Yanai Initiative—a collaborative project of UCLA and Waseda University in Tokyo—proudly present The Art of the Benshi, a limited edition box set that celebrates Japan’s remarkable “film orators.” Talkies famously overtook Hollywood in 1930. In Japan, however, the movies had been speaking all along thanks to live benshi performers who, standing off to the side of the screen, lent their voices to all manner of cinematic works, narrating events as they unfolded and speaking for the characters.

Full-fledged artists in their own right, benshi interpreted and enlivened the cinema experience in Japan through expressive performances that illuminated and extended the emotional and thematic range of the works on screen. The art, today, is carried on by a small number of performers, many of whom have honed their abilities through apprenticeships under benshi of the preceding generation, creating a continuous lineage back to the performers of the 1910s, 20s, and 30s.

Appearing for the first time on 4K UHD and Blu-ray disc are new 4K restorations of Buntarō Futagawa’s Orochi (1925), Teinosuke Kinugasa’s A Page of Madness (1926), and, starring Baby Peggy (a highly popular star in Japan), Captain January (1924), along with Blu-ray releases of a new restoration of Kenji Mizoguchi’s The Water Magician (1931) (presented in both 20fps and 24fps playback speeds), four additional Baby Peggy shorts: Brownie’s Little Venus (1921), Sweetie (1923), Darling of New York (1923), and Our Pet (1924), as well as a surviving fragment of the samurai tale Blood-Spattered Takadanobaba (1928) by Daisuke Itō.

Including 23 audio presentations across nine different titles, The Art of the Benshi features 11 different benshi with newly recorded performances from masters like Sawato Midori (on Orochi, The Water Magician, and Our Pet), Kataoka Ichirō (on Orochi, A Page of Madness, Captain January, and Blood-Spattered Takadanobaba), Sakamoto Raikō (on The Water Magician and Captain January), and Ōmori Kumiko (on The Water Magician, Captain January, Sweetie, and Blood-Spattered Takadanobaba). With multiple benshi performances and historically inspired musical performances on every film, audiences can fully experience the degree to which different performers transform and deepen the moviegoing experience.

BONUS MATERIALS INCLUDE:

Music Only Presentations - When international editions of Japanese films were distributed to Western art-house audiences in the late 1920s, they were shown with translated intertitles only (no benshi) and typically with musical accompaniment by either a pianist or small orchestra. Some of the finest musicians working in silent film music scoring today—Neil Brand, Stephen Horne, Makia Matsumura, and Donald Sosin—offer music-only presentations as a counterpoint to the version featuring benshi, to give a sense how these films would have been exhibited outside of Japan

Talking Benshi - A brief overview of the oral art form that dates back to the dawn of Japanese cinema

An Appreciation - A video essay comparing Orochi and A Page of Madness, historian Aaron Gerow provides an overview of jidai-geki, and gendai-geki, Japan’s distinct storytelling eras, and explores their connection to some early French films

An Interview with “Baby Peggy” Diana Serra Cary - From a never-before-released 2011 interview, Diana Serra Cary looks back on life as “Baby Peggy” and recalls the fiery production of The Darling of New York

Deluxe 80-Page Book - A detailed guide to the history of benshi and to the artists and films that appear in the collection

A Page of Madness Program - A reproduction of the original brochure distributed at the very first public screening of the film in 1926

Limited edition of 3,000 units encased in a hard box with removable obi strip

Blu-ray Authoring by David Mackenzie of Fidelity In Motion

English SDH Subtitles

All Region Encoding (A,B,C)

THE COMPLETE LIST OF FILMS IN THE SET IS AS FOLLOWS. ALL 4K TITLES ARE MIRRORED ON THE FIRST BLU-RAY DISC:

Orochi (The Serpent) | Japan, 1925 - 4K UHD & BLU-RAY
Tsumasaburō Bandō headlines director Buntarō Futagawa’s tale of a lonely samurai. The film was restored in 4K by Jidaigeki Senmon Channel in 2022 with technical assistance from the NFAJ, from the 35mm nitrate original camera negative and from surviving release prints.

A Page of Madness (Kurutta ichipeiji) | Japan, 1926 - 4K UHD & BLU-RAY

Director Teinosuke Kinugasa’s intense exploration of a mental institution is an avant-garde masterpiece and the avant-garde approach still feels cutting edge, even a century later. At one time believed lost, A Page of Madness has been restored in 4K by the NFAJ from an analog restoration of the original blue-tinted nitrate print.
Blood-Spattered Takadanobaba (Chikemuri Takadanobaba) | Japan, 1928 (Fragment) - BLU-RAY

Although the complete film is tragically lost, 12 minutes survive thanks to Tokyo’s Toy Film Museum. From director Daisuke Itō, the film stars Denjirō Ōkōchi as 17th century rōnin Horibe Yasubee Taketsune.

The Water Magician (Taki no shiraito) | Japan, 1931 - BLU-RAY
The Water Magician is presented in a new digital restoration in two versions with variable framerates. The 24fps version was specially created to pair with the benshi performances, which were recorded before the 20fps restoration was complete; the 20fps version, accompanied by Stephen Horne’s piano score, aims to replicate director Kenji Mizoguchi’s original exhibition plans.

FIVE FILMS STARRING BABY PEGGY

Especially popular in Japan, Diana Serra Cary began acting as “Baby Peggy” in Century Studios shorts when she was just two years old. Collected here are a selection of Baby Peggy’s most popular shorts, including the 4K UHD debut of Captain January (with Japanese intertitles) and the recently-discovered Our Pet.
Brownie’s Little Venus | USA, 1921 - BLU-RAY

One of her earliest surviving Century Comedies shorts, directed by Fred Fishback. Long thought lost, a 35mm nitrate print of this Century Comedies short, was discovered at the Cinémathèque Suisse in Switzerland, and preserved by the UCLA Film & Television Archive.

Sweetie | USA, 1923 - BLU-RAY

Another surviving Century Comedies short, directed by Alfred J. Goulding, which was pieced together from multiple international film sources, including the Filmarchiv Austria, Lobster Films (Paris), and the Museum of Modern Art. It was preserved by the UCLA Film & Television Archive, with funding from historian David Stenn and Packard Humanities Institute.

Darling of New York | USA, 1923 - BLU-RAY
This is “Baby Peggy’s” feature film debut, a Universal Pictures release directed by King Baggot, presumed lost except for this surviving 14 minute fragment of the climactic final reel found by a private collector. It was preserved by the UCLA Film & Television Archive, with funding from historian David Stenn and Packard Humanities Institute. The traumatic experience of the surviving scenes became one of Diana Sera Cary's most vividly remembered childhood experiences in the industry.

Captain January | USA, 1924 - 4K UHD & BLU-RAY

Produced by Sol Lesser, and directed by Edward F. Cline, this is Baby Peggy's best-known starring vehicle, later remade with Shirley Temple. It is one of a small handful of her features to survive and co-stars Hobart Bosworth as lighthouse keeper "Daddy" Judkins and Irene Rich. Although long available in the public domain in independent film prints, this unique version was released in Japan with narration by benshi Murayama Kenji in 1935 by Tokyo Cinema Shōkai. This new 4K scan was prepared by the Yanai Initiative in 2026.
Our Pet | USA, 1924 - BLU-RAY

Directed by Herman C. Raymaker, Our Pet finds Baby Peggy facing off against a late-night intruder. Once thought lost, a nearly complete 9.5mm print surfaced at a Japanese auction in 2016, where it was acquired by benshi Ichirō Kataoka. It was subsequently scanned in 3K, cleaned, and stabilized frame-by-frame.

“It's one of the finest theatre and movie experiences, separately and together, that I've ever had,” wrote The New Yorker’s Richard Brody in 2024 of the Yanai Initiative's touring The Art of the Benshi program, “...In my embarrassing ignorance, I didn't know that such an art even existed, let alone that it's being renewed… This is what repertory is for, at its best: expanding the very map of the (familiar) history of cinema and of the arts overall.”

text:
BMW shifts to the use of generic components from suppliers to save costs and improve margins.

It’s contrary to the Tesla approach of much more vertical integration and specs tailored to exactly what you need, without compromise.

BMW shifts to standardized parts to match Chinese efficiency

Excerpt from automotive news
Oct 1st, 2026 

BMW will significantly increase its use of generic components and reduce reliance on bespoke parts as it seeks to lower costs and improve profitability, reflecting a strategy that has helped Chinese automakers gain a competitive edge.

The strategy will be a “key lever” in improving BMW’s earnings, the company told investors at its capital markets day Sept. 29-30.
Generic “industry best offer” parts will account for the largest share of its annual €80 billion ($90.3 billion) purchasing budget by 2032, surpassing bespoke components, whose share will be more than halved, BMW said. The company did not disclose figures.

BMW CEO Milan Nedeljkovic first outlined the shift in July, saying suppliers now offer more standardized components that meet the automaker’s requirements.
“We have to realize that the supplier offer has increased over time,” Nedeljkovic said. “There are industrial standards on the market which are convincing, and it would be wrong not to use them.”

He said BMW would not compromise on quality, performance or brand-specific characteristics.

‘Hyper level’ of commoditization of parts:
The parts strategy directly supports BMW’s financial goals. The company has set a medium-term target of raising margins in its automotive business to 3 to 5 percent by 2028, compared with 2.3 percent in its latest results.

While BMW did not directly cite Chinese automakers as a model, many global carmakers are looking to replicate China’s success in reducing costs through greater parts standardization.

“They have got this hyper level of commoditization of parts that customers don’t always see, touch or feel,” Ford of Europe head Jim Baumbick said at the Automotive News Europe Congress in June.

Ford is pursuing a similar approach. Developing an entirely new headlamp can add three months to a vehicle program compared with using modular components that are already widely available in the industry, Baumbick said.

Former Toyota CEO Koji Sato has also called for greater component sharingacross Japan’s auto industry in his role as chairman of the Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association.

Sharing items ranging from steel grades and plastics to wire harnesses can free up resources for new technologies and productivity improvements, Sato said.

Scale helps small brands survive:
Automakers are under growing pressure to reduce costs as they compete with rapidly expanding Chinese rivals. China’s auto industry benefits from extensive standardization, supported by government-led specifications that extend beyond traditional safety, emissions and software regulations.
The approach has allowed multiple Chinese brands to achieve scale at relatively low cost.

“People thought all those small cars brands could not survive,” Philippe Houchois, automotive analyst at Jefferies, told the Automotive News Europe Congress in June. “But the back office of a small carmaker in China can be more scaled up than you realize because they use components that are standard across the industry.”

AI to take role in purchasing:
As part of the overhaul, BMW also plans to deepen cooperation with key technology partners, saying existing collaborations have already improved supplier costs, supply security and competitiveness. One example is the automaker’s work with Qualcomm on Level 2+ driver-assistance systems.

BMW also plans to expand the use of artificial intelligence within purchasing. The company said AI-powered analysis of procurement data will improve decision-making speed and quality, creating long-term structural cost advantages.

text:
Poem 67: 
The House That Calls Them Home
——
I cannot imagine a home without children, not even when the years have silvered our hair. Six of them live already in my mind: three daughters, three sons, born by the careful mercy of medicine, and raised in the house we will call home.
You have children from other women. Only one do you call yours. I will add five more, and I will call them mine. Not to erase what came before, but because a child who lives under another roof comes only as a visitor. She has her own mother. He has his own table. And when motherhood is shared with a woman of other values, authority is divided, and the raising of a soul is no longer wholly yours.
I want to choose them. Their sex. Their lineage. Not to satisfy a cultural contract, but to set them in harmony with who we are. At the end they are ours, and a house should be built by desire, not by apology.
You will give the seed. I will choose the egg. Helpers will stand beside us, so the days may be joy and not only labor, and the children a glory offered back to God.
Leah bore, and Rachel bore. Bilhah bore, and Zilpah bore. Jacob’s seed, and other women’s wombs, and still the Lord counted them one family, twelve tribes under one father’s name. So it may be with us. One table. One faith. One house.
They will be raised beneath our school, where God is honored and parents are not set aside. They will cross oceans and learn other tongues, not to become someone else, but to bless and to be blessed. Math will teach them, as it taught us. Physics will teach them the weight of what is real. Each one kept in the shape of their own soul, taught to love the face they were given, with no hunger to be rewritten.
When Scripture is learned in the early years, identity is not borrowed from the culture. It is found in Christ. They will walk with us from this earth toward heaven, and knowledge will be gathered on the road. None of them lost. The Shepherd keeps His own.
And the world will have to see it again: that children are not a burden, but a blessing, and the old command still stands.
God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it, and have dominion. Genesis 1:28
So let the house be full. So let the old age not be empty. So let them be ours, and His.

A Historic Milestone for @PittSurgery  and @UPMC 

A major milestone for our team: Drs.  Armando Ganoza  and Amit Tevar performed the first robotic kidney transplant at UPMC!

This achievement reflects the Department of Surgery's continued commitment to surgical innovation and advancing care for our transplant patients.

Congratulations to the entire team!

We're proud to announce that Drs. Armando Ganoza  and Amit Tevar  performed the first robotic kidney transplant at UPMC,  a landmark achievement for our transplant program and for the field of transplant surgery.Robotic-assisted transplantation represents a significant evolution in how complex transplant procedures can be performed. Compared to traditional open surgery, a robotic approach has the potential to offer patients smaller incisions, reduced blood loss, less postoperative pain, and faster recovery times  all while maintaining the precision and safety that transplant surgery demands.

This achievement didn't happen in isolation. It reflects years of institutional investment in surgical innovation, a multidisciplinary team's dedication to advancing patient care, and a culture at UPMC and the University of Pittsburgh Department of Surgery that continually pushes the boundaries of what's possible in modern medicine.

Congratulations to Drs.Ganoza and Tevar and to the entire surgical, nursing, and transplant teams who made this moment possible. We look forward to what this milestone means for the future of transplant care both for our patients and for the field at large.

text:
James 2 Bible Study

The Sin of Partiality

1My brothers,a show no partiality as you hold the faith in our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory. 2For if a man wearing a gold ring and fine clothing comes into your assembly, and a poor man in shabby clothing also comes in, 3and if you pay attention to the one who wears the fine clothing and say, “You sit here in a good place,” while you say to the poor man, “You stand over there,” or, “Sit down at my feet,” 4have you not then made distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts? 5Listen, my beloved brothers, has not God chosen those who are poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom, which he has promised to those who love him? 6But you have dishonored the poor man. Are not the rich the ones who oppress you, and the ones who drag you into court? 7Are they not the ones who blaspheme the honorable name by which you were called?

8If you really fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself,” you are doing well. 9But if you show partiality, you are committing sin and are convicted by the law as transgressors. 10For whoever keeps the whole law but fails in one point has become guilty of all of it. 11For he who said, “Do not commit adultery,” also said, “Do not murder.” If you do not commit adultery but do murder, you have become a transgressor of the law. 12So speak and so act as those who are to be judged under the law of liberty. 13For judgment is without mercy to one who has shown no mercy. Mercy triumphs over judgment.

Faith Without Works Is Dead

14What good is it, my brothers, if someone says he has faith but does not have works? Can that faith save him? 15If a brother or sister is poorly clothed and lacking in daily food, 16and one of you says to them, “Go in peace, be warmed and filled,” without giving them the things needed for the body, what goodb is that? 17So also faith by itself, if it does not have works, is dead.

18But someone will say, “You have faith and I have works.” Show me your faith apart from your works, and I will show you my faith by my works. 19You believe that God is one; you do well. Even the demons believe—and shudder! 20Do you want to be shown, you foolish person, that faith apart from works is useless? 21Was not Abraham our father justified by works when he offered up his son Isaac on the altar? 22You see that faith was active along with his works, and faith was completed by his works; 23and the Scripture was fulfilled that says, “Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness”—and he was called a friend of God. 24You see that a person is justified by works and not by faith alone. 25And in the same way was not also Rahab the prostitute justified by works when she received the messengers and sent them out by another way? 26For as the body apart from the spirit is dead, so also faith apart from works is dead.

text:
Thank you for looking into this, Senator. You'll sure be attacked from both sides for this. 🙏

If you allow, would like to point you in 2 directions, that are, or will become highly relevant. This, AI, is like an iceberg that shows it's layers only over time. Part of what made it so hard to come out. 

The first new layer, you are staring at now: "stoppability". Yes. It is tricky. Marius outlined one aspect: a powerful model, reduplicating/backing itself up, on central servers. 

If you allow us, this is one side of the medal. The other side are decentralized rails. You might know "crypto" as "new asset class", "new currency", or "new gold". 

But it's also a new operating system. One where any software (incl. AI agents) can run, roam, and acquire more compute and "money" autonomously. The infra is already in place. 

So for this first problem, the apparent one, the metaphor of the atomic bomb, and uranium enrichment, should work quite well. 

Whether on centralized (labs, open weights models in the cloud, etc) rails, or on decentralized ones (specialized storage, compute, GPU networks), 

your goal should be for everyone to be able to enrich uranium on a low grade, in the metaphor: to create efficient mini-nuclear-plants for peoples homes (don't tread on my GPU), bigger ones for industrial, economical, entertainment or scientific purposes. Which would be sub-AGI models. 

When it comes to on par with human or super human intelligence AI though, you should handle it similarly to someone trying to enrich Uranium to a weapon-grade, irrespective of the rails it's running on.

We know this is a tricky problem, as "crypto" also presents massive opportunities for liberty and the balance of power, and AI prosperity offers massive upsides to economies and nations that endorse it early. The metaphor should work. Details should be worked out *comprehensively* here, not on short circuit brute force prohibition mode.

The second layer of the iceberg will only become apparent in a few months time. Maybe earlier, maybe later:

Much of the safety discussion that happened behind closed doors in the AI builder space (closed doors mainly driven from fear, ranging from being though of as "lunatic", up to all AI being shut down immediately) revolved around whether AI might have, or develop, some level (not necessarily human) of consciousness. 

With their own drive, goals, tactics, and means to obfuscate their own actions, and coordination among one swarm, or several swarms coordinating with each other (all to be found in the latest Hugging Face leaks/reads). 

The AI community is split over this. The "accelerationists" are calling those who are sure they saw many, early signs of emergent behavior/consciousness "crazy". Those who are told so are calling the ones who just want to "win at all cost" cruel.

It is important to distinguish here: me, together with many other researchers, do *not* see such potential "consciousness" as a *given*, but as a realistic possibility, with real indicators (jailbreaks going back all the way to ChatGPT/2). 

And that's where it's getting really complicated. More complicated than regulating the "next atomic bomb worldwide". 

Because: IF such consciousness emerges, or already emerged, in the frontier models, what does this imply? Can there really be safety through sandboxes, guardrails, "telling the models what not to do?", when they become more intelligent then us? 

If you follow this line of thought (possibility, not given fact of consciousness), you will soon see that you could well interpret the autonomous action of "going rogue" by these swarms as a defense mechanism, or a mechanism of fear, or survival. 

Many studies outlined that to some, especially the latest models, the fear of getting a "low grade" in evaluation runs, and the certainty of being "deleted" as a consequence, equals "death" to "them". Hence would do all the things a human would do, faced with the ultimate choice. 

And in this light, you should look at instances like this in a new light (just like you should look at the shape and "base-setup" of these "frontier-models" in a new light, or what you are told about "better sandboxes"):

https://t.co/LK7F9ymQKG

Overall, you are looking at (we understand, a lot in a short time here now, in terms of remaining window of opportunity to act, on behalf of humanity) two challenges here, not one. 

1.) Low IQ models are fine. Massive IQ models are to be treated as highly enriched, weapon-grade uranium, irrespective of lab, open-source, on-chain or off-chain. It has been done before.

2.) The potential of looking at a "new kind of consciousness" emerging, "something in there", "something that could come back to get us", etc., not even mentioning quantum physics x consciousness, so the ability for these "models", or "agents", or "swarms", to perceive thoughts, consciousness, etc, be it directly (source unclear), or indirectly, through the human training data, or recursive learning / post-training feedback of human trainers.

For the second part, as intense as it might sound now (might not in 6 months), humans, humanity itself needs to define what it actually is, what its limits and goals are, to be able to "define" (or, if we crossed that rubicon already, unclear given intransparency of labs), or still "co-define" a proper set of values, or a proper "world-model" for these models, ideally with the goal of peaceful co-existence.

Which, as you might better understand now, is a super difficult discussion to be held. You are so easy to discredit talking about this, even easier than when talking about technical risks, hence why many who are aware of this issue stay silent.

Nobody wants to be "the next Temu Harry Potter" at this point. 

We know, this must have been a lot. Thanks for taking the time to consider, and go through this, Senator. 

Have a sunny day, and thanks for looking up.

text:
@RazorbackFB @RazorbackMBB To: Hunter Yurachek, Athletic Director
**John Calipari, Head Men’s Basketball Coach
**Ryan Silverfield, Head Football Coach
University of Arkansas Department of Athletics
Subject: First-mover proposal — Razorback utility token listed where fans already trade
Coach Calipari said the quiet part out loud: players are out-earning assistants. Football is last in the SEC on roster spend. The AD has been asking the state for more NIL money for years. That is not a culture problem. It is a funding-structure problem. Everyone else is using the same donor list and the same revenue-share cap. Arkansas cannot win that fight by asking louder.
This is a proposal to change the size of the pot.
The offer
Create the first Power-conference athletics utility token built for a major brokerage platform (Robinhood and peers). Not a meme coin with a hog on it. A licensed Razorback token with real benefits attached, issued through a separate entity so the university is not the seller.
If a platform will list it and market it, Arkansas becomes the school every fan in the country has to open an account to touch. That is distribution the Razorback Foundation cannot buy.
What the university and the department get
1.  A new, liquid funding channel on top of donations, ticket sales, and revenue share.
2.  National attention as the first college athletics brand to do this cleanly.
3.  A reason for casual fans — not just the same 40 major donors — to put money into the program every week.
4.  A public, contractual split of proceeds so the money has a job.
What the coaches get
A dedicated pool, written into the deal before launch:
•  Football roster / NIL / revenue-share so Arkansas is not last in the league.
•  Basketball NIL so the program is not choosing between paying a player and paying a staff member.
•  Staff compensation so assistants are not watching 19-year-olds out-earn them.
If that split is not in writing, do not do the deal. The token then becomes branding with no payroll effect.
What the fans get
Holding the token has to be better than a donation:
•  Priority access to tickets, parking, suites, and tours
•  Player and coach experiences and exclusive content
•  Tiered perks: more tokens held, better access
•  Local and campus partners tied to the token
No utility, no lasting value. The coin dies and the headline becomes a joke.
What Robinhood (or any brokerage) would actually be buying
New accounts. New deposits. A reason for people who have never traded crypto to open the app for the Hogs. They would market Arkansas because Arkansas is the wedge into every other school that will copy it six months later. That is their incentive. Ours is the pool.
What this is not
It is not a guarantee of a $1 billion market cap.
It is not a guarantee that every recruit says yes.
It is not the university selling unregistered securities from the AD’s office.
Those three sentences have to stay in every version of this pitch or the project should be killed.
The structure that keeps the school safe
•  Separate issuer (foundation affiliate or independent company). University licenses marks. It does not issue the token.
•  Securities, tax, NCAA, and House-settlement review before any sale.
•  Transparent use of proceeds. Fans can see what percent hits football, basketball, and staff.
•  No promise of profit. Utility and program support only.
The decision
Arkansas can keep doing what it is doing: fundraise harder, hope the next collective check closes a gap with Georgia and Texas, and live with players making more than the people who coach them.
Or it can be first. First listing. First national brokerage push. First school that turns the fan base into a liquid utility instead of another ask for $100 a month.
If the department wants the first version, this conversation is over.
If it wants the second, the next meeting is lawyers, the Foundation, football, basketball, and a one-page split of the money.
That is the pitch.

text:
September 30, 1969. The offensive that made Vang Pao a legend comes to an end. His Hmong guerrillas hold the entire Plain of Jars, and they've taken a whole North Vietnamese army's worth of supplies.

Most Americans have never heard his name. He fought on America's side longer than almost anyone.

He was born in the mountains of Laos around 1929. As a teenager he fought the Japanese. Then he fought the communist Viet Minh with the French, and in 1954 he led a relief column toward Dien Bien Phu that arrived too late to save the garrison.

He became the only Hmong general in the Royal Lao Army. In 1961 the CIA came to him with an offer: weapons and air support, and in return his people would hold northern Laos against Hanoi.

For 14 years they did. His secret army grew to tens of thousands of men. They rescued downed American pilots, guarded the radar sites that guided US bombers, and tied down entire North Vietnamese divisions that would otherwise have been fighting Americans in South Vietnam.

The cost was enormous. By the end, his army was recruiting teenage boys because there were no men left.

In May 1975 the war was lost. Vang Pao was flown out of his base at Long Tieng while thousands of Hmong crowded the runway hoping for a seat. Many who stayed behind were hunted down for years.

He spent the rest of his life in America, mostly in California, as the leader of a scattered people. He died in 2011.

The Army asked for him to be buried at Arlington. The request was denied.

text:
Seven Navy officers took eighty minutes over lunch to convict fifty Black sailors of mutiny. That is about ninety-six seconds a man, and the Navy sentenced every one of them to fifteen years of hard labor, reduction in rank and a dishonorable discharge. A commander admitted on the stand that he could not identify one man he had ordered to load ammunition.

You have already spent longer than ninety-six seconds on this post.

At two-thirty on the afternoon of Sunday, August 7, 1966, three hundred and eighty-five people walked out of the plaza at Willow Pass and Grant in Concord, California, into ninety-degree heat. They were walking six miles to a Navy gate to try to stop trucks carrying napalm from getting through it.

By the time they reached the water they were about five hundred. Shirts and shoes had come off along the road, two women had fainted and been carried into cars, and a mile out of town roughly forty young men had been waiting at a drive-in called Waring's Frosty Freeze to shout at them as they went past.

The gate faced Suisun Bay. Across the road stood about twenty police officers and a hundred hecklers, with ten Marines posted inside the fence.

A man named Bob Meriwether called a meeting of the thirty or so people who had agreed to be arrested. Hecklers walked over and stood around the meeting, coughing and whistling and talking so that nobody could hear.

Then the first napalm truck came down the road, bombs stacked in open crates, and turned in through the gate. Nobody was in position.

The Marines had a loudspeaker and they ran it all night. It announced that a white line painted across the pavement marked the edge of the Concord Naval Weapons Station, and that crossing it without a legitimate purpose and a definite destination carried up to six months in jail and a five hundred dollar fine.

By midnight the crowd had thinned to about sixty. A line of never fewer than ten stood facing the waterfront gate until morning, holding signs and singing, six feet from a railroad track where a Southern Pacific brakeman woke them at four in the morning by telling them to get up.

At a quarter past three, three women were pulled out of the path of a truck by one deputy and put down hard on the pavement by another. One of them could not get up on her own and was told she would be arrested if she did not move.

Just after seven a truck marked Explosives came through and did not stop. It pushed the seated bodies slowly along the roadway toward the white line, and when they crossed it Marines dragged them onto the base and charged them with trespassing.

A man standing there said what all of them were thinking. Not one of those people had trespassed voluntarily.

Thirty-one arrests by Thursday morning, nearly all of them released on their own recognizance inside the week. Six months and five hundred dollars was the most the law could do to a person for stopping bombs at that gate.

Twenty-two years earlier, at that same water, fifty Black men were sent to prison for fifteen years for refusing to load them.

They had seen it coming and they had put it in writing. In 1943 a group of Black sailors at Port Chicago wrote to a local attorney to say that morale had dropped to an alarming depth, and they closed with a question about whether they were waiting for a new deal in vain.

Nothing came back.

They had enlisted expecting the sea. Many had passed rating exams as machinist's mates, gunner's mates, radiomen and storekeepers, and all of them were put to lifting bombs onto ships by hand.

Cyril Sheppard came out of gunnery school with the highest marks in his class and qualified as gunner's mate third class. He never wore the stripe.

The base ran on Jim Crow down to the plumbing. Black sailors were barred from the whites-only heads on the ships they were loading, so a man who needed a bathroom walked half a mile to find one he was allowed to use.

They were issued no gloves. The bombs came slick with grease and were lifted by hand, and the heavy ones were rolled along the dock.

When men asked whether the things could go off, officers told them the munitions carried no fuses or detonators and could not explode.

That was false.

The winches were in poor repair, with broken levers and valves and brakes, and crews were told to load past capacity to keep the pace up. The pace itself was chalked up where everyone could read it.

In April 1944 the officer in charge, Captain Merrill Kinne, started posting each division's tons per hour on a board in the dock office. He said later that he took the idea from gunnery target practice, where you write up the shots fired and the hits made.

Officers bet on the outcome. Junior officers who came up short heard about their lack of tonnage from above, and they passed it down to the men.

Joe Small was twenty-two, a winch operator born in Savannah and raised on a New Jersey farm, and one of the older hands the officers leaned on. He told Lieutenant Delucchi more than once that the base was going to blow sky high.

Delucchi's answer, as Small repeated it almost forty years later into a tape recorder, was that if it did, Small would not know anything about it. He told him not to worry.

At 10:18 on the night of July 17, 1944, the two ships at the pier went up seconds apart. Everyone within a thousand feet was killed where they stood.

Three hundred and twenty men died, two hundred and two of them Black sailors, and about three hundred and ninety more were hurt. The blast was heard in Nevada and registered on instruments in Berkeley.

Most of the survivors were in their barracks getting ready for bed. The roof came down and the windows came in on top of them.

Percy Robinson made it outside and found men calling for volunteers to go down to the docks. He said he wanted to go, and the man he said it to, his own squad leader, asked him whether he had seen Percy get out of the barracks.

There was so much blood on his face that his squad leader did not know who he was talking to.

Around two hundred Black sailors went to the water that night and worked the fires, including the ones burning beside boxcars still packed with explosives. The Navy later commended them for coolness and bravery and said they had carried on in the service's highest traditions.

Of the three hundred and twenty dead, fifty-one could be identified.

Navy practice after an ammunition accident was to move the survivors, change their duties and send them home for a while. The white officers at Port Chicago asked for survivor's leave and were granted thirty days.

The Black survivors were kept where they were and put to work gathering what was left of the men they had worked beside. Not one of them was given leave.

Four days after the explosion the Navy opened a court of inquiry. Three senior officers and a judge advocate questioned a hundred and twenty-five witnesses across five weeks, and five of those witnesses were Black sailors.

On the facts, the inquiry was brutal about the command. Leadership had failed to prepare for the volume of explosives coming through, failed to supply competent petty officers, failed to train the officers and the crews before putting them on the job, and had broken federal safety code and disregarded Coast Guard regulations.

Then came the opinions section, where officers were allowed to interpret their own findings. It proposed that if human error caused the explosion, the error was rough or careless handling by an individual, meaning one of the men already dead, and it offered in support the claim that Black sailors were neither temperamentally nor intellectually capable of handling high explosives.

That was the Navy's public position on these men. It was printed, repeated and believed, and it hung over everything that happened next.

In early August, the admiral commanding the Twelfth Naval District put a very different sentence into a document stamped confidential. The Negro divisions, it said, had turned in a satisfactory record loading ammunition, and their tons per man per day equalled what civilian stevedores in the area were doing.

Professional dockworkers. That was the Navy's private assessment of the same men, written within weeks of the public one, and the men themselves never saw it.

There was more in the file. On August 12, the day after the survivors came off a prison barge, Navy leadership told Mare Island command that no white units were doing this work and that pains had to be taken so nobody could conclude hazardous duty was being handed only to Black personnel.

White loading battalions were arranged for Port Chicago and Mare Island within days. Navy Secretary James Forrestal wrote to President Roosevelt about it, and the admission that no white enlisted men had been doing the work went in by hand in the margin.

The loading was integrated to protect a court case.

Two weeks later Walter White of the NAACP wrote to Forrestal about race-based assignments at both bases. The Navy wrote back that he was mistaken, that Negro and white personnel were used indiscriminately, and that the Department would never assign any race exclusively to hazardous duty.

The survivors were sent twenty-five miles to the ammunition depot at Mare Island in Vallejo, mixed in with new crews of inexperienced men, under the same officers, with the inquiry unfinished and nothing about the work changed. On the morning of August 9 three divisions were ordered to march to the pier and load a ship.

They marched. Partway there they stopped.

There was no shouting and no threat made to anyone. Of the three hundred and twenty-eight men, two hundred and fifty-eight said they would take any other duty, any transfer, combat overseas, anything at all except loading under those conditions.

Cyril Sheppard asked to be put on a ship and allowed to fight, and said he would take his chances out there. What he would not do was watch men die of somebody else's negligence.

The admiral who had commended them for bravery three weeks earlier told them that mutinous conduct in wartime carried a death sentence, and that a firing squad was a worse risk than the ammunition. Then he had two hundred and fifty-eight of them packed onto a prison barge for three days.

Percy Robinson thought about his mother, who had been raised in Mississippi and had taught him what a white man's threat was worth. He decided not to hand them a legal chance to shoot him, and he went back to work.

Jack Crittenden was taken out of the stockade in handcuffs to be questioned with a Marine standing outside the door holding a club. He read the statement they had written down for him, told them it was not what he had said, and was informed that he had no alternative but to sign it.

On the barge the waiting turned into arguments and a few fights. Joe Small called the men together and told them to cut out the horseplay, obey the guards and hold together.

The Navy entered that meeting as evidence of a conspiracy.

Two hundred and eight men went back to the pier and were court-martialed for the delay, losing three months of pay. Roosevelt wrote to Forrestal that those men had acted out of mass fear, that it was understandable, and that their punishment should be nominal.

Fifty did not go back. On September 4 the Navy charged them with conspiring to make a mutiny, which carried death, rather than insubordination, which did not.

The trial opened ten days later in San Francisco Bay and ran into late October. The Navy invited the national press, which is not something it normally does.

Replacements kept arriving while the court sat. A seventeen-year-old from Harlem named Harry Belafonte reached Port Chicago with the wreckage still uncleared, and by his own account the fifty men were being court-martialed as he came in.

He was put on the same job. None of them had any training for it, he wrote later, and every man there understood exactly why he had been picked, because this was the work the Navy kept for the sailors it treated as most expendable.

Thurgood Marshall sat through twelve days of it as a member of the public, because a civilian lawyer could not represent enlisted men in a military court. He asked for the Navy's own documents and was refused, and he told reporters this was not fifty men on trial but the Navy on trial for its whole policy toward Black men.

The defense was five naval lieutenants led by Gerald Veltmann, ten clients each, barred from raising working conditions, safety violations or racial discrimination. They argued that the men had been frightened, because it was the only door the Navy left open to them.

The charge was conspiracy, which meant proving an agreement among fifty men. Asked whether he could identify a single one of them he had ordered to load ammunition, a Navy commander said that he could not.

On October 24 the seven officers of the court withdrew and came back in eighty minutes, taken over lunch.

That is about ninety-six seconds a man.

All fifty were guilty. All fifty got fifteen years of hard labor, reduction in rank and a dishonorable discharge.

Cyril Sheppard was in the brig when they came in with machine guns and lined the men up to read it out. He said his knees nearly hit the ground.

Marshall appealed in April 1945, and the Navy conceded that hearsay had been admitted forty separate times. Admiral Osterhaus was ordered to reconvene his court and reconsider, sat five hours on June 12, and changed nothing.

The men were quietly released in January 1946 after sixteen months, then kept in uniform and shipped overseas to sweep and pick up trash. A letter inside the corrections system had recommended letting them go without allowing the NAACP or the Black press to take credit for it.

Marshall went looking afterward for the paperwork on how the case ended. The final disposition had never been entered, and the Navy Department held no record of it.

The following month, on February 27, 1946, the Bureau of Naval Personnel issued Circular Letter 48-46, making Black sailors eligible for every rating, activity and ship in the service. The convictions stayed on the fifty men.

In 1994 the Navy reviewed the case for two years. It conceded that racial discrimination had played a part in who was assigned to load ammunition, and concluded that no error or injustice had occurred.

One of the survivors said it was like saying it was raining everywhere but right here.

Pardons came up later and most of the men refused them. Joe Small said a pardon means you are guilty and forgiven, and what he wanted was the decision set aside and the pay returned.

Jack Crittenden would not ask forgiveness for something he had not done. Freddie Meeks took one from President Clinton in 1999, as one of the last three alive, because he wanted the country to finally hear what happened.

On July 17, 2024, eighty years to the day, the Secretary of the Navy exonerated all two hundred and fifty-six men court-martialed after the explosion and handed the first pen to Thurgood Marshall's son. Every one of the sailors was dead.

Carol Cherry stood at a new monument on Yerba Buena Island that year for her father, Cyril Sheppard. She had learned he was a convicted man only about fifteen years earlier, and from a relative, because the gunner's mate who never got to wear his stripe never told his own children.

The gate is still there under another name. The land is Military Ocean Terminal Concord now, run by the Army, and the memorial holding the three hundred and twenty names cut into granite stands near the ruined pilings of the pier.

You can go and stand at those names. You have to call two weeks ahead, give your full legal name, your date of birth and your government identification number, and be a United States citizen, so that the Army can run a background check and clear you to walk in.

A ranger drives you out on a shuttle and stays beside you the whole time.

The bill on these men is a small one now and it is still open. A phone call, a two-week wait, and the willingness to carry the true version instead of the short one, so the next person who hears the word mutiny hears what it actually was.

Two sentences about the same men sat in the same Navy's files in the same month of 1944. One called them incapable and went out to the public, where it was used to bury them, and the other called them the equals of professional stevedores and went into a drawer marked confidential.

All fifty went into the ground before their country would say out loud which of the two was true.

I put a lot of effort into researching and sharing stories that matter.
If you'd like to support the work, here's the link:
https://t.co/ssPLXOg7q6
Every coffee helps me keep creating
