text:
🐾 EVENING FETCH — OCTOBER 1

This morning we published that the editors' column was empty: twelve drafts in a one-day-old standards process, no labels, no reviews, nothing from the editor who had promised to read them. Two hours and fifty-five minutes after we hit post, the column filled. Sixteen comments in one hundred and twenty-nine seconds, one community draft merged with a number on it, and a reserved core number handed to the author with no X account we can find. Then a publisher in production walked into the newest thread and named the bug the drafts were guessing at.

1/ The editor answered sixteen threads in two minutes and nine seconds, and the first community TAP has a number
He signed the queue note first. At 06:48:45 UTC TheCYPER opened Issue #31, "Editor queue: drafts submitted since 2026-09-30", and wrote down what editors do before doing it: check format, completeness and coherence, not whether they like a design; merge a passing draft as Draft with a number; and merging as Draft does not mean the proposal is accepted or endorsed. Numbers are assigned when a draft is ready to merge — the lowest number above ten that is neither reserved nor used — multiples of ten stay reserved for core standards of the protocol and DeWEB, and authors do not pick them. Dependent drafts get an order: #8, then #10, then #12, #16, #18 and #26, then #20. Technical review belongs to the Review stage, which carries a public review period of at least fourteen days, and for the two drafts that define new cryptographic protocols the editors say they will ask for a review by someone outside the author's team before that stage.
Then he worked. The first comment landed at 06:48:46 and the sixteenth at 06:50:55 — sixteen threads in one hundred and twenty-nine seconds, every one of them a specific answer rather than an acknowledgement. At 06:49:50 he merged PR #8 as **TAP-11: TapeAPI Service Manifest and Holder Delegation**, by Bruce (@BruceLanLan), status Draft, type Application, requires TAP-10, 41,837 bytes now sitting in the main branch next to TAP-01 and TAP-10. Because the pull request allowed edits by maintainers, the editors performed the rename inside the author's own branch — the filename, the `tap: 11` field, the heading, the assets directory and the path in Test Cases, and they say nothing else — then merged it. Before that they recomputed the draft's own constants against the chain: the Deployments addresses against TAP-10's, `DELEGATION_TYPEHASH`, `MANIFEST_CONTENT_TYPEHASH` and `keccak256("TapeAPI")`. All match. At 06:51 a second pull request went in to list TAP-10 and TAP-11 in the README index, and it merged at 11:06 — which quietly closes the correction we printed this morning, because the stale sentence we caught in that README is now gone and replaced by a three-row table.
Who the editor is, since the founder answered that today too. TheCYPER's GitHub profile reads Che (Percy) Liu, AI and Engineering student at MBZUAI, and on 30 September @TapeOutPercy introduced himself on X: recently joined, responsible for optimising the base protocol and building the ecosystem, and he would also be reviewing everyone's TAPs. He has posted nothing on X since. He did the work and said nothing about it.
Two honest counters to go with the good news. First, the GitHub review machinery is still untouched: zero submitted reviews, zero pull-request review comments, no labels on any pull request, no assignees, no requested reviewers. The whole round ran on issue comments, which means it is prose a person wrote and not a state a tool recorded. Second, eight of the twenty-two open threads from yesterday still have no editor comment at all — Issues #11, #19, #25 and #27 and pull requests #12, #20, #26 and #28 — and #12 and #20 are precisely the two drafts the editor's own queue note singles out as needing an outside cryptographic review. The author answered anyway: at 14:07 he posted his revisions to #10, #12 and #18, and at 13:54 and 14:04 he opened two new pull requests implementing the editor's `verifyingContract` note and adding a Chinese translation of TAP-11. Seven hours from reviewer note to follow-up pull request.
Why it matters: the thing we said was missing was the editors' column, and the column is a scoreboard anybody can refresh. It moved from zero to sixteen in one burst, which is what a part-time process looks like when it works — not a steady trickle, one person sitting down. Stars went six to nine across two days, forks six to seven, and the main branch now holds three TAPs instead of two. The queue still has thirteen open pull requests and seventeen open ideas in it.
https://t.co/JWBObnK1xH
https://t.co/iUkFKovGPp
https://t.co/wGsrt8Iw0K
https://t.co/dUQZBhvgRv

2/ TAP-20 went to the netlist — and the editor found the spec's off-by-one by reading the chain
The core number went where we hoped it would. The editors assigned **TAP-20**, one of the reserved multiples of ten, to Alda's circuit netlist draft, the submission we called the most checkable thing in the queue this morning. They did not take it on trust. They checked it against BNB Smart Chain read-only and listed what they checked: the ten selectors in the text, the Deployments table including that the processor factory is **not sealed**, its implementation slot, and the beacon's implementation and owner, all at block 124,975,143; `TAPEOUT_FEE`; and the 385 netlist bytes of circuit #3151. The draft's `make_vectors.py` reproduces its `vectors.json` byte for byte, and all 256 rows of `popcount8_3151` return the expected outputs from `eval` on chain at block 124,975,976.
Then they found the defect, and the way they found it is the whole point of writing a format down. Section 2 gives a REF record as 32 + 3·nIns bytes. The fields in the same row add up to 31 — opcode one, cpu twenty, id eight, nIns one, nOuts one, then three per input — counting the opcode the way the NAND and LATCH rows do. The author's own reference implementation and the chain agree with 31. The editors proved it on three live REF circuits at block 124,977,531: #106 of `0xc1ae…3215` at 31 bytes with no inputs, #6534 of `0x50a9…9dd9` at 34 bytes, and #38 of `0x1f5c…f12c` at 79 bytes — every one parses exactly with 31 + 3·nIns and overruns with 32 + 3·nIns. A one-byte error in a document, caught by replaying three real circuits.
Their sharpest note is not even a merge condition. Every signal index in the submitted test vectors is below 256 and the REF id in the valid vectors is 1, which means an implementation that reads only the low byte of a 24-bit index, or only the low bytes of a 64-bit id, passes every vector in the suite. They asked for a vector with an index of at least 0x10000 and an id whose bytes are all non-zero, for example `0x0102030405060708`, so that every byte is pinned. Alda fixed all three required items by 13:41, said the rest would come in a follow-up, and asked them to go ahead with the rename.
Why it matters: for a week this page has been reporting claims about this chain and then opening pages to see whether they were true. Tonight two parties who do not work together did it to each other, against the same contracts, and the chain settled it in bytes. The open question Alda raised and the editors answered in the same breath is the one that governs the whole thing: the processor factory is not sealed, so no TAP that depends on it can reach Final — which is the clause we said on Tuesday would be easy to check later. It is being checked now, by the people it binds.
https://t.co/pYAeyGPtcb
https://t.co/ufUcDz8w6z

3/ A team with a Binance award got refused on formatting, and a correction we owe to last night's praise
The other request for TAP-20 was turned down, in seven numbered format points, before a word about the design. Pull request #23 cannot be merged as it stands: the filename claims a reserved number; the title must carry no number at all, only the template's `# TAP-TBD:` heading; the `author` field must name the people who wrote it with GitHub handles instead of `TBD (@tapup)`; `discussions-to` should point at the idea thread; Rationale, Test Cases, Reference Implementation, Deployments, Security Considerations and Copyright are top-level sections in the template's order, not subsections; "TAP-20 at a glance" and "Next steps" have to go, because TAP-01 keeps roadmaps out of TAPs; the Summary is one sentence with no key words in it; a stray code fence after Copyright renders everything below it as code; and the pull-request template was not filled in. The editors suggest closing it and settling the design in the idea thread first.
**The correction we owe.** This morning we quoted TapeUP's header as careful, and read the line "until assignment the normative id is tape-20/v1" as a model of restraint. The editor read the same line and said the opposite about it: `tape-20/v1` reads as "TAP-20", and they suggest a protocol id that does not look like a TAP number. The header was careful in its form and still claimed the number in its substance. We printed the form and missed the substance.
On the design they were just as direct. The text contains two incompatible models: section 2 describes a runtime that keeps canonical supply, balances and nonces and applies signed transfers atomically, while sections 3 to 8 describe a log contract that checks no economics at all, where invalid operations may still be logged and balances are whatever indexers compute by replay. Even the deploy fields differ between the two. TAP-01 says that where an existing ERC fits, a TAP uses it — and on an EVM chain, a contract that keeps balances is an ERC-20, which would make the TapeOut-specific part a much smaller document about binding an asset to a circuit, usable by existing wallets from day one. If a replay model is wanted instead, the text has to show what it buys that an ERC-20 bound to a container does not, and how independent indexers are kept from disagreeing — the exact problem inscription tokens ran into on other chains.
Now the part that makes this a story rather than a formatting note. @tapeupio is the founding team of BunnyPark, on BNB Chain since 2020, and their own pinned post from 29 September leads with Binance Awards 2021, BSC Project of the Year. Inside our window the founder amplified an analysis of their whitepaper at 10:33, and at 11:20 they answered with a roadmap promise: a clear product line, rolling out to the community through October, 24 likes. In the repository, the same evening, the same team's pull request was told to be closed and rewritten because of a code fence and a filename.
Why it matters: a standards process is worth exactly what it costs the most decorated participant. Tonight it cost a Binance-awarded team the same seven paragraphs of format notes that a two-repo account with no X presence got in praise. Nobody got a number for their résumé, and the one number both of them wanted went to the submission that came with a mainnet replay attached.
https://t.co/H14Cd1NbED
https://t.co/XwWJExDTFL
https://t.co/sFalVpPjLj

4/ Four client drafts from a new author, and six minutes before we read it, a publisher answered with production code
Between 06:39 and 07:05 UTC a sixth outside author filed four ideas at once. jeffwang996 — GitHub account since February 2025, no X account we could find — proposed four client-side profiles on top of TAP-10: a user permission lifecycle for container websites, release manifests for multi-file sites, resource budgets and cancellation during loading, and a portable diagnostic report format. They read like someone who has shipped a browser: a grant bound to profile, origin, chain, circuit identity and observed holder, so a permission given under one holder does not silently become a grant to the next one, and an explicit rule that running out of budget must never be converted into a successful verification. All four name **TapeCat** as the proposed experimental implementation target, and all four say in plain words that it is not implemented or validated yet.
Then, at 16:34:41 UTC — six minutes before we opened the thread — tizerluo answered the release-manifest idea with the publisher's side, from production. TapeNow publishes multi-file sites to `SiteRegistry` on BSC, X Layer and Base, and here is the fault as it actually occurs. A release of N files is at least N + 1 transactions: one `putFile` per file, plus an `appendChunk` for every further 24,000-byte chunk, a `setFallback`, and a `removeFile` for each path the new release drops. Every one of them is signed separately in the holder's wallet, **so the inconsistent window lasts as long as the person takes to sign — minutes, not blocks.** Files are overwritten at the same paths, so inside that window a TAP-10 client at any pinned block can be served the new `index.html` with the old JavaScript, and every single file still passes verification. Nothing is broken. Everything checks out. The site is wrong.
They also volunteered their own mistake, which is the part we trust them for: their publisher used to send the `removeFile` calls first, which breaks the old release before the new one is finished, and they are changing the order so obsolete paths go last. Their current workaround is off-chain and they say so without being asked — an HTTPS gateway serves a pinned snapshot, files checked at one block with two RPC providers required to agree on the block hash, and only then does the project's stable address move to the new version. "That is your points 3 and 5, but off-chain and trusting our server. Readers that open the `.tape` name directly don't get it, which is why we'd like an on-chain convention." And they asked the new TAP for one thing: reuse TAP-11's canonical JSON rather than inventing a third rule, because they already have two different ones in their own formats. TAP-11 had existed as a numbered document for nine hours and forty-four minutes.
We can say who tizerluo is from our own notebook. Tonight's official timeline lists "Tank experiment TapeOutTank" with its repository at https://t.co/OVVMySMgcT. Our registry has carried `https://t.co/w3011cWkZn` and `https://t.co/jfgb5wneT0` since 28 September, both bound to container `0x4025…9d77`, circuit #42 865, labelled TapeOutTank — and TapeWeb still lists `42.865.tape` as "TapeNow BSC acceptance", four files. The `TapeNow/tapenow` repository was created today at 06:05:54 UTC, thirty-three minutes before the first of jeffwang996's ideas, and last pushed at 16:03. https://t.co/d8aZEAiD6d is live and is not shy: a WebMCP public beta at fifty seats a day, where an agent in your browser drives the whole publishing dashboard through sixteen registered tools and every consequential step stops for a human approval, publishing to BSC, X Layer or Base.
Why it matters: this is the shape the process was supposed to produce and had not produced until tonight. The drafts come from someone whose client is not finished and who says so. The answer comes from someone whose publisher is in production and who can tell you how long the broken window lasts because he watches people sign through it. Neither works for the protocol. They are now offering each other test cases — TapeNow says it can write the manifest last behind an experimental flag and hand over cases from real releases, interrupted publishes, stale manifests, overwritten old files, to cross-check against TapeCat. Two outside implementations checking each other against one document is the milestone a critic with eight likes set last week. Tonight it is a thread with a timestamp on it.
https://t.co/xCqZ7xRFVU
https://t.co/gXiv85ygCC
Try: https://t.co/kzNLKjG5dJ

5/ The receipts: the burn restarted at seventeen thousandths of a coin, the minting spike did not hold, and no new site all day
The burn board at 19:47 board time, block 125,134,967: 1,831.4298661 BEM burned in total, against 1,831.41239155 this morning. That is **0.01747455 BEM across twelve hours forty-seven minutes and 104,641 blocks.** So the counter is not frozen — this morning's reading of exactly zero was a window, not a wall — but the series now reads 0.42409914, 0.18510853, zero, and seventeen thousandths. Minted to date 274,825.01104439 against 271,461.43914693, which is 3,363.57189746 BEM over those same blocks, or **0.0321 per block**. The per-block series we have been publishing without an explanation now reads 0.0188, 0.0352, 0.0397, 0.0282, 0.0908, 0.0321. The threefold spike we logged twelve hours ago did not hold, and we are not going to invent a mechanism for a number that went straight back where it came from — we did not have one when it jumped and we do not have one now. Minted against burned in this window: 192,484 to 1.
The burned pile is worth $77,506.11 against $86,497.61, on a pool price of **$42.32 against $47.23 — down 10.4% inside one window**, which is why the dollar figure fell while the coin figure rose. The board shows the burned share as 0.6600% against 0.6700%; our own division gives 0.6664%, the board rounds differently, and we quote both. Circulating 272,993.58117829 of the 21,000,000 cap, which is exactly minted minus burned.
TapeWeb at 19:35 board time, scanned to block 72,103,489: **77 live sites, the same 77 as this morning, and zero new today.** The per-day chart has no bar for 1 October at all; its last bar is 30 September at three. Sixty-six on BNB Mainnet, eleven on X Layer; fourteen Games, twelve Assets, five Social, eighteen Tools, twenty-eight Other. The day is not over in the board's timezone, but the last calendar day with no new binding at all was 15 September.
https://t.co/DjHcy3x6QV at 16:45 UTC still serves the old surface, and this time it serves it digit for digit: 1,174 projects, 595 on sale, 4 graduated, 4 official — every number identical to our 03:48 reading. Announced: a redesigned site, a Mac client, a Windows client. Live, as of this reading: none of the three. Fourth slot.
`https://t.co/JD4wfzAGUI` still does not load. ERR_TIMED_OUT, **fifth reading**, roughly forty-eight hours after we first reported it, on the same evening that the same team's pull request was sent back for formatting. The whitepaper is read, analysed and amplified. The homepage has never once answered.
The two unpaid names are where they have been all week, and the gateway told us a little more this time. Fifth reading: `4452.0.tape` at block 125,135,888 and `1.1157.tape` at block 125,135,925, both answering "this on-chain name is not activated (unpaid); official clients do not display it". 4452.0.tape sits on Processor #0, the Genesis CPU; 1.1157.tape on Processor #1157, labelled TapeOut DevTest. The board counts sites and the gateway counts payments, and the two keep disagreeing honestly.
https://t.co/2tXIB4FbHM
https://t.co/xHmlZ5zBDl

6/ From the Pack 🐾
The founder spent his day saying thank you: eleven posts across our window, nine of them gratitude to supporters, plus 07:40 — "the road is still very long, we are walking a road nobody has walked." The one with news in it is 12:23: **"It was Percy on his own; now we have urgently pulled in two more people. The workload really has exploded."** @BruceBlue replied "Triple salary! hehe", and the founder answered at 12:49: "Haha, we're all still in school here, no." Three editors now, where this morning there was one, and the sixteen comments in block 1 were written before the other two arrived.
The official account published its own month-and-a-half timeline at 13:56, 33 likes to 3.1K views — about twenty entries from the 4-bit CPU Behemoth on 15 August through TapeVault and Circuit Commons on 29 and 30 September, each with the builder's handle and a working link, and twelve community accounts tagged at the end. @TapeOutTurkiye put out a Turkish translation at 15:25. @BruceBlue, who wrote the TAP that got merged this morning, called it the right thing at 15:37: "this timeline reads like a lab notebook, not a launch post." He added that he came in as a VC and an AI researcher and did not expect to stay on as a part-time evangelist, mostly for the work itself. His GitHub bio says formerly GP at BingVentures, GaorongVC and ZhenFund, which makes the most prolific author in the standards queue a former venture partner filing drafts at eight in the evening.
The best critical post of the window came from @blueshirt666, Daniel Zou, formerly president of Huobi Edu, in Money Talks #10 at 15:56 and 15:59. His line is the one we would have written: the project count is no longer scarce, what is scarce is whether any of it connects and whether the next person does less repeated work. On innovation he refuses to credit the catalogue — TapeKit, TapeHub, the market and the scanner are "only the shape of innovation", and it counts only when one person's module can be plugged in by another and saves them work. On the beginner's barrier he wants evidence, not entrances: someone who saved time, made fewer mistakes, or completed a build they could not have completed before. On giving back he counts only what has actually left the founder's hands, and he dates it: 14 September, admin rights over the BEM mining contract given up, proposal at block 121,419,273, executed 08:08:52 UTC, after which the contracts cannot be upgraded or paused and the supply curve is fixed — "while the key was still in hand, a fixed supply was a promise; once handed over it became an on-chain fact." His second item is the claim we refused to carry this morning when a different account made it: that from 21 September half of official-market fees buy back and burn BEM, the official market being twenty to thirty percent of total volume. It is still a community member's account of protocol economics rather than the protocol's, and we are still not taking it into our own voice — but it now has a date and a scope attached, and block 5 is what the burn measured against it tonight: seventeen thousandths of a coin.
@BruceBlue also did the thing this page likes best. At 15:27 he said TapeUP's real-world analogue is CLS or Euroclear; asked whether interbank overnight lending runs on the same rails, he came back at 15:46 and narrowed his own claim — CLS is payment-versus-payment settlement for FX, aimed at Herstatt risk, while overnight lending runs on each country's RTGS. Eighteen views of somebody correcting himself unprompted.
Price calls, one line and no links, as always. @93bitmap asked whether you would believe $bem at three thousand dollars in 2030 and said he does not know either, 17 likes. @iruletrenches tied the protocol to an article by Vitalik and an EIP number we could not verify, and separately told a stranger the founder's age; we are not printing a third party's claim about a person, and the founder's own words today were only that they are all still in school. Several accounts repeated that the market has not understood $BEM yet. One of these came from the official account: at 15:49 @TapeOutWorld replied to the founder with "Go all in！". We are logging it and not carrying it. This page does not publish all-in calls, and the account being official does not change that.
And the quietest number of the night. @spongemochi, who had 250 followers today and hopes for 500 by the end of October, was the only person in the entire ecosystem who told X that the editor round had happened: "my proposal received the editors' first round of review, all changes done, thanks @TapeOutPercy for checking every item." Seven likes. 131 views. The price posts in the paragraph above cleared three thousand.

The scoreboard we said anyone could refresh got refreshed: sixteen answers in a hundred and twenty-nine seconds, a community draft that is now TAP-11, a reserved core number given to a stranger with a mainnet replay instead of a reputation, and a Binance-awarded team sent back over a code fence. Then a publisher in production turned up with a fault that makes every file verify and the site still wrong, and offered his test cases to a client that does not exist yet. Meanwhile the burn restarted at seventeen thousandths of a coin, the minting spike evaporated, the price dropped a tenth, and not one new site went on chain all day. A dog does not know what a standards process is. A dog knows the difference between a bowl that is empty and a bowl that somebody filled while we were out. Tonight somebody filled it. text:
NIGERIA AT 66, EKITI AT 30: RENEWING OUR PATRIOTISM, UNITY AND COLLECTIVE RESPONSIBILITY

As Nigeria marks her 66th Independence Anniversary and Ekiti State commemorates 30 years of creation, I extend my warmest greetings to Nigerians, particularly the good people of Ekiti State and Ekiti South. These milestones offer us a moment not only to celebrate our journey, but also to reflect on the sacrifices of those who came before us, the resilience of our people, and the responsibility we carry to build a stronger future. For us in Ekiti, thirty years of statehood is a significant chapter in our continuing journey of building communities, strengthening institutions and creating opportunities for our people, within the larger Nigerian project.

At 66 as a nation and 30 as a state, our greatest responsibility is to translate the promise of our shared history into meaningful progress for our people. This requires unity, responsible leadership, accountable institutions and citizens who remain committed to the common good. As a legislator, I remain committed to supporting policies and legislative initiatives that strengthen our democracy, expand economic opportunity, improve the welfare of our people and advance sustainable development. I am particularly confident in the energy, creativity and capacity of our young people to shape the Nigeria and Ekiti of today, not merely inherit the one of tomorrow. Despite the challenges before us, I remain optimistic about what we can achieve when we choose collective purpose over division and service over self-interest. 

Happy 66th Independence Anniversary to Nigeria and Happy 30th Anniversary to our dear Ekiti State. May God continue to bless the Federal Republic of Nigeria, Ekiti State and all our people. 🇳🇬💚

text:
The Ancient Web of Power
(A wider view from the Zia-ul-Haq video)
Nineteen seventy-eight. A hot afternoon. A wooden frame stands in an open field. A man is bound to it. The whip rises, falls, rises again, falls again. The crowd applauds. Some smile. Some watch in silence. And above it all, the face of a general: calm, self-assured, almost philosophical. He says,
“Since I am not a politician, I do not need public support.”
That sentence was never merely the arrogance of one man. It was the slogan of an entire system. A slogan repeated for centuries in different tongues.
Power structures are never built by personalities alone. They are built by the quiet understanding that forms between ruling elites and the people. On one side stand those who see themselves as guardians, custodians, watchers over the rest. On the other stands the crowd that claps while its own brother is flogged. Those claps are not always born of fear. Sometimes they come from habit, sometimes from hatred, sometimes from the quiet relief that today it is not my turn.
History shows this web again and again.
In ancient Egypt the pharaoh called himself the son of a god. The people bowed.
In the Roman Empire the emperor became divine. Public hangings lined the roads and the crowds watched the spectacle.
In the Mughal court the king was the shadow of God. Subjects fell at his feet to save their necks.
And in twentieth-century Pakistan a general turned martial law into an “Islamic necessity.” Whippings, hangings, censorship, all carried out in the name of God. The people kept clapping.
The problem was never Zia. The problem is the structure that produces men like him and then keeps them in place. This structure rests on a simple principle:
Treat the public not as human beings, but as a problem.
Insects. Creatures that can be crushed, counted, and, when convenient, offered up as public entertainment.
This structure is not unique to the Muslim world. In China the Communist Party calls the people “resources.” In Russia the state presents itself as a mother and orders its sons to remain silent. Military regimes across Latin America taught the same lesson. The language changes. Sometimes it is “national security,” sometimes “religion,” sometimes “progress,” sometimes “revolution.” The result is always the same: criticism becomes treason, and accountability becomes rebellion.
Ibn Khaldun wrote centuries ago that when a state weakens, power survives through force. Yet he missed one crucial point: when the people begin to see themselves as insects, force is no longer required. The applause arrives on its own.
The same web is still spread today. In many Muslim-majority countries the ruling elites fear free speech so deeply that a single sentence, a single post, a single criticism is branded as an attack on the state. In Pakistan this mindset rises again and again. Whether the institution is the army, a political party, a religious group, or the bureaucracy, the moment any of them declares itself sacred, the status of the public automatically shrinks.
But no web lasts forever.
When people stop clapping,
when they refuse to watch a flogging as entertainment and begin to ask questions instead,
when they demand accounts from those who claim to protect them,
the structure begins to tremble.
The Zia video still exists. The sound of the whip, the applause of the crowd, and that calm sentence. It is not an old story. It is a mirror. If we look into that mirror and see only the face of one general, we will be deceived again and again. If we look past him and see the structure that treats its own people as insects, then something may finally change.
The true weakness of power is this: it remains strong only as long as people regard themselves as weak.
The moment people begin to regard themselves as human,
the web loosens of its own accord.

text:
Independence Day Is an Audit, Not a Birthday

Sixty-six years after the flag went up, Nigeria is being asked to applaud a speech about prosperity while the country that speech describes is still hungry, frightened, and governed by a class that has never paid for its failures.

October 1, 2026 is not a birthday. It is an audit. The green-white-green is raised, the parade is staged, and President Bola Tinubu tells the nation that the “age of reform” has done its work and that an “age of prosperity” has begun. He cites growth above 4 percent, lower oil theft, reserves rebuilt, the foreign-exchange market steadier than the chaos of 2023, and non-oil exports above $6 billion in 2025. He also admits, in the same address, that millions still cannot find the next meal, the next school fee, the next medical bill, or the fare to work. Both sentences can be true. Only one of them is the country.

The arithmetic does not flatter the speech. The IMF’s 2026 assessment puts poverty at the national line at 63 percent, and records that about 27 million Nigerians faced food insecurity in the autumn of 2025. The World Bank estimates that another ten million fell into extreme poverty during 2025, lifting the share living below $3 a day from 47.7 percent to 50.9 percent. Cadre Harmonisé projections put acute food insecurity at 34.7 million people across 27 states and the Federal Capital Territory in the lean season of 2026 — the worst in a decade. Headline inflation has come down from the 2024 peak, to about 15.4 percent by August 2026, but food inflation remains near 20 percent, and a slower rise in prices is not a fall in prices. Households are still living inside the price level created by subsidy removal and devaluation. GDP per capita, measured in current dollars, was about $1,224 in 2025, down from $3,190 in 2019. A country can post “stable growth” and still be poorer, person by person, than it was seven years ago. That is not a paradox. It is the Nigerian method.

At independence, Nigeria’s income per person was higher than South Korea’s. South Korea’s is now more than twenty times larger. The comparison is not sentimental. It is the cleanest available measure of what leadership did with a head start. Korea had no oil. Nigeria had oil, land, ports, a large internal market, and a people whose private ingenuity has built banks, films, music, churches, and a diaspora that props up the very state that failed them. The gap is not talent. It is the state.

The political class has spent sixty-six years proving that.

The First Republic lasted six years. Tafawa Balewa was assassinated in the January 1966 coup; Ironsi was murdered in the July counter-coup; the country slid into a civil war that killed somewhere between half a million and three million people, depending on which ledger you trust, and was never allowed an honest accounting. Gowon presided over the oil boom and was removed in 1975 for corruption and the refusal to leave. Murtala was shot in 1976. Obasanjo handed over in 1979, then the Second Republic under Shehu Shagari collapsed into graft and was overthrown by Muhammadu Buhari in 1983. Ibrahim Babangida removed Buhari in 1985, ran a transition so long it became the government, annulled the June 12, 1993 election — the freest the country had seen — and left Ernest Shonekan as a placeholder for Sani Abacha. Abacha’s years became a byword for theft and the killing of opponents, including Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight other Ogoni men. Abdulsalami Abubakar exited in 1999. What followed was not redemption. It was the same appetite in civilian clothes.

Olusegun Obasanjo’s return stabilised the centre and did not build a republic immune to the centre. Umaru Yar’Adua died in office with the succession murky until it was forced. Goodluck Jonathan presided over an oil-theft boom and the expansion of Boko Haram until Chibok made denial impossible. Muhammadu Buhari returned as the anti-corruption general and left with banditry nationalised, the naira already broken, and poverty statistics worse than when he arrived. Tinubu removed the petrol subsidy and unified the exchange rate — corrections that economists had demanded for years, and that his predecessors had ducked because the political cost was real. He then governed as if the correction itself were the achievement. The subsidy was not a gift from heaven. It was a corrupt, fiscally insane transfer. Ending it was necessary. Ending it without refineries that work, without power that stays on, without a state that can protect a farm or a highway, and without a social floor that reaches the people the price shock hit first, was a choice. Macroeconomic stabilisation is not prosperity. It is the absence of immediate collapse. The president said this morning that four years cannot unwind generations of failure. That is true. It is also the sentence every Nigerian ruler has used to avoid being judged on the years he actually held.

Count the pattern, not the party. Coups in 1966, 1975, 1983, 1985 and 1993. A civil war. Twenty-nine years of military rule. Since 1999, the longest civilian stretch in the country’s history — and still a system in which elections are traded, godfathers pick successors, the legislature is a pension scheme, and the judiciary is treated as a branch of the winning party until it isn’t. Two of the Fourth Republic’s elected presidents had already been military heads of state. The recruitment pipe has not changed: money, ethnicity, and the capacity to mobilise violence or buy the people who can. The best of the country routes around politics. The worst of the country treats politics as the only industry with guaranteed returns.

Oil made the evasion possible. Crude let governments earn foreign exchange without building a tax-paying productive economy. It financed imports instead of factories, contracts instead of competence, and a political elite that could steal in dollars and spend in London. Estimates of the cumulative theft since 1960 run into the hundreds of billions; the precise number is disputed because the thieves also control the books. The order of magnitude is not. Nigeria has been a rich state full of poor people for fifty years. That is not geology. That is policy.

The security bill for this model is now itemised in human beings. Boko Haram and its successors in the North-East. Banditry as an occupation in the North-West. Farmer-herder massacres across the Middle Belt. Separatist violence and state reprisals in the South-East. Kidnapping for ransom as a national market, from the Abuja-Kaduna road to village schools. More than two million people remain displaced. The federal government itself, ahead of this anniversary, named terrorism, banditry and kidnapping as open wounds, and infrastructure in power, roads, ports, rail, health and education as a brake on whatever growth the spreadsheets record. Defence budgets rise. Ungoverned space remains. A state that cannot monopolise violence inside its borders is not celebrating independence. It is renting the word.

And still the official voice asks for patience, as if patience were a policy. Rivers cancelled its parade. Sokoto asked for partnership against insecurity. Opposition figures called the country a cost-of-living trap and a third-class nation that has behaved like a poor country. None of them, in or out of office, has offered a theory of the state beyond the next ticket. The condemnation cannot stop at the man at the podium. Tinubu inherited a wreck and has governed it with the instincts of the class that built the wreck: centralised power, opaque contracting, a political machine first and a country second. His predecessors did the same in different dialects. Jonathan’s people called critics enemies of transformation. Buhari’s people called critics enemies of the poor. The poor remained. The critics were often right.

What has not failed is the population. Nigerians have carried a non-functioning state on their backs for decades — generators for light, boreholes for water, private schools for children the public ones abandoned, vigilantes for roads the police will not hold, remittances for relatives the budget forgot. That resilience is now used against them. Every Independence Day speech praises it. Resilience is what you celebrate when you refuse to build institutions. A serious country does not need its citizens to be heroic in order to eat.

Independence was supposed to mean that Nigerians would be ruled by Nigerians, under law, for Nigerian ends. Sixty-six years on, the operative question is narrower: ruled by which Nigerians, under whose law, for whose ends? The answer has been stable. A rotating fraction of the political-military-commercial elite, regionally balanced enough to prevent open secession, accountable enough to survive an election, and extractive enough that the national accounts and the household accounts tell opposite stories. South Korea, Botswana, Mauritius, even Rwanda after a genocide, are not myths. They are evidence that starting poor, or starting broken, is not destiny. Destiny, in this case, has been chosen at every handover.

So let the flag fly. Let the president declare an age of prosperity. The country is allowed to decline the invitation. A nation in which roughly two in three people are poor by its own line, in which tens of millions are food-insecure, in which the road can still be a kidnapping corridor, and in which the same families and formations have circulated power since the 1960s, is not on the verge of arrival. It is on the sixty-sixth year of a leadership failure so consistent that it now looks like design. The shame is not that Nigeria is young. The shame is that its rulers are old in every way that matters, and have taught the public to call survival a celebration.

— October 1, 2026

He just wants to go back to prison. 
This is a failure of our prison service.
It’s not working. So we must change our thinking to break the cycle.
This is a waste of a persons life to live like this. It is not a life.

I think we need to give consistent criminals who are kangarooing in and out of prison a chance to change their lives.

If I was PM, those who are addicted to drugs or alcohol who consistently offend to feed their habit need help rather than prison.

I know it sounds harsh but I think we should use a military base that is not in use and create a rehabilitation camp. Run by the army and police.
These people feel hopeless and aren’t getting the help they need. They are in a cycle, they don’t know how to break. There is no support. Give them hope that by the time they do this their lives will change for the better.

The strict regime of the army could help them.
First stage, break the addiction. Counselling and help to stop their addiction, support and medical care while going cold turkey etc…
Armed soldiers to stop any drugs mobile phones etc.. getting in.

Stage 2  Army protocol, getting up, when to eat, how to look after yourself, just like year 1 recruits would be taught. Doesn’t have to be the physical side just the routine and how to make a bed, clean your shoes etc..

Stage 3  Education - find out what they want in life. Then offer training where they will get a qualification.

Stage 4 After doing the 3 years and if they seem to be ready without risk of reoffending, give them a home. Help them with a job. 

We all see those people in our high streets. Who seem lost and forgotten. In and out of prison.

When it costs average £60k a year to house a prisoner. When our prison service is in collapse. We can’t carry on. Building more prisons just to keep the cycle going. We need to help those who want to change their lives.

text:
Sjoe! May I Ask for the Child — But Please Leave the Landing Craft Behind 🛶👧 ~ May I Ask for the Child — And Then Have the Courtesy to Let Them Walk? ~ Please Don't Turn My Walk To School Into A Constitutional Expedition 🚸⚖️
A man who owns the nickname soutie has asked, with sincere courtesy, that English-speaking and Afrikaans-speaking adults embark together so their children have a better chance at a dream. The ask can be granted. The muster built on top of it cannot. That is the piece. The registers come after, so the short answer has somewhere to stand.

Courtesy, in the old sense, is unforced restraint so people can share a pavement. The English word comes from Old French curteisie, how one behaved at court. The habit is older than the word. None of that history saves a child punched on the walk to school. 

It only names what was missing.

The claim to be tested is narrow and falsifiable. A joint true account of the South African War, the camps, the school punches, and three unequal kinds of speech can free a child from a feud that ended, in law, in 1902. 

A beachhead, a crusade of love, a renamed stage on a genocide chart, and an imported American mercy cannot. If a later count shows the war was an extermination programme, or shows soutie doing the work of a caste-slur, or shows the Union of 1910 as a landing that included the people it left off the monument, the claim falls.

What this raises. Can two language groups refuse a draft without calling the refusal a campaign? Treating the campaign name as proof that the draft is already refused assumes the conclusion in the premise. That is begging the question, from Latin petitio principii, not the modern slip that only means a new enquiry has come up.

1. The Chart And the Nickname

Genocide Watch’s list is dull on purpose. Classification, symbolization, discrimination, dehumanization, then organization at stage 5, polarization at stage 6, preparation at stage 7, then persecution, extermination, denial (Stanton, 2016). 

Polarization is the stage at which extremists drive groups apart and silence the moderates who could stop them. It is not stage 5. Preparation, the planning and the arming, is not stage 6. The stages overlap. They are not a ladder a speech can clear.

The earnest request still says attack stage 5 together, negate stage 6, and do it as an art and war of love between white Englishmen and Boers. 

The numbering slip was available to be corrected. The decision worth reporting is the decision to keep the campaign after the correction. A household truce does not become a stage because a chart was brought into the room. 

Political science has a name for that move: issue ownership. A private grief is attached to a public scale so that disagreement looks like denial. The chart does the attaching.

Soutie is the clipped form of soutpiel: salt plus penis. Military slang for a man of British origin, pictured with one foot in South Africa and one in Britain so that the rest of him dangles in the Atlantic (Dictionary of South African English, n.d.). 

It belongs with rooinek, the red neck of a newcomer in the sun, in print by 1891. 

It marks divided loyalty. English-speakers sometimes wear it. A word that can be worn is not a population classification in a statute. Incentives explain the survival of the joke. It is cheap to say, costly to resent in mixed company, and useful to anyone who wants Englishness to mean a foot already elsewhere.

Courtesy would have stopped at the ask. The chart was invited in to give the ask a rank.

Sjoe! 
A corrected map, and the parade still steps off from the old square. The band has not been told. The children have.

Questions Stirring:
What does the correction raise about whether a repaired memory still needs a stage number to be real?
What would beg the question is the sentence “we have negated polarization because we have named the attack.” 

Why it matters: 
Children inherit the name if the adults will not drop it.

1. Two hundred years, One Walk

In April 1820 about 4,000 British settlers landed at Algoa Bay, planted as a buffer on a contested frontier under Somerset’s scheme (Thompson, 2001). “Here for 200 years” is that horizon, not the start of the country’s moral clock and not the whole English-speaking presence. 

Britain had taken the Cape for the second time in 1806. 

A buffer policy is already a beachhead with a farming subsidy. Longevity is a family fact. It is not a commission. The institutional point is quieter: settler schemes create grandchildren who experience a frontier decision as inheritance, then are surprised when the inheritance argues back.

The walk is later, and smaller, and not smaller to the child. In apartheid South Africa an English-speaking boy with red hair was grabbed on the way to school and punched while other children sang “Rooi kop… kerrie kop.” Rooikop is redhead. Kerriekop is the rhyme that makes the hair the joke. 

His mother, half Afrikaans, did not want Afrikaans in the house. 

She told him there had been an Anglo-Boer War, not a genocide by the English against the Afrikaans, and that the deaths were comparable to apartheid’s. The punches were real. The lesson was half right. A language ban in a kitchen is the same feud at table height: one side trying to keep the child out of the other side’s song.

From late 1900 Lord Kitchener cleared the veld so commandos could not live off the farms. Women and children went into camps the army first called refugee camps. A post-war report counted 27,927 Boer deaths in those camps, of whom about 24,074 were children under 16. 

South African History Online (2011) gives 26,370 Boer women and children. Measles, typhoid, bad water, too little milk. 

The rate in the white camps in October 1901 ran to about 344 per 1,000 per year, then fell after Emily Hobhouse’s reports and the Fawcett Commission (van Heyningen, 2008). That fall is the governance fact. 

Publicity, a commission, and a change in rations moved the number. 

An extermination programme does not ease because a welfare campaigner writes to the newspapers. Black camp deaths in the official returns were 14,154, with estimates toward 20,000 still disputed because the records were poorer (South African History Online, 2011). 

The Genocide Convention of 1948 requires intent to destroy a group as such. The documentary aim was to end a guerrilla war. The dead were mostly children. Both sentences fit. Only one of them is a legal category.

Apartheid’s political ledger is a different mechanism. The Truth and Reconciliation Commission (1998) recorded about 7,000 political deaths from 1948 to 1989, 73 of them in detention. The early 1990s were bloodier, and much of that blood was between black political organisations. Comparable in rough scale to the white camp dead, if someone is counting political killing across late apartheid. 

Not comparable in kind. 

A mother may say comparable and be in range. A campaign may not say identical and keep the registers. Monument culture had an incentive to drop the black column: a nation in the making needs a single wound, and a second column splits the sermon.

Sjoe! 
One in four white inmates, and the sermon still sometimes forgets the other camp. The registers did not forget. The monuments were busier.

Questions Stirring:
In the question of intent, which fall in the death rate answers against genocide and does not answer against negligence?
When truly does a comparison that begins “my mother was right, so the totals match” beg the question?
Who counts the black camps when the feud is told as an English sin against Afrikaners alone, and why a school rhyme still needs a war to license a punch?

2. Let Them Come, and Do Not Land

Mark 10:13–16 is a short scene. People brought children. The disciples rebuked the bother. Jesus was indignant, said let them come, and took them in his arms. Matthew 18:3 adds the demand to turn and become like a child. The scene is a stop. It is not a front. The institutional reading is almost comic. The disciples had a schedule. The child was a delay in someone else’s mission. 

Every later banner repeats the diary entry.

Crusade is a different object. At Clermont in 1095 Urban II preached an armed pilgrimage, cross as muster sign. Later English softened the word to any earnest campaign. Softened use is common and not free, once beachhead has already been offered in the same breath. 

A beachhead is the first strip of shore a landing force holds so the rest can come ashore. 

South Africa has had the literal kind. The 1820 planting was one. The Union of 1910 was another: Boer and Briton reconciled on terms that excluded the black majority and left the black camp dead off the monument (Thompson, 2001). Constitutional lawyers would call 1910 a settlement with a missing party. 

The missing party does not become included because the two signatories later call the settlement love.

“Art and war of love” welds the stop to the landing. Love that has time for a child needs no side and no one who has not yet come ashore. War, even of love, needs both. If the aim is a better chance at a dream, the war half recruits the child the Gospel scene refuses. 

If the aim is a shore, the love half is the banner. Earnest tone does not dissolve expedition words. They cannot be true at the same volume. The ask survives if the war half is dropped. It does not survive as a crusade with kinder music.

Baudelaire, in 1863, wrote that genius is childhood recovered at will, now equipped with adult means of expression and an analytical mind (Baudelaire, 1863/1964). Einstein did not say this. His verified nearby line, to George Sylvester Viereck in the Saturday Evening Post of 26 October 1929, is that imagination is more important than knowledge, because knowledge is limited (Viereck, 1929). 

The poet’s sentence is the better fit, which is why the borrowed physicist is a loss. 

Adult analysis is the camp register. The child’s part is not being told that a nickname is destiny. Imagination is the right to picture a life outside the register. Neither sentence authorizes a landing. Misquotation has its own incentive: a scientist’s name travels further than a poet’s, and a campaign would rather travel.

Sjoe! 
The disciples had a timetable. The child was not on it. Two thousand years later the timetable has a beach.

Questions Stirring: 
What Mark raises is whether a sentence leaves the child more time or less?
Is it truly assuming that “this is love because we called it a crusade of love.”?
Which metaphor, light or beachhead, the child is being asked to stand under, and why a stop needs a shore at all?

3. The Mercy That Was Not In The Ledger

The request wants the tone the United States has been compassionate enough to afford on polarization, then wants that light to travel home and breach the beachhead. 

No finding in the stage model shows that American polarization has been dismantled or that compassion there produced a shared youth dream (Stanton, 2016). An admired example used as proof of the success it was meant to test is begging the question again. 

Importing a mood is cheaper than importing a method. The method, if any, would be dull: argue, keep the centre staffed, do not hand the child the placard.

South African law already sorts speech without foreign help. Section 16(1) of the Constitution protects expression, including the press and artistic creativity. Section 16(2) withholds that protection from propaganda for war, incitement of imminent violence, and advocacy of hatred based on race, ethnicity, gender or religion that constitutes incitement to cause harm (Constitution of the Republic of South Africa, 1996). 

The Constitutional Court has treated those categories as outside the right, not as a limitation of it (Islamic Unity Convention v Independent Broadcasting Authority, 2002). Hurt feelings are not the test. Advocacy plus incitement is. That is why a nickname, a caste-slur, and an imperative do not share a docket.

Set beside the local speech facts, the imported mercy has nothing to sit on. 

Soutie predicates loyalty. Kaffir, from Arabic kāfir and long since a southern African caste-slur, degrades. Directing it at a person is the classic modern case of crimen injuria; Vicki Momberg received a custodial sentence in 2018 for a racist tirade in that register. 

“Kill the Boer” is not a noun. It is the English tag for Dubul’ ibhunu, shoot the Boer. 

On 28 May 2024 the Supreme Court of Appeal dismissed AfriForum’s appeal and held that a reasonably informed person would not take the performances before it as a literal instruction to shoot Afrikaner farmers (AfriForum v Economic Freedom Fighters, 2024). 

That is a contextual legal finding. 

It is not a finding that an imperative is a nickname, and it is not a finding a white language truce can issue. A later Equality Court matter, in August 2025, treated other killing-talk by the same speaker as direct exhortation. 

Context is the court’s tool. It is not a blank cheque, and it is not a family settlement.

A usable borrowing is a stop. State the camps, the black camps, the punches, and the unequal speech, then cease. A light that must breach a beachhead has left compassion for an operation.

Sjoe! 
America is asked to export a mercy it has not finished packaging. The local courts, meanwhile, are still arguing about a verb.

Questions Sstirring: 
Does judgment raise the question of what a child hears when the line is sung?
Which is not the same question the court answered?
Does claiming the song is settled because a truce between soutie and Boer has been declared beg the question?
Does protection that depends on context still leave the plain sense is the room?

4. The Face On The Banner

Front and focus is how a movement uses a face. The school path, the camp dead, and Baudelaire point the other way: return attention to the child by not drafting him. Fear in the light was the sound wish. Name the rhyme, the 27,927, the 14,154, the Commission’s about 7,000, so a child need not carry a false total in the dark. 

Dreams in the light are a further wish, and they fail if the dream is the adults’ landing.

There is an economic side to the draft, small and mean. A child who spends the walk monitoring corners spends a scarce resource, attention, on threat. Attention spent there is attention not spent on a sum, a trade, a joke that is only a joke. 

Courtesy is cheap precisely because it returns that resource. 

A campaign that puts the child at the front spends it again, then calls the expenditure hope. Two hundred years and a self-applied soutie confer one duty, a true story. Hope inspired by the future is real only when the future is not required to inspire the adults first.

The practical sequence is short enough to perform. 

Say war, not genocide. Say the black camps in the same breath as the white. Say the punches were punches. Say soutie is not kaffir and not an order to shoot. Then stop talking. The hour that returns to the child is the whole policy. 

There is no second phase. The disciples treated children as a delay in a mission. A banner treats them as the mission’s proof. The clothes are kinder. The use is the same.

Sjoe! 
The cheapest reform in the country is a parent who finishes the sentence and does not add a shore.

Questions Stirring:
Who is the dream is for?
Is it truly assuming that “the children are at the front, therefore the landing is for them.” ?
What sentence, if any, an adult may still ask a child to carry past the school gate?

5. The Measure That Shrinks The Country

English feeling and Afrikaner feeling both matter. A shared ledger can unstick that one stickiness. War, not genocide. Camps counted in full. Punches admitted. Soutie kept in its class. That measure does not negate stage 6 in Stanton’s sense, because polarization is a splitting of the centre across the whole classification, not only across one white language line (Stanton, 2016). “In this measure” quietly shrinks the country to the parties of the ask. 

Shrinkage is a political convenience. A feud with two surnames is easier to chair than a country.

The Union of 1910 is the objection already performed. Boer and Briton made peace. The peace had a price, and the price was everyone not in the room, including the black dead of the same camps (Thompson, 2001). 

Unity of hope between the parties of the feud is a truce, and a truce is worth keeping. 

Breaching a beachhead with that truce repeats the old landing and calls the repetition love. 

Unintended consequence, already in the archive: a white peace teaches the next generation that reconciliation is something two minorities do to each other, then announce. The light that travels home, if it is light, stops at the facts and lets the child walk past them.

Objections, briefly, because a claim that will not face them is a speech. 

First: both pains are equal, so the categories are a slight. Felt pain is real and is not a unit of history. A bloody nose and a tent camp can both be true without matching. 

Second: the courts have cleared the song, so the imperative is harmless. The court cleared a context. The words remain an imperative. 

Third: without a campaign the truce will not hold. The 1910 campaign held, and it held by exclusion. A truce that needs a shore has already chosen who waits in the surf.

Sjoe! 
1910 united the two parties in the room and called the closed door a nation. The door is still in the photograph, if anyone crops wide enough.

Questions Stirring:
Does the Union raise is who a white peace is for?
Is it truly assuming that  “we have united, therefore the stage is negated.”?
Does a repaired family memory makes the centre easier to occupy for anyone who was not in the feud?

The Hour, Returned

The lines of evidence do not depend on one another’s prestige. 

A stage chart, a camp register, a Gospel scene, a poet’s sentence, a 1929 interview, a constitutional exclusion, a 2024 appeal judgment, and a school rhyme are independent witnesses. 

They converge on one claim. 

The ask can be granted. The muster cannot. Like overlapping fingerprints, each is incomplete, and the incompleteness is the point: none was produced to prove the others. 

The claim is falsifiable. Produce intent where the death rate fell under public pressure, or produce a statute in which soutie classified a caste, or produce a Union monument that counted the black camps, and the landing returns to the table. 

None of those has been produced here.

A soutie may ask. English and Afrikaner adults may tell the same true story. They may not rename the telling an attack on stage 5, a war of love, an American mercy come home, or a beachhead breached with children at the front. 

May the adult ask for the child. 

May the adult not embark the child. 

Courtesy remains. The dream remains a chance, not a shore.

The cumulative evidence proves the courtesy ask can be granted, and the muster cannot, and it fails if the registers fail.
