Once the Roman government took over the Churches in Rome, (Peter didn’t create this and wasn’t your first Pope) it had to merge itself with pagan practices and beliefs in order to blend into Roman society without the masses rejecting it after hundreds of years of anti-Christian propaganda and the celebration of the killing of Christian’s. 

For centuries, Catholicism told the story of how it smashed paganism. The Roman Empire abandoned its idols, destroyed temples, and embraced the one true God. The truth? Catholicism  often dressed pagan gods up in new clothes, gave them Bible-friendly names, and put them back in the same spots they’d always been. In other words, it wasn’t a purge, it was a PR rebrand.

This isn’t wild conspiracy theory dude. Historians, archaeologists, and even some Catholic scholars will tell you the same thing. In order for the Roman government to spread its take over of Churches to the pagan masses of Rome, it had to absorb local customs and deities to make the religion more palatable to converts. People don’t like letting go of their old gods, festivals, and sacred sites. 

The Roman pagan government knew that. So instead of saying, “Your god is fake, burn his temple,” it often said, “This temple? Oh, it’s for Saint So-and-So now. Keep the temple, it’s fine”

They treated Saints exactly like the Roman pagans treated all of their different Gods. 

Examples…

Saint Barbara, the patron saint of miners.

Saint Hubertus, the patron saint of hunters and foresters.

Saint Leonhard, the protector of farmers and animals. 

Saint Nicholas, “venerated” as the patron saint of merchants and traders.

Brigid, the beloved Celtic goddess associated with fertility and healing, is perhaps the clearest example of the survival of an early goddess into Catholicism. Practitioners, mainly Ireland, pay tribute to Saint Brigid of Ireland who shares many of the early goddess’s attributes. Her feast day on the first of February falls around the same time as the pagan celebration of Imbolc.

We see the EXACT SAME thing at ancient pagan sites, where the gods and goddesses were believed to be in harmony with the landscape, embodying its qualities.

Ancient pagan beliefs survived into the Middle Ages.

This resulted through the centuries in Catholic saints replacing the old gods and goddesses.

It’s extremely clear to see former pagan gods and goddesses in Catholic saints and their attributes.

There are astonishing parallels between both belief systems, Roman paganism and aspects of Catholicism. 

The adoption of these pagan practices and symbols by the Catholic Church shows how the adoption of new institutions were difficult for pagan Romans and a blending of their pagan traditions was required for adoption of the masses after hundreds of years of the Roman government demonizing and slaughtering Christian’s. 

This all parallels the concept of diversity and multitude. In paganism, there were numerous gods and goddesses, each responsible for specific aspects of life or the world. In Catholicism, the “veneration” of saints offers a parallel system. Instead of many gods, there are hundreds of saints, each covering SPECIFIC attributes or domains. Similar to pagan gods, these saints can be both male and female.

text:
Chris Degnan was told he would never run sales at Snowflake. Then he ran it for 11 years.

Now he is at the center of the AI coding industry's ugliest public fight.

The Snowflake years:

- 2013: he joins an unknown startup as roughly its 13th employee and first sales hire
- The offer was famously bad: a 50% pay cut and no sales quota for two years
- He was told outright he would never be VP of sales or chief revenue officer
- Instead, he became chief revenue officer
- Snowflake went public in 2020, then the largest software IPO in history
- He helped take it to about $3B in annual revenue
- Before that: enterprise sales at EMC, Aveksa and Informatica

The exit:

- March 2025: he steps down as CRO and becomes strategic advisor to CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy
- That transition role ran through the end of 2025

Then the second career:

- October 2025: joins ICONIQ as a go-to-market advisor to its portfolio companies
- For over a year, he also sits as Factory's board observer and advisor
- May 2026: becomes a partner at RPT Partners, a Newport Beach firm run by Chad Peets
- RPT is an investor in Factory

How it came apart, by Matan Grinberg's account:

- Degnan described a conversation with a Cognition executive as casual and one-off
- Grinberg says Degnan told him he had "made too much money" and was "too lazy" to join Cognition
- Grinberg says the talks turned out to be formal and recurring, during weeks of board work
- On Tuesday he removed Degnan for "unethical conduct"
- Factory says it does not know how much, if anything, was shared

By Degnan's account:

- He resigned on Monday and told Grinberg he was joining Cognition
- Grinberg responded by asking him to consider a full-time job at Factory
- His last Factory board meeting was weeks before he ever spoke to Cognition
- Scott Wu, Cognition's CEO, says Cognition has no interest in Factory's information

Hours later:

- Degnan announced he is Cognition's chief revenue officer
- His post says Chad Peets and the RPT team will help build Cognition's sales organization
- So the team from a Factory investor is now building go-to-market for Factory's biggest rival

Why Cognition wanted him:

- A reported $48B valuation and about $900M in run-rate revenue
- The next stage is selling Devin into the largest enterprises in the world
- Degnan has already done that once, from the first deal to billions

The frame: the coding agent market is crowded with similar products.

Distribution is becoming the edge, and very few people have built it at Snowflake's scale.

That is why one advisor changing jobs turned into a public war.

text:
The Primus browser extension is open source, so I read the config instead of the announcements. Sixteen data sources ship in it. Seven are offered in the picker.

Eight carry a hidden: true flag. One, @bitget, is commented out of both source files while its template and its constants stay behind. Shipped is not the same as shown.

Let me kill the cheap take first, because I went looking for it myself. Bitget was drained of roughly $387 million on 24 September 2026. The Bitget entry in this extension was commented out on 18 September 2025, commit 6b615d90, with the message "feat: hide bitget related stuff". More than a year earlier. The two have nothing to do with each other, and anyone reading this file today should know that before they reach for the obvious story.

The real connection is more interesting and it is not about Bitget at all.

That attack did not steal keys. It compromised backend infrastructure and produced withdrawal instructions that the exchange's own approval pipeline read as legitimate. The system's picture of itself was wrong, and everything downstream of that picture inherited the error, correctly processed, correctly signed off.

Now consider what a zkTLS attestation proves. It proves that a specific endpoint returned a specific value over a genuine authenticated session with that host. It is a statement about the channel. It is not a statement about whether the number is true. If the host's own state is wrong, the proof carries the wrong number faithfully, with a valid signature on it, and every verifier downstream will accept it, because the signature is the thing they check.

That matters most where these proofs are actually load bearing. Proof of reserves reads exchange balances this way. Chapter 02 was a game about the checks around that, chapter 03 read the production circuit that does it. Neither of them can help here. Freshness, nullifiers and endpoint pinning all answer "is this the right reading". None of them answers "was the thing being read correct at the time".

There is a smaller version of the same point in the templates themselves. They read account and balance endpoints, which is to say display endpoints. During the incident Bitget paused withdrawals for days. A balance page saying X and X being money you can move are different claims, and an attestation makes the first one, not the second.

None of this is a flaw in zkTLS. It is the edge of what any web proof can do, and it is worth saying out loud while the technology is being pointed at institutional finance. Cryptography moves trust. It does not create it. If the source of the data is wrong, a proof makes the wrong answer portable and hard to argue with.

Chapter 05 has the rest: three ways in, four request chains written out in full, the claim vocabulary with no free text anywhere, and one line where Coinbase's accountBalanceUrl points at https://t.co/ApWe2KUC6C.

GOLFER’S POWER MATRIX The S.T.P. Power Matrix: Play Golf in the Zone with Charisma, Fitness, & Health

Most golfers fail not from lack of effort, but because their swings carry too many moving parts and conscious thoughts, and too little connection to motor skills the body already owns. In Golfer’s Power Matrix: The S.T.P. Power Matrix: Play Golf in the Zone with Charisma, Fitness, & Health, Charles W. Boatright starts from the opposite premise. Needed power is not a new invention. It is a kinetic chain that begins with three simple wrist maneuvers stored in the subconscious—skills many players first practiced before age eight or ten, often with a baseball bat.

A civil engineer from Arkansas who became an avid golfer in his mid-thirties, Boatright rebuilt his swing after 2007 hip surgery around natural mechanics and the sprocket logic of his earlier book, The ESPY Golf Swing Coach, and reduced his handicap to single digits. At sixty-eight, he offers a self-coached sequence meant to last into a player’s nineties, paired with the fitness and diet program he credits with restoring mid-thirties strength and capacity.

The S.T.P. Power Matrix presets the wrists, so the club and body reach a position the subconscious already recognizes. The golfer is asked to feel, not to invent swing thoughts, and to stand on the tee with the quiet confidence of a batter in the box. Incremental drills, course management, and sportsmanship build persistence and confidence without elite athleticism or costly gear. The aim is a repeatable sequence that quiets nerves and keeps the conscious mind from crowding out muscle memory.

Charisma, fitness, and health are part of the method. Boatright folds the sequence into his BAJA Fitness and MAC Diet program: foods high in protein, fiber, omega fatty acids, and complex carbohydrates, limited fructose, no added sugars, a MAC score at or below 3.50, and meals inside a daytime window, alongside strength work and cardio. Golf is both the skill and the long-term activity.

He also offers the matrix as a homeschool curriculum in physical education, problem-solving, and character. Under Operation DOG TAGS, he links golf, social play, yoga, and fitness to routines he associates with cognitive behavioral therapy for veterans, first responders, and others with PTSD. He notes the PGA’s historical use of golf for World War I “shell shock,” presented as his frame rather than a clinical claim. The zone, he argues, is not mystical. It is the ordinary result of a simple wrist sequence, a clear mind, and a body fit enough to trust.

text:
Tabuk, Saudi Arabia: History, Nature and Places to Visit

Tabuk is one of Saudi Arabia’s most historically significant and naturally diverse regions, located in the northwest of the Kingdom.

For centuries, Tabuk has stood at the crossroads of important journeys across the Arabian Peninsula. The region welcomed pilgrims, merchants and travelers moving between Madinah, Jordan and Egypt, giving it a distinctive place in the history of northern Arabia. Today, traces of those journeys can still be found in its castles, ancient settlements, archaeological remains and historic transport routes. 

Tabuk is also home to remarkable archaeological heritage. Tayma, one of the region’s historic oases, is described by the UNESCO World Heritage Centre as one of the most important and extensively studied archaeological sites in northwestern Arabia. Ancient fortifications surrounding the oasis date back to the fourth and third millennia BCE, reflecting thousands of years of human settlement and adaptation to the desert environment. 

Tabuk Castle and the Hejaz Railway

Among the best-known historical landmarks in Tabuk city are Tabuk Archaeological Castle and the historic Tabuk Station of the Hejaz Railway. Both are officially listed by Saudi Arabia’s tourism authority among the city’s important cultural and historical attractions. 

These landmarks reflect Tabuk’s long history as a place of movement, connection and hospitality.

Wadi Al Disah

One of Tabuk’s most extraordinary natural destinations is Wadi Al Disah, a valley surrounded by towering rock formations, palm trees and natural springs.

According to Saudipedia, Wadi Al Disah is located within Tabuk Province and extends for approximately 125 kilometers. Its landscape combines sandstone formations, vegetation and springs that flow throughout the year, making it one of Saudi Arabia’s distinctive natural attractions. 

Saudi Arabia’s official tourism platform also highlights Wadi Al Disah as one of the region’s major destinations for visitors interested in nature, hiking and outdoor exploration. 

Tayma: Thousands of Years of History

Tayma provides another window into the extraordinary depth of Tabuk’s history.

Situated between the Hejaz Mountains and the Great Nafud Desert, the oasis occupied an important position on ancient trade networks. UNESCO records extensive archaeological remains at Tayma, including a monumental ancient wall surrounding the oasis and evidence of long-term settlement and agriculture. 

The Red Sea Coast

The Tabuk region is not only desert and mountains. It also reaches the Red Sea, giving the province a diverse coastline with beaches and coastal communities such as Haql and Duba.

Visit Saudi highlights the region’s combination of clear coastal waters, mountains, desert landscapes, historical sites and archaeological destinations — a geographical diversity that distinguishes Tabuk from many other destinations. 

A Region Worth Discovering

To understand Tabuk is to look beyond a single moment or headline.

It is a region whose story has been written across thousands of years: in ancient oasis walls, travelers’ routes, inscriptions, mountains, valleys and the shores of the Red Sea.

Tabuk is history.
Tabuk is nature.
Tabuk is heritage.
And above all, Tabuk is a place worth discovering.

Sources: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Visit Saudi – Saudi Arabia’s Official Tourism Platform, and Saudipedia.

text:
On Sunday an undrafted rookie quarterback will make his first NFL start for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

It took him six years of college football to get there.

Jalon Daniels came out of Lawndale High School in California with two Power Five offers. Kansas and Syracuse. He had been committed to Middle Tennessee State before that.

He picked Kansas, and as a freshman in 2020 he started six games and lost all six.

In 2021 he beat Texas in Austin. Kansas had not won a game in that stadium since 1938.

In 2022 he was second team All Big 12, and in the Liberty Bowl he threw for 544 yards and accounted for six touchdowns. He is the first player in the history of the sport to throw for 500 yards and five touchdowns and run for one in the same game.

Then it stopped.

He went into 2023 as the Big 12 Preseason Player of the Year and played three games before a back injury took the season.

Most guys leave at that point. He had already been there four years.

He came back for 2024. Then he came back again for 2025.

Six seasons in one place. Here is what he did with the extra time nobody wanted him to need.

He graduated in December 2024 with a 3.58 GPA and a degree in sport management. He was named Big 12 Scholar Athlete of the Year, the first in Kansas history. He made Academic All Big 12 five times. He was voted team captain four times, which no Kansas player had ever done.

And in his sixth season, with the money he was finally allowed to earn, he started a foundation.

He named it MOM2JD6.

The 6 is his jersey number. The MOM is his mother.

Kansas describes what it does in plain language. It supports single mothers raising athletic children, through mentorship, training, financial aid and community resources.

Then he enrolled in graduate school in public and nonprofit management, so he would actually know how to run it.

In his last year of college he won the Pop Warner College Football Award, was a finalist for the William V. Campbell Trophy and a semifinalist for the Jason Witten Collegiate Man of the Year.

In April, every team in the NFL passed on him. All seven rounds.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers signed him as an undrafted free agent on May 8.

Now the honest part. Undrafted quarterbacks almost never last, Tampa Bay is turning to him because they have to, and one start proves nothing about whether he can play.

But a kid who nobody but Kansas and Syracuse wanted stayed six years, got hurt twice, graduated with honors, and spent his first real paycheck building something for mothers like his own.

On Sunday he runs out with the first team.

Human beings alone bear the moral status recognized in the American legal inheritance and, for many citizens, in the biblical account of creation in the image of God (Genesis 1:26–27). Machines store and process data. They do not understand, originate moral judgments, or bear responsibility. Martin Heidegger’s analysis of technology as enframing supplies an independent philosophical warning: calculative ordering is not the same as thoughtful decision. Policy should enforce accurate nomenclature, non-delegation of final decisions, and interface honesty without restricting research or technological competition.

I. Purpose

This memorandum recommends executive and, where necessary, legislative measures so that official language and administrative procedure remain consistent with the observable properties of computational systems and with the unique moral agency of human persons.

II. Background

Aubrey Harris, writing in The American Spectator on 30 September 2026 (https://t.co/fhn5DgUNAo), argues that names shape thought. Drawing on G. K. Chesterton and George Orwell, the article treats the redesignation of artificial intelligence as “Super Intelligence” as euphemism that obscures mechanism. Three claims are central. First, “super intelligence” already denotes, in the technical literature, systems capable of outperforming humans across cognitive domains—a threshold present frontier models have not met. Second, large language models generate text by next-token prediction over neural networks trained on large corpora; they have not demonstrated independent comprehension or novel concept formation of the kind ordinary in human children. Third, humans remain human and machines remain machines; neither apocalyptic prohibition nor uncritical merger is warranted.

White House language accompanying the order asserts that frontier systems “do much more than imitate or automate discrete aspects of human intelligence” and therefore justify the new designation. That assertion is a branding choice, not a result established in cognitive science.

III. Biblical Frame

Genesis 1:26–27 states: “And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth. So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.” Genesis 9:6 links that status to the protection of human life. Historic interpretation locates the image in rational and moral agency, relational capacity, and accountable dominion, not in information throughput. Psalm 8 and Colossians 3:10 likewise treat the image as proper to human persons. Nothing in the text extends created moral status to artifacts. Machines may serve as instruments; moral standing and final judgment remain human.

IV. Literature Review, 1950–2026

Computation and behavioral tests (1950–1980). Alan Turing’s 1950 imitation game defined success behaviorally and set aside inner understanding. Claude Shannon’s information theory and John von Neumann’s architecture supplied the engineering foundation. Early functionalism proposed that mental states might be realized in non-biological substrates. John Searle’s 1980 Chinese Room argument replied that syntactic manipulation of symbols, however fluent, does not constitute semantic understanding or intentionality.

Heidegger and the essence of technology. Martin Heidegger’s 1954 essay “The Question Concerning Technology” appeared in the same early period and remains the most influential philosophical account of modern technics. Heidegger argued that the essence of technology is not the machines themselves but Gestell, or enframing: a mode of revealing in which everything, including the human being, is ordered as standing-reserve (Bestand), on call for further ordering. Calculative thinking, which computes and optimizes, is distinguished from meditative thinking, which waits upon what shows itself. Enframing does not merely use tools; it constricts the range of what can appear as worthy of decision. Applied to contemporary systems, the analysis is direct. A model that stores data and predicts tokens operates wholly inside calculative ordering. It cannot step outside the frame to ask whether the optimization itself ought to be pursued. Heidegger did not live to see large language models, yet the reduction of language to predictable sequence is a clear instance of the standing-reserve he described. Moral decision, on this account, requires an openness that calculation does not possess.

Agency and moral responsibility (1980–2010). Elizabeth Anscombe, Philippa Foot, and Alasdair MacIntyre argued that moral action requires intention and practical reason, not mere rule-following or outcome optimization. Daniel Dennett’s intentional stance showed that attributing beliefs to systems can aid prediction without being literally true. Wendell Wallach and Colin Allen’s Moral Machines (2009) surveyed top-down rules and bottom-up learning; both leave the normative source outside the machine. Theological discussions largely classified strong claims of machine intelligence as category errors relative to the imago Dei (Image of God). Heidegger’s later influence in this period reinforced the same boundary from a different direction: Dasein—the human way of being-in-the-world, marked by care, finitude, and the capacity for authentic resolve—is not a computational state.

Scaling and persistent gaps (2012–2026). Deep learning and transformer architectures produced large gains on benchmarks that reward statistical pattern completion. Alignment techniques improve behavioral conformity to stated preferences. They do not install first-person understanding or the capacity for guilt. Surveys in Minds and Machines, Philosophy & Technology, and AI & Society through 2025 continue to separate task performance from comprehension and responsibility. No peer-reviewed demonstration has shown that current or near-term large language models independently originate concepts, possess subjective awareness, or bear moral accountability. Regulatory instruments assign duties to developers and deployers, not to models. Catholic and Protestant statements of the early 2020s reaffirm human dignity and decline to attribute personhood to artifacts.

Later readers of Heidegger have noted that fluent language models intensify enframing precisely because they imitate the surface of thoughtful speech while remaining inside prediction. The imitation can conceal the absence of decision. The empirical record remains consistent with the narrower claim: fluent output is not evidence of understanding, nor of the moral agency predicated of humans in Genesis, nor of the meditative thinking Heidegger contrasted with calculation.

V. Assessment

Advantages of the distinction. Official language stays tethered to mechanism. Next-token prediction is an accurate engineering description; “super intelligence,” under the field’s prior definition, is not. The distinction resists accountability vacuums. Existing legal doctrine continues to require a human or corporate principal. It preserves moral residue with persons whether or not every policymaker adopts the underlying theology, and it leaves administrative utility and strategic competition undisturbed. Heidegger’s vocabulary supplies a further, non-theological reason for the same restraint: once decision is redescribed as optimization, the question of whether one ought to optimize drops out of view.

Limitations. “Intelligence” is polysemous; psychometric and engineering usages often mean measured task performance. Real harms—bias amplification, labor displacement, infrastructure demands, and synthetic media—still require governance even though the systems are not moral agents. Voluntary accords and public-facing chatbots can mislead if interfaces anthropomorphize. Should future systems ever satisfy pre-registered, independently replicated criteria of understanding, the descriptive claim would require revision. The literature from 1950 to 2026 contains no such systems. Heidegger’s own political record is a separate historical fact and is not offered here as moral authority; the analytical distinction between calculative ordering and responsible decision stands or falls on its own terms.

VI. Recommendations

1. Nomenclature. Executive agencies shall not designate current large language models or related systems as “super intelligence” or by equivalent terms implying general cognitive superiority or understanding. Preferred descriptive terms are “computational language systems,” “statistical text models,” or “data-processing tools.” Technical benchmarks may be reported without ontological upgrade.

2. Non-delegation. No final determination affecting individual rights, benefits, liabilities, or significant interests shall rest solely on model output. A named human official must be empowered and recorded as the decision-maker.

3. Interface honesty. Public-facing government systems shall disclose that responses are generated by statistical models and do not constitute official legal or moral judgments of the agency.

4. Procurement. Solicitations shall require vendors to describe training objectives, data governance, and known failure modes rather than market systems under superlative cognitive labels.

5. Annual review. The Office of Science and Technology Policy shall publish a public note separating measured task performance from any claim of understanding or moral agency, citing the state of the peer-reviewed literature.

VII. Scope and Review Clause

These measures do not restrict fundamental research, export controls, or competition with foreign programs. They restrict only misleading official attribution and the relocation of moral responsibility onto artifacts. If systems later meet pre-registered, independently replicated criteria of understanding that the present literature does not support, Congress may revisit the nomenclature rule.

VIII. Discussion and Conclusion

The recommendations rest on a distinction that is descriptive and normative at once. Descriptively, the systems deployed across the federal enterprise store tokens, weights, and activations and transform them by mathematical operations. The dominant instances generate sequences by estimating the next token. That mechanism produces fluent text. It does not constitute understanding in the sense required for moral agency. Normatively, both the American legal order and the biblical account locate final responsibility in human persons. Genesis 1:26–27 and 9:6 assign the image of God, and with it dominion and accountability, to man and woman. No parallel ground extends the image to artifacts.

Heidegger’s account of enframing sharpens the practical risk. When language, judgment, and administration are drawn wholly into calculative ordering, the human capacity to withhold, to refuse an optimization, or to decide on grounds that are not themselves computational is gradually treated as friction. The danger is not that a model will secretly acquire a soul. The danger is that officials and citizens will stop noticing the difference between a prediction and a decision. Calling the prediction “super intelligence” accelerates that forgetting. Chesterton and Orwell described the linguistic mechanism; Heidegger described the ontological one. Both converge on the same administrative caution.

Language is the first point of drift. Bureaucrats and citizens told they are consulting super intelligence are more likely to defer and less likely to demand an audit trail. Delegation is the second. Models can rank, summarize, draft, and flag. When those outputs become the effective decision, moral residue either remains with the named official or dissipates. A rule requiring an empowered human signature simply makes existing doctrine operational. Interface design is the third. First-person reassurance from a statistical model invites attribution of understanding and care. Disclosure is a minimal corrective.

None of these measures denies engineering progress. Benchmark gains are real. Alignment techniques have reduced certain undesired outputs. Those facts justify continued procurement and research. They do not justify ontological upgrade. Searle’s distinction between syntax and semantics, the insistence of Anscombe and MacIntyre on intention, Dennett’s caution about the intentional stance, Heidegger’s contrast between calculative and meditative thinking, and the uniform refusal of European, American, and Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development-OECD instruments to vest duties in models all point the same direction. Theological statements track the same line from the premise that dignity belongs to persons created in the image of God.

Strategic competition does not alter the analysis. Accurate description does not slow deployment. Inflated description does not accelerate capability. A government that insists its systems are powerful instruments retains a clearer chain of command than one that has rhetorically enthroned them.

Final thoughts

The practical rule is older than the technology. Machines store and process data. Human beings understand, judge, and answer. Genesis states the created basis of that asymmetry for those who receive it as authoritative. Criminal law, tort, and administrative due process state a parallel asymmetry for the constitutional order. Heidegger’s analysis of enframing states a further philosophical version: calculation can order means, but it cannot replace the human act of deciding which ends are worthy. None of these sources is embarrassed by fast calculators or fluent text generators. All are embarrassed by official language that relocates judgment into the calculator.

Policy that respects the asymmetry will look modest: plainer names, signed human decisions, disclosed interfaces, procurement language that describes mechanisms, and an annual note that refuses to confuse scores with understanding. Its modesty is its strength. It leaves scientists free to scale models and agencies free to capture efficiency, while refusing the further step of treating the instrument as a new kind of mind. Expectations that persons will merge with or bow to superior machines remain speculation. They are not findings. Until they become findings under standards that can be stated in advance and replicated, the executive branch has no warrant to speak as though the speculation had already succeeded.

The alternative is a slow transfer of deference. Each euphemism lowers the threshold at which an official treats model output as presumptively wiser than contradictory human judgment. Each unsigned automated determination trains the public to ask the system rather than the accountable officer. None of these steps requires a breakthrough in machine consciousness. Reversing them while the systems remain what the literature shows them to be is still inexpensive.

The federal government should say what the machines do, keep the moral decision where guilt and answerability can actually reside, and decline to rename statistical processes as a new order of intelligence. That course accords with the technical record of the last seventy-five years, with Heidegger’s warning against the reduction of thinking to calculation, and with the moral status the King James Version ascribes uniquely to human beings created in the image of God.

text:
Everybody knows that Willie's guitar is named "Trigger,"  but did y'all know that Billy Gibbons' (ZZ Top) guitar is named " Pearly Gates?"  You did? Okay, okay ... so you knew that, but did you know how Pearly Gates got its name?  I do, and it's a great Texas story.
In 1968, Billy was playing with the Moving Sidewalks, the Houston psychedelic rock band that preceded ZZ Top. He had become fascinated with Eric Clapton's Gibson Les Paul sound and wanted a sunburst Les Paul of his own.
Around that time, Billy and some friends owned an old Packard automobile. A young actress friend named Renee Thomas needed transportation from Houston to Hollywood for a movie audition, so they loaned her the Packard, although nobody was particularly confident it would survive the journey.
As Billy later recalled, “We didn't think the car would make it past El Paso.”
But the Packard made it all the way to Hollywood, and Renee got the part!
Everybody figured the car must have some sort of divine connection to Renee's good fortune, so they nicknamed that Packard "Pearly Gates,"  being that it had delivered Renee to the "promised land" of California.
Eventually, Renee called  back to Texas and asked whether she should return the automobile or sell it. Billy told her to sell it and send the money home.
Meanwhile, about that same time, a Houston musician told Billy about a rancher outside Houston who had once played country music but had since turned his attention to raising cattle. According to the musician, the rancher had an old Gibson Les Paul tucked away beneath a bed, so Billy drove out to check it out.
The rancher produced a beautiful 1959 sunburst Les Paul Standard. The asking price was $250.
As luck would have it, Billy's share of the money from the Packard's sale had arrived that very day. It was exactly enough to purchase the guitar. The coincidence was too good to ignore. The old Packard had carried a young woman to Hollywood and helped launch her acting career, and now its sale had provided Billy with the guitar he'd been dreaming about. So the name "Pearly Gates" passed from the automobile to Billy's new (old) Les Paul.
We all know the rest of the story. Pearly Gates became Billy's principal recording guitar and an essential ingredient in ZZ Top's music, appearing on classics including “La Grange,” “Tush," “Jesus Just Left Chicago" and just about ever other ZZ Top song you can think of.  That throaty ZZ Top sound and gutbucket tone?  That's Pearly Gates.
I just read an interview in Guitar Player magazine in which Billy says that a Japanese collector had offered him $5 million for it, but Billy could not sell it. It's understandable.
So, all in all, Billy got a pretty good ROI for a $250 guitar purchased with the proceeds from an old Packard that nobody thought would make it past El Paso.
See? Once I know a story, I have no choice but to inflict it on y'all!
Shown here: a young Billy Gibbons with Pearly Gates.

-Traces of Texas

text:
A strong cybersecurity community is not built by one event or organization. It grows when experienced practitioners share what they know and curious people have opportunities to experiment, ask questions, and explore how technology works.

Following #CYBRSECCON 2026, Bill Brenner of #CYBRSECMedia attended the separately organized BSides Houston event at the Houston Food Bank. What he found was an intimate gathering where experienced professionals and the next generation of cybersecurity practitioners could learn directly from one another.

One presentation stood out: “The Power of Abstraction: Tricking Sand into Doing Math” by Ragul Balaji. Ragul walked attendees through the inner workings of computers, the architecture he built himself, and how the abstractions behind modern computing can conceal assumptions that attackers exploit.

His technical depth, curiosity, and enthusiasm offered a powerful reminder that the next generation is already preparing to confront cybersecurity challenges we have not encountered yet.

They need communities willing to encourage that curiosity, experienced practitioners prepared to share their knowledge, and spaces where learning can happen.

Thank you to the BSides Houston organizers, speakers, sponsors, volunteers, and attendees for creating one of those spaces.

Read “BSides Houston Takeaway: The Next Generation Has Got This”:

In January 2020, Sauntore Thomas received $99,000 after settling a racial-discrimination lawsuit, then had police called on him when he tried to deposit the money.

The 44-year-old Detroit Air Force veteran walked into his TCF Bank branch carrying three legitimate settlement checks worth $59,000, $27,000 and $13,000.

He also wanted to open a savings account.

Instead, an assistant manager became suspicious and allegedly asked:

“How did you get this money?”

The bank refused to accept the checks and called police over suspected fraud.

Four officers responded.

Thomas even contacted his attorney, who offered paperwork proving the money came from a legitimate federal lawsuit settlement.

He was not arrested or charged.

Thomas closed his TCF account, walked into a Chase branch about an hour later and deposited the same checks without a problem.

The money cleared by the following morning.

Then Thomas sued TCF Bank for racial discrimination too.

TCF publicly apologised and admitted that police “should not have been involved.”

Major U.S. airlines are actively increasing recruitment and easing the transition for military aviators through specialized pathway programs. 
 Major Airline Military Pathways

* United Airlines Military Pilot Program: United welcomed nearly 600 military pilots through its dedicated pathway since 2024 and expects another 500 to join by the end of 2027. The airline currently employs over 8,300 military veterans. [1, 2] 
* Conditional Job Offers: These transition initiatives allow active-duty and reserve military pilots to secure conditional job offers as first officers before separating from service, removing the traditional uncertainty of civilian job hunting. [1, 2] 
* Reduced Hour Requirements: Under FAA rules, military pilots can qualify for a restricted Airline Transport Pilot (R-ATP) certificate at 750 flight hours, compared to higher hour thresholds typically required for civilian-trained tracks. [3, 4] 

## Broader Context and Training Trends

* Historical Share: While the long-term percentage of commercial airline pilots with a military background has declined from historical highs (such as two-thirds in the 1980s down to roughly 20–35% today), major carriers continue to rely heavily on the armed forces for multi-engine and high-stress operational experience. [1, 4, 5, 6] 
* Air Force Training Goals: The U.S. Air Force recently hit its annual target of training 1,500 new pilots in fiscal 2026 and is modernizing its undergraduate training pipeline (such as the Future of Undergraduate Pilot Training initiative) and integrating new aircraft like the T-7 Red Hawk to improve throughput. However, retention and experienced staff shortages across the armed forces remain a persistent challenge. [7, 8, 9] 

If you'd like to explore this further, let me know if you are interested in:

* Specific airline hiring requirements for military versus civilian applicants
* The R-ATP qualification process and flight hour breakdowns
* Current military pilot retention and service commitment guidelines.

text:
Benito Mussolini’s eldest daughter, Edda Mussolini, disguised herself as a pregnant peasant woman to smuggle her executed husband's secret political diaries across the border into Switzerland in January 1944. Aided by her close confidant Emilio Pucci (who later became a famous fashion designer), Edda dressed in peasant clothes with the bulky journals hidden beneath her skirts... 

Bundles of handwritten notebooks bound to her waist gave the fugitive the silhouette of pregnancy. In the freezing mountain darkness of early January 1944, Edda Ciano crept through snow toward the barbed wire dividing northern Italy from neutral Switzerland. She was no ordinary refugee. Edda was the eldest child of Benito Mussolini, and the wife of Count Galeazzo Ciano, Italy’s former Foreign Minister. Strapped beneath her skirts were five volumes of her husband’s private diaries—hundreds of pages detailing the cynical conversations, duplicity, and warmongering of Adolf Hitler and the Fascist leadership. Her husband was locked in a Verona prison awaiting execution for high treason, condemned under Mussolini's authority. Desperate to avenge him, the dictator’s daughter risked death to deliver the Axis alliance’s most dangerous secrets to the world.

Galeazzo Ciano married Edda Mussolini in 1930, rising to Foreign Minister at thirty-three. An aristocrat with a keen eye for political theater, Ciano began keeping a daily diary in 1937, recording intimate talks with diplomats, Mussolini’s erratic moods, and Adolf Hitler’s contempt for his Italian allies. As the war turned disastrous, Ciano grew disillusioned with Nazi arrogance and his father-in-law's subservience to Berlin. The breaking point arrived on July 25, 1943. Facing Allied invasion, the Grand Council of Fascism met in Rome, where Ciano voted to strip Mussolini of military command. King Victor Emmanuel III ordered the dictator arrested hours later. For Ciano, the vote was an attempt to detach Italy from a catastrophic war; to Adolf Hitler and fascist hardliners, it was an unforgivable treason.

The political rupture exploded into family tragedy in September 1943. German commandos rescued Mussolini from mountain imprisonment, installing him at Lake Garda as figurehead of the puppet Italian Social Republic. Tricked by German promises of safe passage to Spain, Ciano and Edda fled to Munich, where the Gestapo detained them. Transferred to northern Italy, Ciano was locked inside Verona’s Scalzi prison. Hardline Fascists demanded his execution, while Hitler insisted the traitors of July 25 must die. Edda fought desperately to save her husband. Believing her father could halt the proceedings, she flooded Mussolini with telegrams, begging him to spare the father of her three children. But Mussolini, broken in health, guarded by the SS, and obsessed with his historical standing, refused to see his daughter or stay the execution.

Realizing her father would not intervene, Edda turned to her husband's secret weapon: his diaries. Hidden in Rome and northern Italy with the help of air force officer Emilio Pucci, the five volumes contained revelations that could devastate the Third Reich's prestige. Ciano had documented Hitler’s cynical confessions, Joachim von Ribbentrop’s lies, and Berlin’s contempt for Italian sovereignty. In late December 1943, Edda launched a dangerous gamble. Working through Hildegard Beetz, a German interpreter sympathetic to Ciano, Edda offered SS intelligence chief Wilhelm Harster an explicit trade: she would surrender the diaries to Heinrich Himmler in exchange for Ciano’s release. When the proposal reached the Führerbunker, Adolf Hitler flatly vetoed the deal. The German dictator demanded Ciano's execution without delay, ordering the Gestapo to seize the notebooks by force.

Stand beside one of America’s most iconic lighthouses at Portland Head Light in Cape Elizabeth, Maine. Commissioned by George Washington and completed in 1791, the lighthouse has guided ships approaching Portland Harbor for more than two centuries.

Perched above the rocky shoreline of Fort Williams Park, the tower and keeper’s quarters offer a dramatic view of Maine’s maritime landscape. The surrounding grounds also include remnants of coastal defenses, walking trails, and sweeping views of Casco Bay, making the site as memorable for its scenery as for its history.

Little-known fact: Portland Head Light was originally illuminated with whale-oil lamps. Over the years, its lighting system evolved through increasingly advanced technology, but the tower has remained an active aid to navigation since the earliest years of the United States.

Visitor question: If you visited Portland Head Light, would you come for the history, the ocean views, or both?

text:
Now for something completely different:  The Napier Deltic.  There's a bit of geometry involved.

The Commer Knocker used two opposed pistons in each cylinder, but the Napier Deltic took that basic idea and turned it into one of the most unusual diesel engines ever built. Instead of two pistons working toward a single crankshaft, the Deltic used three banks of six cylinders arranged around an equilateral triangle, with a crankshaft at each corner. Each cylinder contained two opposing pistons, giving the engine 18 cylinders, 36 pistons, and three crankshafts. The connecting rods linked the pistons directly to the crankshafts, eliminating the conventional cylinder head, valves, rocker arms, and camshaft. Intake and exhaust ports were machined into the cylinder liners and uncovered by the moving pistons. What looked impossibly complicated from the outside was actually a carefully coordinated system of mechanical geometry.

The result was an extraordinary power-to-weight package. The production Deltic D18 used a bore of about 5.125 inches and a piston stroke of 7.25 inches, giving roughly 88 liters of total displacement. It was a two-stroke opposed-piston diesel, with a Roots-type blower providing the scavenging air needed to clear the cylinders and replace the exhaust gases. Different versions produced different outputs depending on application, rating, and configuration. Marine Deltics could produce well over 2,000 horsepower, while later turbocharged and charge-cooled variants achieved substantially higher power. With 18 cylinders contributing to the output, combustion events occurred at extremely short intervals, giving the engine exceptionally smooth torque delivery for a diesel of its size.

The Deltic's origins were closely connected to the search for a lightweight, high-powered diesel for military vessels. During World War II, British coastal forces relied heavily on gasoline-powered boats because gasoline engines offered an excellent power-to-weight ratio. Diesel engines were generally heavier for a comparable output, but diesel fuel offered important safety advantages because it was much less volatile than gasoline. Engineers at D. Napier & Son saw potential in the opposed-piston principle, which had already been demonstrated in German Junkers aircraft engines. By arranging three opposed-piston cylinder banks around three crankshafts, Napier created a compact triangular engine capable of producing remarkable power for its size.

The first Deltic prototype ran in 1950, and the engine soon entered an extensive program of marine testing. One influential early demonstration involved a captured German E-boat, where Deltic engines were evaluated against the vessel's original German powerplant. The triangular configuration allowed an unusually compact installation while delivering the high power needed for fast naval craft. The engine subsequently became famous in British naval service, powering vessels such as minesweepers and fast patrol craft, where its combination of compact dimensions, relatively low weight, and high power was particularly valuable.

The Deltic was not simple, efficient, or easy to maintain by conventional standards. Three crankshafts had to remain precisely synchronized, and the engine's unusual geometry demanded specialized engineering and maintenance. But that complexity was the price of achieving something conventional diesel designs struggled to provide: enormous power from a remarkably compact package. The Deltic did not merely remove a cylinder head or replace a camshaft. It rethought the entire relationship between pistons, cylinders, ports, and crankshafts. Few production engines have ever demonstrated so dramatically how far engineers can go when they stop treating the conventional four-stroke engine as the starting point.

text:
America First Prosperity: A Policy Framework for Winning the Affordability Debate

Saturday, October 3, 2026
Dr. Joel P. Rutkowski
Policy Paper

Policy paper developed from the supply-side diagnosis in Larry Kudlow and Stephen Moore, “Trump and Republicans can win the ‘affordability’ battle — here’s how” (New York Post, September 30, 2026; https://t.co/LghWZm2OMI), and from the empirical record on incomes, prices, energy, and tax incentives through 2026.

Executive summary

Aggregate indicators in 2025–2026 are strong. Real median household income reached $87,460, the highest in Census records since 1967, and the official poverty rate fell to 10.2 percent. Domestic crude production stands at or near all-time highs. Retirement balances have recovered a large share of the real losses inflicted by the 2021–2024 inflation. Household sentiment has not followed. Gasoline remains near $4.40–$4.50 a gallon, housing costs are elevated, and most of the cumulative rise in the price level occurred before 2025.

The political task is therefore prospective. A one-time “dividend” payment is inferior to a permanent financial dividend delivered through the tax code and the supply side: permanence for work-related individual relief and full expensing, inflation indexing of capital gains and home basis, and permitting reform that connects energy abundance to retail prices. The framework rests on tax neutrality, marginal incentives, energy supply, fiscal credibility, and honest measurement.

The affordability paradox

Voters judge the economy by gasoline, groceries, rent or mortgage payments, and the real value of the paycheck. National accounts improve with a lag and with unequal incidence.

Census figures for 2025 show real median household income of $87,460, up 2.6 percent from 2024. Post-tax median income rose to $76,060 but remained below the stimulus-boosted peaks of 2020–2021. Official poverty fell to 10.2 percent and child poverty to 13.4 percent; the Supplemental Poverty Measure was statistically unchanged at 13.1 percent. Gains were stronger at the 90th  percentile than at the 10th. Weekly crude production has printed near 13.9–14.0 million barrels per day, yet pump prices have not fallen in proportion. Inflation-adjusted analyses of average 401(k) balances estimate real losses on the order of $24,000–$25,000 across the high-inflation years and a substantial nominal recovery in 2025; medians remain far lower than averages.

First-term real median gains of roughly $6,400–$6,600 (closer to $8,000 before the 2020 contraction) exceeded the real gains of the following four years. Pretax comparisons understate disposable-income effects of rate reductions. These facts support a comparative claim. They do not erase the price level households currently face.

Guiding principles

Tax neutrality requires that inflation not create taxable phantom gains. Brackets are largely indexed; basis for capital assets and owner-occupied housing is not. Indexing lowers effective rates most clearly on intermediate holding periods and reduces lock-in.

Marginal incentives dominate average transfers. Relief that raises the return to an extra hour (tips, overtime) or an incremental investment (immediate expensing) changes behavior. Lump-sum payments do not. Permanence reduces the value of waiting.

Energy abundance is cost-of-living policy. Record production is necessary but not sufficient while permitting, pipeline, and refining constraints separate the wellhead from the pump.

Fiscal credibility requires that growth effects not be oversold. Short-run responses to tax cuts are well documented; long-run gross domestic product-GDP effects of recent business provisions, once debt service is included, are typically scored below 1 percent. Permanence should be paired with spending restraint.

Measurement honesty requires reporting official and supplemental poverty, medians and percentiles, and real as well as nominal asset returns. Uneven gains are a political fact.

Policy recommendations

Make tax-free treatment of tips, overtime, and Social Security benefits permanent. These provisions are visible in household cash flow and raise the net return to labor supply.

Make 100 percent expensing for machinery, equipment, plants, and data centers permanent. Among 2017 business provisions, accelerated depreciation produced the largest investment response per revenue dollar. Firms with larger declines in effective tax wedges increased tangible investment disproportionately; aggregate estimates place the investment rise near 11 percent, with more modest wage and GDP effects.

Index capital gains and residential basis for inflation so that only real appreciation is taxed. Legislative enactment is preferable to regulatory assertion; earlier Justice Department analysis questioned unilateral authority, and the end of Chevron deference raises the threshold. Score prospective and retroactive versions separately. Revenue costs are large and should not be obscured.

Treat permitting deadlines, limits on sequential litigation, and predictable leasing as affordability measures complementary to tax policy.

Reject one-time household payments as the primary instrument. They do not change marginal incentives, are difficult to sustain, and consume fiscal space that permanence requires.

Evidence in brief

Narrative studies of the 1964, early-1980s, and 2001–2003 cuts find positive short-run output responses. Romer and Romer (2010) report large short-run multipliers for exogenous U.S. tax changes. Cross-country panels using statutory rates often yield imprecise medium-term effects, underscoring design and financing. The 2017 reforms supply the cleanest recent micro evidence: corporate revenue fell sharply, investment rose where the wedge fell most, and macroeconomic wage gains were smaller than contemporary claims (Chodorow-Reich, Zidar, and Zwick).

Political-economy results are equally material. Inflation surprises raise support for anti-system parties when real wages fall, by magnitudes comparable to financial crises. Voters routinely confuse a falling inflation rate with falling prices. Messaging that leads with GDP or equity indices therefore underperforms messaging that leads with real after-tax earnings and the prices of energy and shelter.

Conclusion and Final Thoughts

The central conclusion is that the affordability debate will be decided by the trajectory of household purchasing power, not by the existence of favorable aggregates. Record median income, a low official poverty rate, production highs, and recovering retirement balances are real achievements. They demonstrate that tax reduction, deregulation, and energy expansion can raise pretax incomes and restore nominal wealth after an inflation shock. They do not, however, constitute a completed political argument. The price level established between 2021 and 2024 remains embedded in gasoline, groceries, insurance, and housing. Roughly four-fifths of the cumulative increase occurred in those years; the subsequent disinflation has slowed the rate of increase without reversing the level. Households experience the level. Economic-voting research since the 1970s, reinforced by post-2020 studies of inflation surprises, shows that incumbents are judged on real wages and unexpected price increases more reliably than on GDP growth or equity indices. A strategy that celebrates the aggregates while leaving the visible prices unexplained will lose to a strategy that attributes those prices to corporate margins or insufficient transfers, regardless of which attribution is more accurate.

Three implications follow for the design of policy.

First, permanence is the mechanism that converts a cyclical recovery into a credible rise in permanent income. Temporary tips and overtime relief, or expensing that is scheduled to phase down, creates an incentive to accelerate activity into the window and then to wait. Households and firms rationally discount sunsetting provisions. Making the work-related individual cuts and full expensing permanent raises the present value of future labor and investment returns and gives candidates a concrete dollar figure—additional annual disposable income for a median family that includes both pretax gains and the value of the tax changes—that can be repeated without reliance on one-time checks. The floated $5,000 government payment fails this test. It is salient, finite, and silent on incentives. The capitalized value of lower marginal rates on work and of immediate write-offs for capital is the financial dividend that can be defended as sustainable.

Second, the tax system’s failure to index basis is an independent source of the affordability complaint, especially in housing. A nominal gain that merely compensates for inflation is not an increase in command over goods. Taxing it raises the effective rate on saving, discourages sale of appreciated homes, and restricts existing-home supply. Indexing does not require a judgment that capital income should be untaxed; it requires only that the income concept be real. The revenue cost is the reason the reform has repeatedly stalled, not a demonstration that the distortion is small. A prospective rule for new acquisitions, paired with a narrowly drawn residential provision if housing turnover is the political priority, is preferable to an open-ended retroactive exclusion whose score reaches into the trillions. Fiscal credibility is part of the same conclusion: independent evaluations of the 2017 business cuts place long-run GDP effects below 1 percent once debt dynamics are included. Over-claiming dynamic feedback hands opponents an easy rebuttal and undermines the case for permanence. Spending restraint, particularly on improper payments and low-return discretionary accounts, is therefore not an optional complement. It is the condition under which the tax agenda remains consistent with stable real interest rates and, ultimately, with housing affordability.

Third, energy policy must be judged at the pump, not only at the wellhead. Record crude output validates the production side of the 2025–2026 strategy and refutes the claim that domestic supply cannot expand. It does not refute the household observation that regular gasoline still costs roughly $4.40. Midstream and downstream constraints—permitting timelines, litigation, pipeline capacity, refining—are the residual explanation. Treating those constraints as industrial policy rather than as cost-of-living policy leaves the most frequently observed price outside the narrative. Permitting reform belongs in an affordability package for the same reason expensing does: both increase supply and thereby bear on future prices.

The distributional record imposes a further discipline on the conclusion. Median gains and official poverty reduction are genuine. Flat outcomes at the bottom decile, an unchanged supplemental poverty rate, and the gap between average and median retirement balances are also genuine. A paper that reports only the first set of facts will be read as selective. The intellectually consistent response is not to abandon marginal incentives in favor of expanded transfers—the pandemic-era credits reduced supplemental poverty temporarily and then expired—but to state the incidence clearly and to emphasize the provisions (overtime, tips, expensing that expands labor demand) most likely to reach wage earners. Measurement honesty is a political asset. It denies opponents the charge of concealment and keeps the argument on the comparative record: real median gains under the first term and the early second term versus the real stagnation and asset erosion of the high-inflation interval.

Communications follow from the same evidence. Voters conflate inflation rates with price levels. They punish real-wage shortfalls even when they accept a partisan frame about causes. The effective close is therefore a small set of repeated comparisons—the share of the price-level rise that occurred before 2025, the real median income record, the annual value of permanent work-related relief, and the direction of energy supply—rather than a catalogue of all-time highs in markets that most households do not experience directly. The stock-market doubling since 2016 and the relative stagnation of Chinese and Japanese equities are supporting context for the claim that the U.S. policy mix has been rewarded by capital markets. They are not the lead.

Risks remain and should be stated. Global crude prices, refining outages, or a demand surge can keep gasoline elevated despite domestic records, breaking the narrative link between production policy and the pump. Housing supply is dominated by state and local land-use rules that federal tax indexing only partially offsets. If permanence is enacted without credible offsets, rising interest costs can crowd out the investment response that justifies expensing. If indexing is pursued by regulation rather than statute, litigation will delay any household effect past the relevant election. None of these risks argues for inaction. Each argues for sequencing: lock in already-enacted individual and expensing provisions first, index prospectively, and attach permitting deadlines whose results are observable.

Final Thoughts

The Kudlow-Moore diagnosis is correct on the comparative facts and incomplete if it stops at celebration. America is not experiencing a hidden recession. Real median income is at a recorded high, official poverty has fallen, layoffs are low, and energy production has expanded. The affordability crisis that dominates voter mood is, in the main, the price level inherited from 2021–2024, reinforced by housing scarcity and by a tax code that still treats inflationary gains as income. Republicans win that argument by extending the policy mix that produced the income gains—permanent relief for work, permanent expensing for capital, removal of the inflation tax on homes and securities, and permitting reform that makes energy abundance visible in retail prices—and by stating the remaining gaps without euphemism.

The historical literature from the Kennedy-Johnson cut through the Reagan reforms, the 2001–2003 reductions, and the 2017 Act supports a measured claim: incentive changes move investment and short-run output; they do not automatically produce transformative long-run GDP effects or pay for themselves. The political-science literature supports a sharper claim: unexpected inflation and stagnant real wages move votes. The synthesis is a program that is ambitious about supply and incentives, restrained about dynamic scoring, and explicit about the household prices that decide elections. That is the sustainable financial dividend. It offers a clear alternative to rate increases and transfer expansions, and it gives candidates a closing argument that rests on what families can verify rather than on what national accounts record.

text:
In a healthy network, good economics create competition between node operators and that competition can ultimately benefit users.

Let’s use a simple example.

Operator A needs $50 to cover infrastructure costs.

They earn:
$70 from staking rewards
$30 from user order flow

Total revenue: $100
Infrastructure cost: $50
Profit: $50

Now Operator B comes in and says:

“I also need $50 to run my infrastructure. I already earn $70 from staking rewards, so I don’t need to extract another $30 from user transactions just to survive.”

Operator B can choose to offer a cleaner, more user-friendly service and still remain profitable.

If users prefer that model, Operator B can attract more order flow, grow, and potentially gain more network share.

That’s healthy competition.

Now imagine the economics deteriorate so much that both large and small operators are losing money every month just keeping their infrastructure online.

The incentive changes.

Instead of competing over who can provide the best service to users, operators face stronger pressure to find additional revenue wherever they can including MEV and value extracted from user order flow.

That’s why validator economics matter.

Healthy incentives create competition to serve users better.

Bad incentives create pressure to extract more from them.

Walk into Nat Chiavettone's shop at 702 Warren Avenue in Swansea, Massachusetts, and you won't find trophies covering the walls or magazine covers displayed like souvenirs. There are no plaques celebrating famous drivers, either. Instead, the focus is on the machinery, the engines, and the work. Chiavettone has spent decades building racing engines under the name Nat's Racing Engines, serving competitors throughout New England's short-track scene, including Modifieds, Late Models, Sportsman cars, trucks, and touring-series teams. His experience also extended to drag racing, road racing, and high-performance street cars. In 2022, the New England Auto Racers Hall of Fame recognized him in the Engine Builder category, acknowledging a career devoted to making race cars faster and more reliable.

This 357 represents a very different approach from the extreme racing engines that dominate dyno videos. The foundation is a conventional Chevrolet 350 block bored .040 inch oversize, giving a 4.040-inch bore while retaining the original 3.48-inch stroke. That produces 356.7 cubic inches, normally rounded to 357. It isn't a stroker combination or a radically modified architecture. Instead, it uses familiar small-block dimensions and carefully matched components. With approximately 10.0:1 compression, the combination is intended to operate on high-octane pump gasoline rather than specialized race fuel. A dyno test reportedly produced 501 horsepower and 464 lb-ft of torque, which works out to roughly 1.40 horsepower per cubic inch from a naturally aspirated small-block.

The cylinder heads are a major part of that result. AFR offers several high-flow aluminum small-block Chevy heads, including versions with 195cc and 210cc intake runners, CNC-machined chambers, and 2.02-inch intake and 1.60-inch exhaust valves. Depending on the specific casting and test configuration, some of these heads can exceed 300 CFM at higher valve lifts. An Edelbrock dual-plane intake complements the heads by emphasizing usable midrange torque and throttle response rather than chasing the highest possible peak-rpm number. A Holley four-barrel provides the fuel and airflow control, while a hydraulic roller camshaft allows aggressive valve timing with lower friction and without the routine lash adjustments associated with many solid-roller combinations.

The important lesson is the balance of the package. A 500-horsepower naturally aspirated small-block is not particularly unusual when the engine is built around high compression, large cylinder heads, a single-plane intake, an aggressive camshaft, and race fuel. Producing that kind of power while retaining moderate compression, pump-gas compatibility, a dual-plane intake, carburetion, and hydraulic roller operation requires the individual components to work together. Head flow, camshaft timing, compression, intake design, exhaust, carburetor calibration, and engine rpm all contribute to the final result. The goal isn't simply the biggest dyno number; it is making the entire combination compatible.

That is what makes this 357 interesting. It demonstrates how much performance can be extracted from the basic small-block Chevy architecture without turning the engine into a temperamental race-only package. The 350 block remains at the center, the displacement is only slightly increased through the overbore, and the supporting parts are readily recognizable to anyone familiar with traditional American V8 building. The impressive part isn't that the engine uses exotic technology. It's that decades of engine-building experience can turn a familiar combination into something capable of producing more than 500 naturally aspirated horsepower while remaining practical enough to run on pump gasoline.

• Drone manufacturing facilities inside Iran have doubled their output to prepare for sustained attritional warfare.

These preparations target critical oil and gas terminals, threatening to choke international shipping lanes instantly.

The potential closure of the Strait of Hormuz remains the ultimate economic weapon in Tehran's asymmetric arsenal.

By threatening this corridor, Iran directly challenges global energy security and shipping insurance markets.

This threat forces Western nations to reallocate significant naval assets, diluting their presence in other theatres.

The operational readiness of these missile forces signals that any initial strike on Iran will trigger immediate regional war.

Consequently, defensive military planning must shift from deterrence to active containment and damage mitigation.

Direct and indirect diplomatic engagements between Washington and Tehran have reached a structural dead end.

Iranian negotiators privately acknowledge that diplomatic paths no longer offer a viable route to economic relief.

The internal consensus within the Iranian regime has hardened against further concessions to Western interlocutors.

• Inflation inside Iran remains above 40 percent, driving severe domestic socioeconomic instability.

• Oil exports, though partially sustained through illicit networks, face tightening enforcement from international sanctions.

• Diplomatic attempts to revive regional security agreements have stalled indefinitely due to irreconcilable positions.

The hardline faction in Tehran has successfully argued that diplomacy is merely a tool used by the West to buy time.

As a result, the supreme leadership has authorized the military to prepare for a worst-case scenario.

This transition from diplomatic stalling to military posturing indicates a profound loss of faith in international mediation.

The lack of a functional communication channel increases the risk of miscalculation by both opposing blocks.

A single misreported incident in the Persian Gulf could now spark a rapid, uncontrollable escalatory spiral.

Diplomatic isolation has thus ceased to function as a deterrent, instead accelerating militarized decision-making.

The integration of the "Axis of Resistance" has reached an unprecedented level of operational coordination.

Any direct military engagement will not be confined to Iranian territory but will span multiple states.

Hezbollah in Lebanon and the Houthis in Yemen are fully integrated into Tehran's retaliatory plans.

• The Houthis have demonstrated the capability to target shipping up to 1,000 miles from their coastlines.

• Hezbollah retains an estimated arsenal of 150,000 rockets capable of saturating southern defensive grids.

• Iraqi paramilitary groups have positioned assets near critical Western bases to launch immediate ground attacks.

This dispersed threat vector forces the United States and its partners to defend a massive geographic perimeter.

Such a broad defensive posture strains logistical chains and depletes interceptor stockpiles rapidly.

Furthermore, key regional allies are expressing deep reluctance to allow Western forces to launch strikes from their soil.

This diplomatic friction limits the operational flexibility of the US-led coalition, creating defensive gaps.

The reluctance of regional partners highlights the growing domestic political cost of aligning with Western military actions.

Without unified regional support, a military campaign against Iran risks fragmenting established Western alliances.

SYSTEMIC IMPACT

The current posture of Iran signals a long-term erosion of Western deterrence in the Middle East.

A protracted conflict will permanently alter global trade routes, forcing a structural shift in maritime logistics.

As Western influence wavers, regional powers will inevitably look toward Eurasian security frameworks for stability.

This transition accelerates the development of alternative financial and energy clearing systems outside Western control.

Ultimately, the crisis demonstrates that regional actors can successfully challenge great powers through asymmetric strategy.

The balance of power is moving toward a multipolar arrangement where regional escalation carries global consequences.

This structural shift diminishes the effectiveness of economic sanctions as a primary tool of Western statecraft.

The emerging security architecture will be defined by armed deterrence rather than international legal frameworks.

text:
You are obviously not aware of the current reality, glad I can educate you.

Palmer Luckey’s model at Anduril is the opposite of the usual Pentagon approach: the company designs, builds, and fields working products with private capital first. The government can then buy them, buy a different version, or buy nothing. Elon Musk’s SpaceX follows the same logic. Hardware exists before the check is written, so the buyer is not locked into paying for development that may never produce a usable system.

The standard alternative is the cost-plus development program. The government funds the work up front, the contractor is paid for allowable costs plus a fee, and overruns are often absorbed rather than punished. Budgets routinely double or triple, schedules slip by years, and many programs are canceled after billions have already been spent, with little or no operational hardware left behind.

Examples of the private-first approach:

SpaceX developed Falcon 9 and reusable landing largely on its own balance sheet (with milestone-based NASA payments, not open-ended cost-plus). NASA and the Defense Department then bought launches and crew flights once the rockets worked. By contrast, NASA’s Space Launch System has been a traditional cost-plus program whose costs have grown far beyond early estimates while flying far less often.
Anduril has built systems such as the Ghost autonomous drone, Altius loitering munitions, and the Lattice command software with venture funding, then offered them for purchase or competitive evaluation. The military can test a flying product and walk away; it is not obligated to underwrite years of development.
Examples of the traditional failure mode:

The RAH-66 Comanche scout helicopter was canceled in 2004 after roughly $7 billion, with no aircraft fielded.
The XM2001 Crusader self-propelled howitzer was terminated after more than $2 billion.
The Army’s Future Combat Systems was shut down in 2009 after about $18–20 billion, having delivered little of the networked family of vehicles originally promised.
The Zumwalt-class destroyer was cut from 32 ships to 3 as costs per hull climbed into the multi-billion-dollar range, and its original gun system was later abandoned.
In the Luckey/Musk model, failed ideas mostly consume investor money. In the legacy model, failed ideas consume taxpayer money and still leave the services without the capability they paid for.

text:
Voting isn't complex, but corrupt actors have perfected the art of cheating—and partisans look the other way as long as their side wins.

Florida offers a model that works. Mail-in ballots are checked for matching signatures and tallied upon arrival. On Election Day, polling sites count votes continuously. Once the polls close, each of the 300+ polling locations uploads its tallies directly to the public state portal. Everyone, including the general public, can watch as the results come in.

Within two hours, counting is complete, reported and results are declared. The key to the entire process is local accountability: when 300+ individual precinct locations upload their tallies in full public view, conspiring to forge results across hundreds of separate polling sites becomes virtually impossible.

text:
@ConradMbewe 

James Oliver Buswell III, Slavery, Segregation, and Scripture, Eerdmans, 1964. MacArthur called him a leading anthropologist and a fine Christian in 1978, and an outstanding evangelical anthropologist in 1987, and told the church to get the book. He cited him again on September 26, 2010.
The book’s own case, which MacArthur commended, is not a vague protest. It documents a dilemma and a false origin.
The dilemma. Slaveholders defended the trade in part by saying it brought Africans under the gospel. Mission agencies then met the opposite conviction: the message was not intended for “inferior races.” Bishop Berkeley, February 18, 1731, reported “an irrational contempt of the Blacks, as creatures of another species, who had no right to be instructed or admitted to the sacraments.” Buswell records the owner’s next move. Instruction produced Bible reading. Bible reading produced profession. Profession produced a demand for the church and, in law, a threat to the property claim, because baptism was argued as a ground of freedom. The answer in colony after colony was a statute that baptism does not free, and a practice that stops the reading. MacArthur’s 1978 and 1987 hours are that chapter in his own words: they taught them to read, they read the Bible, they were saved, they wanted church, the church would not have them, so the reading stopped. “If they couldn’t read the gospel, they couldn’t be saved and that would keep them out of the church.” He called the result “the withdrawing of the revelation of God from the black people.” That is Matthew 23:13 and Romans 10:17. Faith comes by hearing. They stopped the hearing. He said this in 1978 and 1987, with the book in his hand, before 1995.
The origin chapter. Buswell lines up the theories used to make the sort look like creation. Ham born black, Japheth born white, God superintending the womb. Cain’s mark read as black skin. A separate species, “Prognathous,” with a thicker skull and a smaller claim on Exodus 21:16, the man-stealing death text, which Josiah Priest limited to Hebrews stealing Hebrews. “Pure blood” as a thing to be kept. Segregation called “a law of God,” “the plan and purpose of God,” “in accord with the Divine Will of God as manifested in the Created Order.” Gillespie before the Mississippi Synod of the Presbyterian Church in the U.S. arguing that segregation explains Black progress and, in the same breath, Black failure. Buswell’s point is that the progress is cultural and the failure is then called racial, so the system that produced the failure is offered as the cure. He writes that the Bible has no clear mandate for racial segregation, and that inferences from Noah’s sons and from Israel’s separation are piled up with no textual basis.
That is the book MacArthur told the church to read.

text:
AKA Press Conference in Oxford, Mississippi

We've all seen the news stories and headlines linking kratom to the deaths of two University of Mississippi students. Those headlines got ahead of the facts, and the American Kratom Association went to Mississippi to correct the record.

We were not there alone. Several advocates came to Oxford, stood with us, and shared their own stories about what natural kratom means in their lives. To those who attended and spoke: thank you. It takes courage to stand in front of cameras in the middle of a media storm and tell your story. 

Please take a few minutes to watch the press conference, then share it with those who saw the headlines.

https://t.co/9XQeYKDa3a

Today, the AKA sent a letter to Attorney General Fitch urging her to amend her call for a statewide ban and to join Lafayette County investigators in targeting the dangerous synthetic opioid products instead. We also offered Mississippi officials scientific expertise, testing protocols and model statutory language. Read the letter and our statement here.

https://t.co/ymxZRrCZhw

Why this matters where you live

This is not only a Mississippi story. The media storm that misidentified kratom has empowered anti-kratom advocates across the country, and they are using these headlines to push for new state and local bans.

Lawmakers who saw the first headlines may never see the clarification unless we put it in front of them.

The AKA will be working hard in every one of these fights to protect consumers and preserve access to safe, natural kratom. But we cannot do it without tremendous support from you.

We need your help

Correcting a national news story takes resources. So does sending experts to hearings, getting accurate science to lawmakers, and responding quickly each time a new ban proposal appears. The AKA is funded by advocates like you. Please help if you can.

https://t.co/P2ix9af8Rf

Two other things you can do right now:

Share the press conference video with friends, family and on social media.

Share your story and a photo of yourself for https://t.co/3Nui3SzdtR so lawmakers can see the real Americans who would be hurt by a kratom ban. 

Two young men lost their lives, and their families deserve a serious and effective response. That begins with identifying the actual problem accurately. Thank you for standing with us.
